archivedStories.title: Detect and reset dirty worker worktrees at startup to recover from abrupt session termination
archivedStories.description: When Claude Code sessions stop abruptly (OOM kill, user interrupt, network drop), worker worktrees are left with staged/unstaged changes and reported as dirty submodules. On spiral.sh startup (before launching workers), detect each worker worktree with non-empty git status --porcelain output. For each dirty worktree, run git reset HEAD followed by git checkout -- . to restore a clean state. Emit a worker_reset_dirty_worktree event to spiral_events.jsonl listing which worktrees were cleaned. This ensures the next spiral run starts from a consistent state without manual intervention.
acceptanceCriteria: Implemented as described in the story description.

archivedStories.title: Auto-cleanup stale spiral-worker-* branches on startup
archivedStories.description: Crashed runs leave behind orphaned spiral-worker-* branches. At startup of run_parallel_ralph.sh, scan for and delete any spiral-worker-* branches not checked out in any live worktree, then run worktree prune. Prevents branch accumulation that degrades git performance.
acceptanceCriteria: Implemented as described in the story description.

archivedStories.title: Remove orphaned index.lock files before worktree creation and in cleanup
archivedStories.description: OOM-killed workers leave .git/index.lock behind, causing all subsequent git operations to silently fail. In the Step 2 worktree creation loop and in cleanup_parallel(), detect and remove index.lock files from previously crashed workers before attempting new git operations.
acceptanceCriteria: Implemented as described in the story description.

archivedStories.title: Auto-restore prd.json from backup when corruption detected at iteration start
archivedStories.description: Validate prd.json with `jq empty` at the start of each iteration. If corrupted by a mid-write crash, restore from the most recent prd-backups/prd-iter*.json snapshot. Also fix the two non-atomic direct writes to prd.json in sequential mode to use temp+mv.
acceptanceCriteria: Implemented as described in the story description.

archivedStories.title: Add configurable timeout for Phase T (synthesize_tests.py) with SPIRAL_TEST_SYNTH_TIMEOUT
archivedStories.description: Phase T had no timeout and could hang indefinitely blocking the iteration. Wrap synthesize_tests.py and spiral-core synthesize in timeout --kill-after=30. Exit code 124 (timeout) produces a warning event and safe empty output. Adds SPIRAL_TEST_SYNTH_TIMEOUT env var (default 60s).
acceptanceCriteria: Implemented as described in the story description.

archivedStories.title: Validate heartbeat requeue succeeded and force-reset on failure
archivedStories.description: requeue_stale_stories() was called with || true — if it silently failed the story stayed stuck forever. After calling it, verify the story passes field is now false. If not, force-reset it via direct jq write with a warning log.
acceptanceCriteria: Implemented as described in the story description.

archivedStories.title: Detect and log .rej files after git apply --reject fallback
archivedStories.description: When git apply --3way unexpectedly fails and falls back to --reject, .rej files silently mark broken state. After the --reject apply, scan for new *.rej files, log them with a manual-review warning, and emit a patch_rejected event to spiral_events.jsonl.
acceptanceCriteria: Implemented as described in the story description.

archivedStories.title: Add predictive preemptive memory pressure trigger in memory-watchdog.ps1
archivedStories.description: The watchdog was purely reactive. Add -PreemptivePressureMB parameter: when free RAM drops below threshold at level 0, pre-escalate to level 1 proactively before hitting hard thresholds. Controlled by SPIRAL_PREEMPTIVE_PRESSURE_MB (default 0 = disabled). Passed through from spiral.sh watchdog invocation.
acceptanceCriteria: Implemented as described in the story description.

archivedStories.title: Detect and alert when deferred worker launch queue is stalled
archivedStories.description: When all queued workers wait indefinitely due to sustained memory pressure, only the periodic Queue: N deferred message was emitted with no escalation. Track _QUEUE_STALL_SECS across loop cycles. After SPIRAL_QUEUE_STALL_WARN_SECS (default 600s), emit a prominent warning suggesting reduce RALPH_WORKERS or lower SPIRAL_WORKER_MEMORY_LIMIT.
acceptanceCriteria: Implemented as described in the story description.

archivedStories.title: Merge per-worker retry-counts.json back into root after parallel run
archivedStories.description: Per-worker retry-counts.json files were never merged back to root after parallel runs. After merge_worker_results.py, collect all worker retry-counts.json files and merge into the root file using max-value semantics — ensuring retry counts are never decremented across parallel runs.
acceptanceCriteria: Implemented as described in the story description.

archivedStories.title: Clean up stale /tmp spiral files from previous crashed runs on startup
archivedStories.description: ralph-bench-output-worker-*.txt files and spiral-docker-lock-* dirs accumulate in /tmp across runs and are never cleaned. At startup of run_parallel_ralph.sh, remove all Spiral-specific /tmp files from previous invocations (safe: patterns are SPIRAL-specific and never needed across runs).
acceptanceCriteria: Implemented as described in the story description.

archivedStories.title: Add SIGINT/SIGTERM trap to spiral.sh for graceful shutdown and checkpoint flush
archivedStories.description: spiral.sh uses set -euo pipefail but has no signal trap. A Ctrl+C mid-iteration leaves background ralph workers running as orphan processes, may leave prd.json partially written by jq, and does not write a clean checkpoint. Adding a trap handler that kills child processes, flushes the current phase to checkpoint, and prints a summary message before exit allows the user to resume cleanly.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.sh registers signal handlers: trap '_spiral_cleanup INT' INT and trap '_spiral_cleanup TERM' TERM near the top after variable initialization

_spiral_cleanup kills the current background child process group, writes {"iter": N, "phase": P} to _checkpoint.json atomically, and prints '[SPIRAL] Interrupted at iter N phase P â€” run again to resume'
After Ctrl+C mid-Phase-I: no orphan ralph.sh or claude CLI processes remain (verified with ps aux | grep ralph)
Rerunning spiral.sh after interrupt resumes from the correct phase per checkpoint
uv run pytest passes (51/51)
technicalNotes: Track child PIDs: CHILD_PIDS=(); add each background PID via CHILD_PIDS+=($!)
Cleanup: for pid in "${CHILD_PIDS[@]:-}"; do kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true; done
Checkpoint flush inside handler: echo "{\"iter\": $ITER, \"phase\": $PHASE}" > $_checkpoint_tmp && mv $_checkpoint_tmp _checkpoint.json
Note: set -e in cleanup handlers can cause issues â€” use explicit || true

archivedStories.title: Move retry-count increment responsibility from spiral.sh to ralph.sh for correctness
archivedStories.description: spiral.sh currently increments retry counts in retry-counts.json after ralph.sh returns. If ralph is killed by a timeout, OOM, or SIGTERM before completing, the outer loop never runs its increment code and the retry count stays at 0, allowing a pathological story to consume infinite timeout-killed attempts. Moving the increment into ralph.sh itself (on any non-clean exit) makes retry counting immune to outer-loop failures.
acceptanceCriteria: ralph.sh increments retry-counts.json for the current story ID at the end of any failed attempt (passes=false after the story), using an atomic jq-based read-modify-write
On a successful attempt (passes=true), ralph.sh resets the retry count to 0 for that story
spiral.sh no longer writes to retry-counts.json (reads only, for decomposition decisions)
Increment is atomic: uses jq write to tmp file then mv â€” no partial writes
uv run pytest passes (51/51)
technicalNotes: In ralph.sh after story attempt: STATUS=$(jq -r --arg id "$STORY_ID" '.userStories[] | select(.id==$id) | .passes' prd.json)
If passes=false: jq --arg id "$STORY_ID" '.[$id] = (.[$id] // 0) + 1' retry-counts.json > retry-counts.json.tmp && mv retry-counts.json.tmp retry-counts.json
If passes=true: jq --arg id "$STORY_ID" '.[$id] = 0' ... same pattern
Guard: [[ -f retry-counts.json ]] || echo '{}' > retry-counts.json before first use

archivedStories.title: Implement main.py as a proper CLI with init, run, and status subcommands
archivedStories.description: main.py currently prints 'Hello from spiral!' and is a placeholder. Implementing init (wizard), run (forward to spiral.sh), and status (PRD summary) subcommands makes Spiral professionally usable.
acceptanceCriteria: main.py implements argparse with three subcommands: init, run, status
uv run spiral --help prints subcommand descriptions
uv run spiral init invokes lib/setup.py wizard (subprocess.run)
uv run spiral run [args...] executes spiral.sh with forwarded arguments (subprocess.execvp)
uv run spiral status reads prd.json and prints: 'X/Y stories complete (Z%) â€” N pending'
pyproject.toml [project.scripts] entry: spiral = 'main:main' exists and is registered
technicalNotes: Use argparse.ArgumentParser with add_subparsers(dest='command')
run subcommand uses parse_known_args() to forward unknown flags to spiral.sh
Locate spiral.sh relative to main.py: SPIRAL_SH = Path(__file__).parent / 'spiral.sh'
status: load prd.json, compute passed/total/pending, print summary â€” no external deps
Add tests/test_main.py with at least 2 tests: status output format, init calls setup.py

archivedStories.title: Add estimated token cost card to spiral_dashboard.py overview
archivedStories.description: The dashboard tracks model usage per story in results.tsv but shows no cost estimate. archivedStories.title: Add --dry-run flag to spiral.sh to test loop control flow without API calls
archivedStories.description: ralph.sh supports --dry-run but spiral.sh has no equivalent. Testing spiral.sh loop logic (checkpoint, gate, phase ordering, DAG checks, config validation) requires a live Claude API call, making iteration on the control flow expensive. A spiral-level --dry-run that skips Phase R, Phase T, and Phase I API calls while running all other logic (preflight, gate, DAG, checkpoint, merge) enables fast local testing.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.sh parses --dry-run flag and exports DRY_RUN=true
Phase R: '[dry-run] skipping research agent â€” using empty output' and writes {"stories":[]} to _research_output.json
Phase T: '[dry-run] skipping test synthesis'
Phase I: passes --dry-run to ralph.sh; ralph prints dry-run summary without calling Claude
Phase V: '[dry-run] skipping validate â€” assuming pass' with VALIDATE_EXIT=0
All other phases (G gate, M merge, C check-done, DAG check, preflight) run normally
bash spiral.sh 1 --gate proceed --dry-run completes in under 10 seconds
technicalNotes: Parse near top: --dry-run) DRY_RUN=true; shift ;;
Phase guards: [[ "${DRY_RUN:-false}" == true ]] && { echo '[dry-run] ...'; ... } || { real logic }
Export DRY_RUN so ralph.sh inherits it
Useful for CI testing of spiral.sh itself â€” add to GitHub Actions workflow as smoke test

archivedStories.title: Auto-generate progress.txt skeleton with Codebase Patterns on first run
archivedStories.description: ralph/CLAUDE.md instructs every ralph agent to read progress.txt for 'Codebase Patterns' before starting. On first run, progress.txt does not exist, leaving all first-iteration workers with no codebase context. spiral.sh should generate a structured progress.txt skeleton from prd.json (overview, tech stack detected from pyproject.toml/package.json) if the file is absent before the first ralph invocation.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.sh checks if progress.txt exists before starting Phase I; if absent, generates it

If progress.txt already exists, it is NOT overwritten
Generated file is under 40 lines to stay within ralph's context budget

Tech stack: STACK=''; [[ -f pyproject.toml ]] && STACK+='Python '; [[ -f package.json ]] && STACK+='Node.js '; etc.
Write using bash heredoc: cat > progress.txt << EOF only if [[ ! -f progress.txt ]]
Keep file compact â€” ralph agents have limited context and should not read a 200-line file

archivedStories.title: Add TLA+ ModelAssignmentConsistent invariant to SpiralWorkers.tla
archivedStories.description: specs/SpiralWorkers.tla models multi-worker concurrency but does not account for the model assignment protocol introduced by route_stories.py. The new protocol requires that model fields are written to prd.json before workers read story assignments, and that no two workers race to re-annotate the same story. Adding a ModelAssignmentConsistent invariant to the TLA+ spec verifies these properties with TLC before deployment.
acceptanceCriteria: SpiralWorkers.tla adds VARIABLE modelAssignments (story_id â†’ model string) to the state
ModelAssignmentConsistent invariant: all assigned models are in ModelTypes == {"haiku", "sonnet", "opus", ""}
RouteStoriesAction models route_stories.py writing all model assignments atomically before workers start
No worker action can modify modelAssignments (read-only for workers)
TLC model checker runs: tlc -config SpiralWorkers.cfg SpiralWorkers.tla without errors or counterexamples
A comment block describes the model assignment protocol invariants
technicalNotes: Add to state: modelAssignments = [s \in StoryIDs |-> ""]
RouteStoriesAction: modelAssignments' = [s \in StoryIDs |-> IF pending(s) THEN classify(s) ELSE ""]
Invariant: \A s \in StoryIDs: modelAssignments[s] \in ModelTypes
TLC available via: java -jar tla2tools.jar -config SpiralWorkers.cfg SpiralWorkers.tla

archivedStories.title: Dashboard: add progress.txt activity feed section showing recent ralph entries

archivedStories.title: Auto-create timestamped prd.json backup before Phase M merge
archivedStories.description: Phase M (merge_stories.py) is the only phase that writes to prd.json. If it crashes mid-write or the research agent inserts bad stories, the PRD may be corrupted. archivedStories.title: Validate _research_output.json schema before Phase M merge
archivedStories.description: Phase R writes _research_output.json and Phase M immediately reads it in merge_stories.py. If the research agent produces malformed JSON or omits the 'stories' key, merge_stories.py raises an unhandled exception that crashes the entire iteration. A lightweight check between R and M surfaces the real error clearly.

If the file is missing or invalid JSON: print a warning, skip Phase M, continue to Phase G
If 'stories' key is missing from the top-level object: print a warning and skip Phase M
If validation passes: proceed to merge_stories.py normally

Add 1-2 unit test cases to test_merge.py covering the missing-stories-key path

archivedStories.description: prd_schema.validate_prd() enforces required fields and types but never checks for duplicate IDs. All existing validate_prd tests continue to pass
uv run pytest passes (all tests)

archivedStories.title: Add --status flag to spiral.sh for quick session inspection
archivedStories.description: There is no way to inspect a SPIRAL session state without running it. A --status flag that reads _checkpoint.json and prd.json and prints a human-readable summary (current iteration, phase, pending/passed story counts) without launching any agents improves operational visibility, especially when resuming after a crash.
acceptanceCriteria: bash spiral.sh --status prints: current iter, last phase from checkpoint, total/pending/passed story counts
If no checkpoint exists: prints 'No active session' and exits 0
If prd.json does not exist: prints an error and exits 1
Does NOT start any agents or modify any files
Exits 0 immediately after printing (does not enter the main loop)
technicalNotes: Add --status to the argument parser at the top of spiral.sh
Read _checkpoint.json with jq if present: ITER=$(jq .iter $CHECKPOINT_FILE), PHASE=$(jq -r .phase $CHECKPOINT_FILE)
Read story counts with jq: total, passed, pending
Exit 0 before the main while-loop when --status is detected

archivedStories.title: Detect API 429 rate-limit in ralph.sh and pause without burning a retry
archivedStories.description: When the Anthropic API returns HTTP 429 (rate limited), the Claude CLI exits non-zero and ralph.sh counts that as a failed story attempt, consuming a retry budget entry. Stories can be falsely skipped after 3 rate-limit events. Distinguishing 429 from a genuine failure lets SPIRAL pause and retry without penalizing the story.
acceptanceCriteria: ralph.sh inspects claude CLI stderr/stdout for '429', 'rate_limit_error', or 'Too Many Requests'
On rate-limit detection: sleep 60 seconds and retry the SAME story without incrementing the retry counter
A separate RATE_LIMIT_RETRIES counter (max 5) prevents infinite loops on persistent rate limits
Rate-limit detection applies to all AI tools (claude, qwen, amp paths in ralph.sh)
Logs: '[ralph] Rate limited â€” waiting 60s before retry (attempt N/5)'
technicalNotes: Capture claude stderr to a temp file: claude ... 2>"$RALPH_STDERR_TMP"
After invocation: if grep -qE '429|rate_limit_error|Too Many Requests|overloaded_error' "$RALPH_STDERR_TMP"; then ...
Pattern covers Anthropic 429, overload (529), and common client-side rate-limit messages
Reference: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api/errors

archivedStories.title: Dashboard: add per-iteration story velocity bar chart
archivedStories.description: spiral_dashboard.py has overview metrics and model performance sections but no chart showing stories completed per SPIRAL iteration over time. A velocity chart answers 'is the project getting faster or slower?' and helps users tune config. Data is available in results.tsv via the spiral_iter and outcome columns.
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard HTML includes a 'Velocity by Iteration' section with a bar chart
X-axis: SPIRAL iteration number; Y-axis: stories completed (outcome=passed) in that iteration
Chart renders using inline SVG (no external JS library â€” stdlib-only requirement)
Section renders correctly when results.tsv is empty or missing (shows empty state message)
uv run pytest passes (all tests)
technicalNotes: Group results rows by spiral_iter, count outcome=='passed' per group
Add compute_velocity(results) helper that returns {iter: count} dict
Render as SVG using raw <rect> elements for bars (same approach as other dashboard charts)
spiral_dashboard.py is stdlib-only â€” no chart libraries

archivedStories.title: Add SPIRAL_MAX_RESEARCH_STORIES cap in Phase M merge
archivedStories.description: SPIRAL_MAX_PENDING limits total incomplete stories but does not limit how many NEW stories Phase R can inject in a single iteration. A research agent producing 30 stories per pass overwhelms the backlog even when MAX_PENDING is set. A per-iteration cap on newly-added stories makes growth predictable.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.config.example.sh documents SPIRAL_MAX_RESEARCH_STORIES (default: 0 = unlimited)
merge_stories.py respects SPIRAL_MAX_RESEARCH_STORIES env var: truncates research candidates to the cap before deduplication
When truncation occurs: prints '[merge] Capping research output: N â†’ MAX stories'
SPIRAL_MAX_RESEARCH_STORIES=0 or unset: unlimited (no behavior change)
test_merge.py adds test_max_research_stories_cap that verifies truncation
technicalNotes: Read env var in merge_stories.py: max_research = int(os.environ.get('SPIRAL_MAX_RESEARCH_STORIES', '0'))
Apply BEFORE dedup: if max_research > 0: candidates = candidates[:max_research]
Export from spiral.sh: export SPIRAL_MAX_RESEARCH_STORIES="${SPIRAL_MAX_RESEARCH_STORIES:-0}"

archivedStories.title: Add spiral-doctor command to verify all runtime dependencies
archivedStories.description: First-time SPIRAL setup fails in hard-to-debug ways when claude CLI, jq, or uv is missing or misconfigured. archivedStories.title: Rotate progress.txt when it exceeds a configurable line limit
archivedStories.description: progress.txt grows unboundedly across SPIRAL sessions. After many iterations it can exceed 5000+ lines, and ralph.sh reads it at the start of every iteration. Large files slow context loading and consume unnecessary tokens. Rotation archives the old file and starts fresh, preserving history without forcing ralph to read it all.

SPIRAL_PROGRESS_MAX_LINES documented in spiral.config.example.sh (default: 2000, 0=disabled)
Print: '[spiral] progress.txt rotated (N lines â†’ archive)' when rotation occurs

Archive: cp "$PROGRESS_FILE" "progress-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).txt" && > "$PROGRESS_FILE"

archivedStories.title: Warn when resuming from a checkpoint older than 24 hours
archivedStories.description: When SPIRAL crashes and is re-run days later, it resumes from the saved checkpoint. If the checkpoint 'ts' field is >24 hours old, the codebase may have diverged (external commits, file changes), causing subtle bugs. A startup warning helps users decide whether to resume or start fresh before agents are launched.
acceptanceCriteria: After loading _checkpoint.json, spiral.sh computes checkpoint age from the 'ts' field
If age > 86400 seconds (24 hours): print a stderr warning with the age in hours

--reset flag: removes _checkpoint.json and starts from iteration 1

archivedStories.title: Emit per-iteration summary JSON to .spiral/_iteration_summary.json
archivedStories.description: After each SPIRAL iteration (Phase C), write a compact JSON summary capturing iteration number, timestamps, stories passed/failed, and phases completed. archivedStories.title: Add prd.json write lock to prevent parallel worker corruption
archivedStories.description: When 3 parallel ralph workers each read-modify-write prd.json concurrently, the last writer overwrites prior writes. The current tempfile+os.replace approach is atomic per-process but not inter-process safe. A file-based advisory lock must serialize prd.json updates across workers.
acceptanceCriteria: A helper acquires an exclusive lock before reading prd.json and releases it after the atomic write
Running 3 workers that each mark different stories done simultaneously results in all 3 stories showing passes=true in the final prd.json
The lock times out after 30 seconds and raises a clear error rather than deadlocking
technicalNotes: On Windows use a .prd.json.lock sentinel file with spin-wait and exponential backoff; on Linux use fcntl.flock
merge_worker_results.py is the primary write path for parallel workers
Cross-platform: write a .prd.json.lock sentinel file, spin-wait up to 30s

archivedStories.title: Enforce dependency-order execution: skip story if deps not yet passed
archivedStories.description: DAG cycle detection finds circular deps, but ralph still picks stories by priority ignoring whether their dependencies are complete. A story depending on US-010 should not be started if US-010 is still pending. This prevents wasted iterations and confusing failures caused by missing prerequisite work.
acceptanceCriteria: Before ralph starts a story, spiral.sh or ralph.sh checks that every dependency story ID has passes=true or _decomposed=true
If a dependency is not satisfied, the story is skipped for this iteration (not counted as a retry), and a clear log message is emitted
A story with all dependencies satisfied is not skipped
Integration test: prd.json with US-002 depending on US-001 (not passed) â€” ralph correctly skips US-002 and works on US-001 instead
technicalNotes: Add dependency readiness check in ralph.sh immediately after story selection
Use jq to query: .userStories[] | select(.id == DEP_ID) | .passes
Skipped-for-deps stories should NOT have retryCount incremented

archivedStories.title: Add SPIRAL_STORY_BATCH_SIZE to cap stories visible to ralph per iteration
archivedStories.description: Large PRDs (100+ stories) waste context tokens because ralph sees all pending stories when selecting one. A SPIRAL_STORY_BATCH_SIZE config (default: 20) means ralph only sees the top-N highest-priority pending stories, reducing prompt overhead and preventing context window overflow on big projects.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.config.sh template includes SPIRAL_STORY_BATCH_SIZE with default 20
When SPIRAL_STORY_BATCH_SIZE=5, ralph receives a prd.json slice containing only the 5 highest-priority non-passed stories
Stories outside the batch window are not skipped â€” they appear in the next batch after higher-priority ones complete
When SPIRAL_STORY_BATCH_SIZE=0, the feature is disabled and all pending stories are shown (current behavior)
technicalNotes: Implement as a Python helper: lib/slice_prd.py --top N --prd prd.json
Sort by PRIORITY_RANK (critical=0, high=1, medium=2, low=3) then by story index for stable ordering
Alternatively implement inline in ralph.sh using a jq sort + head slice

archivedStories.title: Add SPIRAL_COST_CEILING to abort when cumulative API spend exceeds budget
archivedStories.description: Spiral can run for hours on large projects, accumulating substantial API costs. A SPIRAL_COST_CEILING config (in USD) reads from results.tsv to estimate cumulative token spend using Anthropic pricing and aborts before the next iteration if the ceiling is reached, preventing runaway costs.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.config.sh template includes SPIRAL_COST_CEILING (default: '' = disabled)
At the start of each iteration, spiral.sh computes cumulative estimated USD cost from results.tsv using haiku/sonnet/opus per-token pricing
If cumulative cost >= SPIRAL_COST_CEILING, spiral.sh prints a cost summary and exits with exit code 2
Estimated cumulative cost is printed in the per-iteration summary
Unit test: mock results.tsv with known token counts and assert cost computation matches expected USD
technicalNotes: Anthropic pricing (2025): haiku ~$0.80/$4 per MTok in/out, sonnet ~$3/$15, opus ~$15/$75
Store pricing in a PRICING_TABLE bash associative array or lib/pricing.py
results.tsv columns include model; token counts can be approximated from output size if not directly available

archivedStories.title: Write structured JSONL event log to .spiral/spiral_events.jsonl
archivedStories.description: Spiral has no structured observability layer beyond progress.txt prose and results.tsv. A JSONL event log at .spiral/spiral_events.jsonl capturing every phase transition, story state change, and fatal error enables post-run debugging and feeds future analytics tooling.
acceptanceCriteria: Every phase transition in spiral.sh appends a JSON event: {ts, event:'phase_start'|'phase_end', phase, iteration}
Every story completion in ralph.sh (pass or fail) appends: {ts, event:'story_passed'|'story_failed', storyId, retryCount, model}
Every fatal error appends: {ts, event:'error', message, context}
.spiral/spiral_events.jsonl is valid JSONL (one JSON object per line) after a full run
Log appends across restarts â€” it is not truncated on resume
technicalNotes: Implement log_event() helper in spiral.sh using printf + jq for JSON escaping
Use ISO-8601 timestamps: date --iso-8601=seconds (GNU) or date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ
Keep writes non-blocking using >> (append) not atomic write
Rotate when exceeding SPIRAL_EVENT_LOG_MAX_LINES (default: 10000)

archivedStories.title: Cache research HTTP responses in .spiral/research_cache/ with TTL
archivedStories.description: Phase R re-fetches the same documentation URLs on every Spiral iteration, burning Firecrawl credits and slowing research. Caching responses by URL hash with a configurable TTL (default 24h) eliminates redundant fetches when iterating on the same project across multiple runs.
acceptanceCriteria: A SPIRAL_RESEARCH_CACHE_TTL_HOURS config variable (default: 24) controls cache lifetime
When the research agent fetches a URL, the response is saved to .spiral/research_cache/<md5-of-url>.json with a fetched_ts field
On subsequent fetches of the same URL within TTL, the cached response is returned without an HTTP call
Setting SPIRAL_RESEARCH_CACHE_TTL_HOURS=0 disables the cache entirely
Cache entries older than TTL are automatically pruned at the start of Phase R
technicalNotes: Cache key = md5(normalized_url); store as JSON: {url, fetched_ts, content}
Implement as a shell wrapper or inject cache-check instructions into the Phase R research prompt
The .gitignore should exclude .spiral/research_cache/ by default

archivedStories.title: Record phase start/end timestamps in .spiral/_checkpoint.json
archivedStories.description: The checkpoint stores iter and phase but not timing data, making it impossible to identify bottleneck phases across iterations. Adding phaseDurations (phase -> elapsed_seconds) to the checkpoint enables performance analysis and informs capacity planning for long-running projects.
acceptanceCriteria: _checkpoint.json gains a phaseDurations field: {R: N, T: N, M: N, I: N, V: N} in integer seconds
Each phase records its elapsed time before writing the checkpoint
state_machine.py validate-phases accepts and validates phaseDurations as optional positive numbers
Dashboard or per-iteration summary log shows per-phase timing for the last completed iteration
technicalNotes: Use $SECONDS bash builtin or PHASE_START=$(date +%s); ELAPSED=$(( $(date +%s) - PHASE_START ))
Phase I (ralph) timing should include total time across all worker processes
Store durations as integers (whole seconds)

archivedStories.title: Record _passedCommit git SHA in prd.json when story passes
archivedStories.description: When ralph marks a story passes=true, there is no link back to the git commit that implemented it. Adding a _passedCommit field with the HEAD SHA provides complete traceability: given any story ID you can run git show <SHA> to see exactly what code change satisfied it.
acceptanceCriteria: After ralph commits changes and before writing passes=true, it reads git rev-parse HEAD and stores it in story._passedCommit
prd_schema.py accepts _passedCommit as an optional string field without emitting errors
If git rev-parse fails (no git history), _passedCommit is omitted rather than erroring
story_review_report.py includes _passedCommit as a hyperlink column
technicalNotes: In ralph.sh: COMMIT_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo '')
Use jq to inject: jq '(.userStories[] | select(.id == "$STORY_ID")) += {_passedCommit: "$COMMIT_SHA"}' prd.json
prd_schema.py: optional validation â€” _passedCommit must match /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/ or be empty string

archivedStories.title: Add epicId grouping field to PRD schema and story review report
archivedStories.description: Large PRDs have dozens of stories with no grouping mechanism. An optional epicId field allows grouping related stories into milestones (e.g., 'auth', 'dashboard', 'api'). The story review report and dashboard should render stories grouped by epic with per-epic completion progress.
acceptanceCriteria: prd_schema.py accepts an optional epicId string field on each story; validates it is a non-empty string if present
story_review_report.py groups stories by epicId in HTML output, with a per-epic progress bar
Dashboard adds an 'Epics' section showing epic name, total stories, and % complete
Stories without epicId are grouped under an 'Ungrouped' section
technicalNotes: epicId is a free-form string like 'auth', 'payments', 'onboarding'
Optional prd.json top-level epics array: [{id, title, description}] for epic metadata
merge_stories.py should treat stories with same epicId+similar title as potential duplicates

archivedStories.title: Add SPIRAL_ON_COMPLETE hook variable for post-completion automation
archivedStories.description: When Spiral finishes all stories, there is no way to trigger downstream automation without modifying spiral.sh. A SPIRAL_ON_COMPLETE environment variable holds a shell command executed once when the loop completes successfully, enabling webhooks, desktop notifications, CI triggers, and Slack alerts.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.config.sh template documents SPIRAL_ON_COMPLETE with a commented example
When SPIRAL_ON_COMPLETE is set and check_done exits 0, spiral.sh runs eval "$SPIRAL_ON_COMPLETE" before exiting
If the hook command fails, a warning is printed but spiral.sh still exits 0
SPIRAL_ON_COMPLETE is not run when spiral exits due to iteration limit, SIGINT, or errors
technicalNotes: Use eval "$SPIRAL_ON_COMPLETE" in bash to preserve env vars
Example: SPIRAL_ON_COMPLETE='curl -s -X POST $SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL'
Log the first 80 chars of the hook command for debuggability

archivedStories.title: Add unit tests for synthesize_tests.py (report parsing and priority mapping)
archivedStories.description: synthesize_tests.py is a Phase T critical-path component with complex logic: finding recent reports, normalizing test names, deduplicating against PRD stories, and mapping categories to priorities. It has no unit tests, making refactoring risky.
acceptanceCriteria: tests/test_synthesize_tests.py covers find_recent_reports with missing dir, empty dir, and multi-report scenarios
Tests cover normalize() with punctuation, unicode, and empty string inputs
Tests cover PRIORITY_MAP for all known categories and unknown-category fallback to 'medium'
Tests cover deduplication: a failing test matching an existing PRD story title does NOT produce a duplicate candidate
All tests pass with uv run pytest tests/test_synthesize_tests.py
technicalNotes: Use tmp_path pytest fixture for file-system based tests
Mock report.json format: {summary: {failed:1, passed:9, total:10}, tests: [{id, name, status, category}]}
Import path: sys.path.insert(0, 'lib') then from synthesize_tests import ...

archivedStories.title: Add unit tests for merge_stories.py (deduplication and atomic prd.json patch)
archivedStories.description: merge_stories.py orchestrates Phase M, patching prd.json with new research stories. Its word-overlap deduplication, ID assignment, priority ordering, and overflow logic are untested. A bug could silently insert duplicate stories or corrupt prd.json.
acceptanceCriteria: tests/test_merge_stories.py covers overlap_ratio with identical, partial, and disjoint title pairs
Tests cover is_duplicate threshold behavior at 59%, 60%, and 61% overlap
Tests cover ID assignment: given existing IDs US-001..US-005, next new story gets US-006
Tests cover atomic write: a simulated os.replace failure leaves original prd.json unchanged
Tests cover overflow: when max-new cap is hit, excess stories are written to overflow file
All tests pass with uv run pytest tests/test_merge_stories.py
technicalNotes: Use tmp_path for temp prd.json files
Test priority ordering: critical stories appear before medium stories in merged output
Test the --max-new flag at boundary values (0, 1, N)

archivedStories.title: Add unit tests for state_machine.py (StoryLifecycle and phase transitions)
archivedStories.description: state_machine.py contains the SpiralPhaseStateMachine and StoryLifecycle classes enforcing correctness invariants. It has doctest examples but no pytest suite. Without systematic tests, an inadvertent relaxation of transition rules could allow corrupted states to pass validation silently.
acceptanceCriteria: tests/test_state_machine.py covers all valid StoryLifecycle transitions: pending->implementing->passed, failed_retry->implementing->passed
Tests cover all invalid transitions (e.g., passed->implementing) and verify InvalidTransition is raised
Tests cover decompose() from both pending and failed_retry states; decomposed is terminal
Tests cover SpiralPhaseStateMachine backward transition raises InvalidTransition
Tests cover validate_checkpoint() with valid, missing-ts, and invalid-phase inputs
All tests pass with uv run pytest tests/test_state_machine.py
technicalNotes: The docstring examples can seed the pytest tests directly
Test new_iteration() resets phase ordering correctly
Test validate_story_states() with a PRD where a passed story has an unresolved dependency

archivedStories.title: Implement worker heartbeat file for stale-worker detection and auto-requeue
archivedStories.description: A crashed parallel ralph worker (OOM kill, API hang) leaves its assigned story stuck indefinitely. Each worker should write a heartbeat timestamp every 30 seconds; the coordinator detects stale heartbeats (>120s) and re-queues the story without incrementing retryCount.
acceptanceCriteria: Each parallel worker writes .spiral/workers/<worker_id>.heartbeat containing {pid, storyId, ts} every 30 seconds
The coordinator checks heartbeat files every 60 seconds; a file not updated in >120s is considered stale
When stale, the story is re-queued (passes stays false, retryCount NOT incremented) and a warning is logged
Heartbeat files are cleaned up on normal worker exit
Integration test: kill a worker mid-run and verify the story is re-queued within 3 minutes
technicalNotes: bash: while sleep 30; do echo '{...}' > .spiral/workers/$WORKER_ID.heartbeat; done & (background loop)
Coordinator: find .spiral/workers/ -name '*.heartbeat' -mmin +2 | while read f; do requeue; done
On Windows use a PowerShell Start-Job for the heartbeat background loop

archivedStories.title: Add schemaVersion field to prd.json with auto-migration on load
archivedStories.description: prd.json has no version field, making it impossible to detect schema changes and safely migrate old files. Projects started months ago on an older Spiral version may have structurally incompatible prd.json files. A schemaVersion field enables migration scripts and clear error messages.
acceptanceCriteria: prd_schema.py accepts an optional schemaVersion integer field (current version: 1)
prd_schema.py emits a warning (not error) when schemaVersion is absent, suggesting the user run spiral --migrate
A lib/migrate_prd.py script upgrades prd.json from any prior version to the current schema (adds missing required fields with defaults)
spiral.sh runs a migration check at startup and aborts with a clear message if prd.json is on an incompatible future version
New prd.json files created by spiral-init include schemaVersion: 1
technicalNotes: Current schema version: 1 (first versioned release)
Migration from unversioned: add schemaVersion=1, add missing dependencies:[] to stories that lack it
lib/migrate_prd.py must be idempotent (safe to run multiple times)

archivedStories.title: Add story tags field and --focus-tags CLI filter to spiral.sh
archivedStories.description: SPIRAL_FOCUS provides a theme hint but does not filter by structured metadata. A tags array on each story (e.g., ['frontend', 'auth', 'bugfix']) combined with a --focus-tags CLI flag lets users run targeted spiral sessions that only implement matching stories, supporting sprint planning and staged rollouts.
acceptanceCriteria: prd_schema.py accepts an optional tags field: a list of non-empty lowercase strings matching /^[a-z0-9_-]+$/
spiral.sh accepts --focus-tags 'frontend,auth' to restrict Phase I to stories whose tags contain at least one match
Stories without matching tags are skipped for the iteration (not failed, not retry-counted)
When --focus-tags is not set, all stories are eligible (no behavior change)
merge_stories.py auto-assigns tag 'bugfix' to stories where isTestFix=true
technicalNotes: jq filter: .userStories[] | select(.passes == false) | select((.tags // []) | any(. == "frontend"))
Tags are additive: a story with tags ['frontend', 'auth'] matches --focus-tags 'auth'
Research output schema should include optional tags field

archivedStories.title: Add HTML dashboard auto-refresh meta tag with configurable interval
archivedStories.description: The HTML metrics dashboard is static and requires manual browser reload. Adding a <meta http-equiv='refresh'> tag with interval from SPIRAL_DASHBOARD_REFRESH_SECS (default: 30) turns it into a live dashboard during active runs without requiring a web server.
acceptanceCriteria: SPIRAL_DASHBOARD_REFRESH_SECS is documented in spiral.config.sh template (default: 30)
Generated dashboard HTML includes <meta http-equiv='refresh' content='30'> (or configured value)
Setting SPIRAL_DASHBOARD_REFRESH_SECS=0 omits the meta tag entirely (static mode)
The refresh interval is displayed in the dashboard footer: 'Auto-refreshing every 30s'
technicalNotes: Inject the meta tag in spiral_dashboard.py HTML generation function
<meta http-equiv='refresh' content='{interval}'> goes in <head>
Consider showing a JS countdown timer as a UX enhancement (optional)

archivedStories.title: Add SPIRAL_SKIP_STORY_IDS for permanent manual story exclusion
archivedStories.description: The _skipped flag handles auto-skip after MAX_RETRIES, but users sometimes want to permanently park a story (blocked externally, or descoped mid-run) without deleting it. SPIRAL_SKIP_STORY_IDS provides a comma-separated list of IDs always passed over without penalty.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.config.sh template documents SPIRAL_SKIP_STORY_IDS with a commented example
Stories whose IDs appear in SPIRAL_SKIP_STORY_IDS are skipped during Phase I selection without incrementing retryCount
Skipped stories appear in --status output with a [MANUAL SKIP] indicator
check_done.py treats manually-skipped stories as non-blocking (they do not prevent SPIRAL COMPLETE)
technicalNotes: Parse SPIRAL_SKIP_STORY_IDS as comma-separated in spiral.sh
jq filter: select(.id as $id | ($SKIP_IDS | split(",") | any(. == $id)) | not)
Manually-skipped stories appear in the HTML review report tagged as 'Skipped by user'

archivedStories.title: Merge parallel worker results.tsv files into main results.tsv
archivedStories.description: In parallel mode, each worker writes telemetry rows to its own worktree's results.tsv. After merge_worker_results.py finishes, the worker results.tsv files are abandoned ï¿½ only the main prd.json is updated. This means the main project's results.tsv is missing all telemetry from parallel runs, breaking spiral_dashboard.py accuracy and spiral_report.py analysis.
acceptanceCriteria: run_parallel_ralph.sh reads each worker's results.tsv after all workers complete
Rows from all worker results.tsv files are appended to the main project results.tsv
Header row is written only if main results.tsv does not already exist
Duplicate rows (same story_id + timestamp combination) are not inserted twice
spiral_dashboard.py shows correct total attempt count when re-run after a parallel session
technicalNotes: Worker worktrees live at $WORKTREE_BASE/worker-N/ ï¿½ each has its own results.tsv at that worktree root
run_parallel_ralph.sh already has a merge step for prd.json; add results.tsv merge immediately after
Use awk/tail to skip the header of each worker file before appending to main
Sort merged rows by timestamp column to maintain chronological order

archivedStories.title: Add disk space preflight check before creating N git worktrees
archivedStories.description: run_parallel_ralph.sh creates N git worktrees, each a full copy of the repository working tree. On large repos or machines with limited disk, this can silently fail mid-execution when disk fills up, leaving the project in an inconsistent state. A preflight check that estimates required space and aborts early with a clear message prevents this.
acceptanceCriteria: Before creating any worktree, compute estimated required bytes: repo_size_kb * RALPH_WORKERS
Check available disk space on the filesystem containing WORKTREE_BASE using df
If estimated_required > available_space * 0.9, abort with a clear error listing repo size, worker count, and free space
On Linux/macOS/Git-Bash the check uses POSIX df syntax; on systems where df fails it degrades gracefully
Check is skipped if SPIRAL_SKIP_DISK_CHECK=1 is set in environment
technicalNotes: Use: du -sk "$REPO_ROOT" to get repo size in KB
Use: df -k "$WORKTREE_BASE" | awk 'NR==2 {print $4}' for available KB
Git worktrees share .git objects ï¿½ actual disk use is ~working tree size, not full clone
Add the check near line 200 of run_parallel_ralph.sh before the worker creation loop

archivedStories.title: Add unit tests for merge_worker_results.py (parallel result promotion)
archivedStories.description: merge_worker_results.py is a critical path module that promotes passes=true, _skipped, _decomposed flags, and new sub-stories from N worker prd.json files back into the main prd.json. It has no test file. Bugs here silently lose work completed by parallel workers.
acceptanceCriteria: tests/test_merge_worker_results.py created with at least 8 test cases
Test: single worker with one passed story promotes it to main prd
Test: worker with _skipped story propagates skipped flag to main prd
Test: worker with _decomposed parent and new sub-stories ï¿½ both promoted correctly
Test: two workers both passing the same story ï¿½ no duplicate in main
Test: worker prd.json fails schema validation ï¿½ returns exit code 1, main prd unchanged
Test: worker file missing ï¿½ warning printed, other workers still processed
All new tests pass: uv run pytest tests/test_merge_worker_results.py -v
technicalNotes: Use tmp_path pytest fixture to create isolated prd.json files per test
Import merge_worker_results.main() directly or invoke via subprocess
Follow pattern of existing tests/test_merge.py for fixture setup style

archivedStories.title: Validate spiral.sh integer CLI arguments before arithmetic
archivedStories.description: spiral.sh performs bash integer arithmetic on --ralph-workers, --ralph-iters, --capacity-limit, and the positional max_iters argument. If a user passes a non-integer value, bash arithmetic fails with a cryptic 'arithmetic syntax error' deep in the loop. Validating integer flags immediately after parsing prevents this with a clear usage error.
acceptanceCriteria: After argument parsing, check MAX_SPIRAL_ITERS, RALPH_MAX_ITERS, RALPH_WORKERS, CAPACITY_LIMIT are valid integers
On invalid value, print: 'Error: --flag requires a positive integer, got: VALUE' and exit 1
TIME_LIMIT_MINS is also validated when --time-limit is used
Valid values pass through unchanged with no regression on normal usage
uv run pytest passes (all existing tests still green)
technicalNotes: Add validation block immediately after the while [[ $# -gt 0 ]] argument parsing loop in spiral.sh
Use bash regex: [[ "$RALPH_WORKERS" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] for positive integers
RALPH_WORKERS must be >= 1; MAX_SPIRAL_ITERS >= 1; CAPACITY_LIMIT >= 0

archivedStories.title: Add SPIRAL_RESEARCH_RETRIES to retry Phase R on transient Claude crash
archivedStories.description: Phase R spawns a Claude agent that writes _research_output.json. If the Claude process crashes (OOM kill, network timeout, API error) before writing the file, spiral.sh continues to Phase T with a stale or missing research output. Adding SPIRAL_RESEARCH_RETRIES (default 2) retries the Claude invocation before falling back.
acceptanceCriteria: SPIRAL_RESEARCH_RETRIES config variable defaults to 2 (read from spiral.config.sh or env)
After Phase R Claude invocation, check if _research_output.json was written and is valid JSON
If missing or invalid, retry the Claude invocation up to SPIRAL_RESEARCH_RETRIES times
Each retry prints: '[R] Research output missing or invalid ï¿½ retrying (attempt N/TOTAL)'
After all retries exhausted, print a warning and continue with previous iteration output or empty
Research succeeding on retry causes Phase T and M to proceed normally
technicalNotes: Check _research_output.json validity after claude invocation: python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('$RESEARCH_OUTPUT'))"
Add a retry loop in spiral.sh Phase R section wrapping the claude invocation command
Exponential backoff is not needed here ï¿½ retries are cheap since Claude starts fresh

archivedStories.title: Add unit tests for spiral_dashboard.py compute functions
archivedStories.description: spiral_dashboard.py contains compute_overview, compute_velocity, compute_model_performance, compute_status_breakdown, and compute_bottlenecks as pure data transformation functions with no test coverage. Bugs in these functions produce silently incorrect dashboard metrics that operators rely on for decision making.
acceptanceCriteria: tests/test_spiral_dashboard.py created with at least 10 test cases
Test compute_overview: empty inputs produce zero counts with no crash
Test compute_overview: partial inputs produce correct passed/pending/skipped counts
Test compute_velocity: rows from multiple iterations produce correct velocity per iteration
Test compute_model_performance: mixed model rows produce correct per-model success rates
Test elapsed time: valid ISO timestamps produce human-readable duration string
Test compute_status_breakdown: stories and attempts produce correct breakdown dict
All tests pass: uv run pytest tests/test_spiral_dashboard.py -v
technicalNotes: Import compute_* functions directly from lib.spiral_dashboard (add sys.path insert)
Build minimal prd/results/retries fixtures as Python dicts ï¿½ no temp files needed
The module is stdlib-only so no extra test dependencies are required

archivedStories.title: Add --prd flag to spiral.sh to specify alternate PRD file path
archivedStories.description: spiral.sh always uses prd.json in the current working directory. Users running spiral on monorepos with multiple prd files or non-standard locations must cd to specific directories or use symlinks. Adding a --prd flag matching ralph.sh's existing --prd flag would eliminate this friction and enable scripted multi-project automation.
acceptanceCriteria: --prd PATH flag accepted in spiral.sh argument parsing block
When --prd is given, PRD_FILE is set to the provided path instead of prd.json
Relative paths are resolved to absolute at parse time using cd/pwd
If the provided path does not exist, spiral.sh exits with an error before any processing
bash spiral.sh --prd /other/project/prd.json --gate skip runs end-to-end correctly
When --prd is absent, behavior is identical to current (backward compatible)
technicalNotes: Add '--prd) PRD_FILE="$2"; shift 2 ;;' to the argument parsing while loop in spiral.sh
Resolve absolute path after parsing: PRD_FILE="$(cd "$(dirname "$PRD_FILE")" && pwd)/$(basename "$PRD_FILE")"
REPO_ROOT derivation uses dirname of PRD_FILE when --prd is supplied

archivedStories.title: Sort prd.json stories by priority and dependency level after Phase M merge
archivedStories.description: After Phase M (merge_stories.py) inserts new research stories, they appear in insertion order, not priority order. Since ralph picks the first story where passes=false, low-priority new stories inserted ahead of high-priority pending stories get implemented first. Re-sorting after every merge ensures ralph always works highest-priority first.
acceptanceCriteria: merge_stories.py sorts all userStories after merging: critical < high < medium < low
Within each priority tier, stories with fewer unmet dependencies come first
Stories with passes=true, _decomposed=true, or _skipped=true sort to the end
Sort is stable: stories with equal priority and dep count preserve relative insertion order
Existing unit tests for merge_stories.py still pass; one new test verifies sort order
technicalNotes: Add sort step at end of merge_stories.py main() before the atomic prd.json write
Priority rank: critical=0, high=1, medium=2, low=3
Dependency count tiebreaker: len(story.get('dependencies', []))
Python stable sort: stories.sort(key=lambda s: (done_rank(s), priority_rank(s), dep_count(s)))

archivedStories.title: Add SPIRAL_WORKER_MEMORY_LIMIT for per-worker V8 heap cap
archivedStories.description: All processes (orchestrator, research, workers) share the same SPIRAL_MEMORY_LIMIT for V8 --max-old-space-size. The orchestrator runs lightly while workers run full Claude CLI sessions. Separate limits let operators give workers more memory without over-allocating for the orchestrator, reducing OOM risk on memory-constrained machines.
acceptanceCriteria: SPIRAL_WORKER_MEMORY_LIMIT config variable added, defaulting to ${SPIRAL_MEMORY_LIMIT:-1024}
run_parallel_ralph.sh exports SPIRAL_MEMORY_LIMIT=$SPIRAL_WORKER_MEMORY_LIMIT before each worker launch
spiral.sh orchestrator continues using its own SPIRAL_MEMORY_LIMIT for research phase NODE_OPTIONS
Worker ralph.sh processes inherit the overridden SPIRAL_MEMORY_LIMIT via environment
templates/spiral.config.example.sh documents SPIRAL_WORKER_MEMORY_LIMIT with example value 2048
technicalNotes: In run_parallel_ralph.sh, before spawning each worker: export SPIRAL_MEMORY_LIMIT="${SPIRAL_WORKER_MEMORY_LIMIT:-$SPIRAL_MEMORY_LIMIT}"
ralph.sh already sets NODE_OPTIONS from SPIRAL_MEMORY_LIMIT so only the env var needs to change
Add SPIRAL_WORKER_MEMORY_LIMIT=2048 with comment to spiral.config.example.sh

archivedStories.title: Log Gemini Phase R failure reason (rate-limit vs error vs empty output)
archivedStories.description: Phase R uses || true to swallow all Gemini CLI errors. When Gemini returns empty output, spiral.sh logs 'Gemini web research returned empty' but gives no reason ï¿½ making it impossible to distinguish a 429 rate limit, API key error, network failure, or legitimate empty output. Capturing stderr enables targeted recovery messages.
acceptanceCriteria: Gemini invocation captures stderr to a temp file: gemini ... 2>"$GEMINI_ERR_TMP" || true
If GEMINI_RESEARCH is empty and stderr contains '429' or 'rate limit', print: '[R] Gemini rate-limited ï¿½ Claude will browse URLs directly'
If stderr contains 'PERMISSION_DENIED' or 'API key', print: '[R] Gemini auth error ï¿½ check GEMINI_API_KEY'
If stderr is non-empty but unknown pattern, print the first line as diagnostic context
If GEMINI_RESEARCH is non-empty, no stderr check is performed
Temp file is cleaned up after the check in all code paths
technicalNotes: Replace: GEMINI_RESEARCH=$(gemini ... 2>/dev/null || true) with stderr capture pattern
GEMINI_ERR_TMP=$(mktemp); then gemini ... 2>"$GEMINI_ERR_TMP" || true; then check file
Rate limit detection pattern: grep -qi '429\|RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED\|rate.limit\|quota' "$GEMINI_ERR_TMP"

archivedStories.title: Isolate parallel worker failures so one crash does not abort sibling workers
archivedStories.description: run_parallel_ralph.sh spawns N workers in background subshells. If a worker exits non-zero, bash set -e behavior in the outer script can propagate the error and abort remaining workers. Workers that fail due to git conflicts, OOM, or network errors should be reported individually while sibling workers continue to completion.
acceptanceCriteria: Each background worker PID is collected into an array after launch
After all workers are spawned, iterate per-PID: wait $PID; worker_status=$?
If a worker exits non-zero, print: '[parallel] Worker N exited with status S ï¿½ continuing remaining workers'
Failed worker worktree is cleaned up on the same path as successful workers
merge_worker_results.py is still called with all worker prd paths ï¿½ missing workers emit warnings but do not abort the merge
If all workers fail, exit run_parallel_ralph.sh with a non-zero exit code
technicalNotes: Replace any bulk 'wait' call with a per-PID wait loop: for pid in "${WORKER_PIDS[@]}"; do wait "$pid" || failed=$((failed+1)); done
Track failed_count; if failed_count == RALPH_WORKERS, exit 1 after cleanup
The existing EXIT/INT/TERM trap handles cleanup ï¿½ this change only affects normal worker exit code handling

archivedStories.title: Dashboard: add per-story attempt history drilldown via HTML details element
archivedStories.description: spiral_dashboard.py shows aggregate metrics but not which specific attempts were made for a given story. When debugging a repeatedly-failing story, engineers must manually parse results.tsv. Adding an expandable drilldown per story (all attempt rows with model, status, duration, commit) makes failure analysis self-contained in the dashboard.
acceptanceCriteria: HTML dashboard has a Stories section with one row per story showing id, title, status indicator
Each story row has a Details toggle (HTML <details> element) expanding to show attempt rows from results.tsv for that story_id
Attempt rows show: timestamp, model, tool, status, duration_sec, retry_num, commit_sha
Stories with no attempt history show 'No attempts recorded' in the expanded section
Feature uses only HTML/CSS with no JavaScript dependency
Dashboard still generates correctly when results.tsv is missing (Stories section shows prd data only)
technicalNotes: Group results rows by story_id in a new compute_story_attempts() function before HTML generation
Use HTML5 <details><summary> accordion elements ï¿½ zero JavaScript required
Insert Stories drilldown section after the overview cards and before the velocity chart

archivedStories.title: Store _failureReason field in prd.json when story is skipped or decomposed
archivedStories.description: When a story exceeds MAX_RETRIES and is skipped, the reason (time budget exceeded, quality gate, all retries exhausted) is written only to progress.txt as free text. After many iterations, identifying why a specific story was skipped requires grepping progress.txt. Storing a structured _failureReason in prd.json makes this queryable and visible in the dashboard.
acceptanceCriteria: When ralph.sh skips a story after MAX_RETRIES, set _failureReason: 'MAX_RETRIES exhausted (quality gate failed)' or similar
When a story is skipped due to time budget exceeded, set _failureReason: 'TIME_BUDGET_EXCEEDED (Xs > Ys limit)'
_failureReason is preserved when merge_worker_results.py promotes skipped stories from workers to main prd
spiral_dashboard.py displays _failureReason in a tooltip or the story drilldown section
prd_schema.py validates _failureReason as an optional string field (no required update to existing stories)
technicalNotes: In ralph.sh, when writing _skipped=true via jq, pipe a second jq to set ._failureReason
Escape reason string for JSON: use jq --arg reason "$REASON" '.field = $arg'
Add optional _failureReason: { type: 'string' } to prd_schema.py STORY_SCHEMA

archivedStories.title: Wizard: dry-run SPIRAL_VALIDATE_CMD before writing to spiral.config.sh
archivedStories.description: The /spiral-init wizard asks for SPIRAL_VALIDATE_CMD but never verifies the command works before writing it to config. If the user enters a wrong path or missing executable, every Phase V validation will fail and spiral will loop forever treating all tests as broken. A quick dry-run during setup catches this at the source.
acceptanceCriteria: After user enters SPIRAL_VALIDATE_CMD, wizard runs: timeout 30 bash -c "$SPIRAL_VALIDATE_CMD" and checks exit code
If exit 0: print '[wizard] Validate command verified ï¿½ writing to config'
If non-zero exit or timeout: print 'Command returned exit N ï¿½ use anyway? (y/N)' and wait for input
If exit 127 (command not found): print specific error '[wizard] Command not found: <cmd>' with install hint
User pressing Enter (default N) re-prompts for the command; y accepts as-is
Empty SPIRAL_VALIDATE_CMD input skips the dry-run and uses the detected project default
technicalNotes: Add dry-run check in ralph/skills/spiral-init.md after the SPIRAL_VALIDATE_CMD input block
Use timeout to prevent hanging on infinite-loop test suites
Exit code 127 is the standard POSIX shell 'command not found' code

archivedStories.title: Add integration test for run_parallel_ralph.sh with mock worker scripts
archivedStories.description: run_parallel_ralph.sh (622 lines) is the most complex orchestration script and has zero automated test coverage. It creates git worktrees, partitions prd.json, spawns background processes, merges results, and cleans up ï¿½ many steps that can fail independently. A minimal integration test using mock worker scripts validates the orchestration without real Claude agents.
acceptanceCriteria: tests/test_parallel_orchestration.py or tests/test_parallel_integration.sh created
Test setup: creates a temp git repo with a minimal prd.json (3 stories) configured for 2 workers
Mock SPIRAL_RALPH: a bash script that marks one story passes=true in its worker prd.json and exits 0
After run_parallel_ralph.sh, main prd.json has the story marked passes=true
After completion, worktrees are cleaned up from the filesystem
Second scenario: one mock worker exits 1, the other succeeds ï¿½ successful worker's result is still merged
Test is runnable via: uv run pytest tests/test_parallel_orchestration.py -v
technicalNotes: Use pytest with subprocess.run to call run_parallel_ralph.sh with a custom SPIRAL_RALPH env pointing to a mock script
Mock ralph.sh script: reads its worker prd.json, finds first pending story, sets passes=true via jq, exits 0
Requires git to be available in the test environment (already a SPIRAL prerequisite)

archivedStories.title: Add --version flag to spiral.sh showing installed git version
archivedStories.description: There is no way to query which version of SPIRAL is installed. Users updating their installation or reporting bugs cannot identify the exact version. Adding --version that prints the git describe output from SPIRAL_HOME makes version identification trivial and enables bug reports to include version context.
acceptanceCriteria: --version flag added to spiral.sh argument parsing
When --version is given, print 'SPIRAL version <git-describe or commit SHA>' and exit 0
Version derived from: git -C "$SPIRAL_HOME" describe --tags --always 2>/dev/null
If SPIRAL_HOME is not a git repo (zip install), print: 'SPIRAL version unknown (not a git repository)'
--version is documented in --help output
technicalNotes: Add '--version) echo "SPIRAL version $(git -C "$SPIRAL_HOME" describe --tags --always 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"; exit 0 ;;' early in argument parsing
Use --dirty=+ suffix to indicate uncommitted changes: git describe --tags --always --dirty=+
Expose as SPIRAL_VERSION env var for checkpoint.json recording

archivedStories.title: Auto-detect SPIRAL_STORY_PREFIX from existing prd.json IDs at wizard init
archivedStories.description: When /spiral-init runs on a project that already has a prd.json with custom story IDs (e.g., FEAT-001, TICKET-042), the wizard defaults to SPIRAL_STORY_PREFIX=US, causing new stories to get inconsistent IDs. Auto-detecting the prefix from existing IDs and pre-filling the wizard improves consistency without user effort.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral-init wizard scans existing prd.json userStories[*].id before prompting for STORY_PREFIX
If existing IDs share a consistent prefix pattern ([A-Z]+-NNN), extract that prefix
Pre-fill the SPIRAL_STORY_PREFIX prompt with the detected prefix
If no existing stories or no consistent prefix found, default to 'US' as before
User can still override the pre-filled value
Detected prefix is written to spiral.config.sh as SPIRAL_STORY_PREFIX=<value>
technicalNotes: Detection step in spiral-init.md: DETECTED_PREFIX=$(cat prd.json | jq -r '.userStories[0].id // "" | split("-")[0]' 2>/dev/null)
Validate detected prefix matches ^[A-Z]+$ before using it
Only use detected prefix if at least 2 existing stories share the same prefix

archivedStories.title: Emit SPIRAL_VERSION to _checkpoint.json for version mismatch detection on resume
archivedStories.description: When a SPIRAL session is interrupted and resumed later, the installed SPIRAL version may have changed (e.g., user git-pulled an update). If the new version changed checkpoint format or phase behavior, resuming from an old checkpoint can cause subtle bugs. Recording the version in _checkpoint.json enables detection and a warning on mismatch.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.sh derives SPIRAL_VERSION at startup: git -C "$SPIRAL_HOME" describe --tags --always 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown'
When writing _checkpoint.json, include a spiralVersion field with the current SPIRAL_VERSION
When loading an existing checkpoint, compare its spiralVersion field with current SPIRAL_VERSION
If versions differ, print: '[checkpoint] WARNING: checkpoint written by SPIRAL <old>, current is <new>'
Warning is informational only and does not abort execution
uv run pytest passes with checkpoint tests updated to include the spiralVersion field
technicalNotes: Add SPIRAL_VERSION derivation near the top of spiral.sh after SPIRAL_HOME is set
The checkpoint read/write is in spiral.sh inline or lib/state_machine.py ï¿½ update whichever writes the checkpoint dict
Version comparison uses string equality; no semver parsing needed

archivedStories.title: Add SIGCHLD trap to spiral.sh to reap zombie worker processes
archivedStories.description: When parallel workers exit, their process table entries persist as zombies until the parent calls wait(). Without a SIGCHLD handler, SPIRAL accumulates zombie workers during long parallel runs, eventually exhausting PID space. A `trap 'wait -n 2>/dev/null; true' SIGCHLD` in spiral.sh immediately reaps terminated children on signal delivery.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.sh installs a SIGCHLD trap that calls `wait -n 2>/dev/null; true` to reap all available zombie children
After N parallel workers complete, `ps aux | grep defunct` shows zero zombie entries from spiral.sh children
The trap does not interfere with the existing SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown trap (US-017)
technicalNotes: Use `trap 'while wait -n 2>/dev/null; do :; done; true' SIGCHLD` to drain all zombies in one handler invocation
`wait -n` (bash 4.3+) waits for any one child; the `true` suppresses non-zero exit when no children remain
Source: http://www.microhowto.info/howto/reap_zombie_processes_using_a_sigchld_handler.html

archivedStories.title: Lock git worktrees during active worker execution to prevent prune races
archivedStories.description: `git worktree prune` can silently remove a worktree whose directory was briefly absent during worker setup, causing a live worker to operate on a deleted worktree. The `git worktree lock` command prevents automatic pruning of an in-use worktree. SPIRAL should lock each worktree at worker launch and unlock it on worker exit.
acceptanceCriteria: run_parallel_ralph.sh calls `git worktree lock .spiral-workers/worker-N --reason 'worker-N running story $STORY_ID'` immediately after `git worktree add`
`git worktree unlock .spiral-workers/worker-N` is called in the worker's EXIT trap so it fires even on crash
Running `git worktree prune` while a worker is active does NOT remove the locked worktree
technicalNotes: `git worktree lock [--reason <string>] <path>` — officially supported since Git 2.7
Place unlock in the EXIT trap alongside the existing SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers
Source: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree#Documentation/git-worktree.txt-lock

archivedStories.title: Guard against 'branch already checked out' before git worktree add
archivedStories.description: Git refuses to create a worktree for a branch already checked out in another worktree, causing a hard failure that crashes the worker launch loop. Before calling `git worktree add`, SPIRAL must verify the target branch is free or use detached HEAD mode to avoid the collision entirely.
acceptanceCriteria: Before `git worktree add`, run_parallel_ralph.sh calls `git worktree list --porcelain` and checks if the target branch appears in any existing worktree
If the branch is in use, the script falls back to `git worktree add --detach .spiral-workers/worker-N <commit>` (detached HEAD mode)
A clear log message explains the detached HEAD fallback when it occurs
technicalNotes: `git worktree list --porcelain` outputs `branch refs/heads/<name>` per worktree; grep for the target branch name
Detached HEAD worktrees (`git worktree add --detach`) are not subject to the branch-in-use check
Source: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree#_notes (branch already checked out limitation)

archivedStories.title: Handle HTTP 529 overloaded_error with separate backoff strategy from 429
archivedStories.description: The Anthropic API returns 529 (overloaded_error) when its servers are under load — distinct from 429 (rate_limit_error). The existing 429 handler uses the `retry-after` header, which is absent on 529 responses. A separate handler with exponential backoff and jitter (2s base, 30s cap, 10% jitter) should be applied for 529 errors to avoid immediate re-hammering.
acceptanceCriteria: ralph.sh detects HTTP 529 or `error.type == overloaded_error` in Claude CLI output separately from 429 detection
On 529, ralph.sh applies exponential backoff: `sleep $((base * 2**attempt + RANDOM % jitter_range))` up to 30s cap
529 events are logged to `.spiral/spiral_events.jsonl` as `api_overloaded` with retry attempt number
529 retries do NOT consume a story's `_retryCount` (unlike implementation failures)
technicalNotes: Anthropic API returns 529 for system-wide overload; distinct from per-account 429 with retry-after header
Recommended backoff: base=2s, cap=30s, jitter=10% of delay: `jitter=$(( (delay * 10) / 100 ))`
Source: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api/errors and https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api/rate-limits

archivedStories.title: Prune stale git worktree admin records on worker completion
archivedStories.description: When a worktree directory is removed without `git worktree remove` (e.g., after a crash), Git retains orphaned admin records in `.git/worktrees/`. These accumulate over many SPIRAL runs. Adding `git worktree prune` to the post-worker cleanup step removes dangling references and keeps `.git/worktrees/` clean.
acceptanceCriteria: After each worker completes, spiral.sh (or run_parallel_ralph.sh cleanup hook) calls `git worktree prune`
`git worktree list` shows no stale entries after N completed parallel runs
If `git worktree prune` is run while another worker is locked, it does not remove the locked worktree
technicalNotes: `git worktree prune --dry-run` logs what would be removed; useful for debugging without side effects
`git worktree prune --expire now` removes entries with no grace period for CI cleanliness
Source: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree#Documentation/git-worktree.txt-prune

archivedStories.title: Detect streaming Claude API overload errors returned with HTTP 200 status
archivedStories.description: When Claude CLI streams a response, an overloaded_error can arrive in the first chunk while the HTTP status is 200 OK. Standard exit-code-based retry logic silently misses these errors, causing story implementation to proceed with empty output. SPIRAL needs to inspect streamed output for `"type": "error"` in the first response chunk.
acceptanceCriteria: ralph.sh (or its Claude invocation wrapper) inspects Claude CLI stdout for the pattern `"type":"error"` in the first line/chunk
When detected, the overloaded_error is treated identically to an HTTP 529 (apply 529 backoff, log `api_overloaded` event)
A bats test verifies the detection with a mocked claude binary that emits a canned overload JSON body
technicalNotes: Claude CLI streams NDJSON; first line may be `{"type":"error","error":{"type":"overloaded_error","message":"..."}}`
Capture first line: `first_line=$(claude ... | { IFS= read -r line; echo "$line"; cat > /dev/null; echo "$line"; })`
Source: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api/errors (streaming errors section)

archivedStories.title: Apply jitter to all API retries in ralph.sh to prevent thundering herd
archivedStories.description: When multiple parallel SPIRAL workers hit a 429/529 error simultaneously and retry after the same fixed delay, they re-hit the API limit together (thundering herd). Encapsulating retry logic with per-worker random jitter in a shared `lib/spiral_retry.sh` bash function prevents synchronized retries across workers.
acceptanceCriteria: A new `lib/spiral_retry.sh` exports a `spiral_api_retry <cmd>` function that wraps any Claude CLI invocation with retry+jitter logic
Each retry delay adds `RANDOM % SPIRAL_RETRY_JITTER_S` seconds (configurable, default 5) to the base backoff
spiral_retry.sh is sourced by both spiral.sh Phase R and ralph.sh Phase I
SPIRAL_RETRY_JITTER_S is documented in templates/spiral.config.example.sh
technicalNotes: Jitter formula: `sleep_s=$(( base_delay + (RANDOM % jitter_range) ))` where RANDOM is bash built-in (0-32767)
Each worker's RANDOM seed differs by PID: `RANDOM=$$` at script start produces worker-unique sequences
Source: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api/rate-limits (retry recommendations)

archivedStories.title: Add SPIRAL_RUN_ID correlation field to all structured log entries
archivedStories.description: When multiple SPIRAL runs share a `spiral_events.jsonl` file or a metrics file, there is no way to filter entries from a single run. Generating a `SPIRAL_RUN_ID` UUID at startup and including it in every structured output row enables complete run-level filtering without modifying file paths.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.sh generates `SPIRAL_RUN_ID=$(uuidgen 2>/dev/null || printf '%x%x' $(date +%s) $RANDOM)` at startup and exports it
Every row written to `spiral_events.jsonl` includes `"run_id": "$SPIRAL_RUN_ID"`
Every row written to `results.tsv` includes `run_id` as a new column
SPIRAL_RUN_ID is written to `_checkpoint.json` so it persists across crash-resume cycles
technicalNotes: Equivalent to OTel's `Resource.service.instance.id` — enables filtering all events from one run
Write to checkpoint: `jq '. + {run_id: env.SPIRAL_RUN_ID}' _checkpoint.json > _checkpoint.json.tmp && mv _checkpoint.json.tmp _checkpoint.json`
Source: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/logs/data-model/ (log correlation IDs)

archivedStories.title: Add bats test scaffold for spiral.sh phase transitions
archivedStories.description: spiral.sh has no shell-level tests — only Python unit tests for the lib/ utilities. A bats-core test suite validates that each phase flag (--gate skip, --gate proceed, --skip-research) produces the expected exit codes and output files without requiring a live Claude API, providing test coverage for the orchestration layer.
acceptanceCriteria: test/spiral_phases.bats exists with bats-core, bats-assert, and bats-mock as git submodules in test/
`setup_file()` creates a temp REPO_ROOT with a minimal prd.json and a mocked `claude` binary on PATH
Tests cover: `--gate skip` exits 0, `--gate quit` exits 0 with no implementation, `--skip-research` skips Phase R
`bats test/spiral_phases.bats` runs in CI without any real API key or network access
technicalNotes: bats-core setup: `git submodule add https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core test/bats`
Mock claude binary: create a bash stub via bats-mock that writes canned _research_output.json and exits 0
Use `run bash spiral.sh 1 --gate skip` and `assert_success`; check artifacts with `assert_file_exists`
Source: https://bats-core.readthedocs.io/en/stable/writing-tests.html

archivedStories.title: Add bats tests for lib/ shell utility scripts
archivedStories.description: validate_preflight.sh, memory-pressure-check.sh, and spiral_assert.sh have no automated tests. bats-core provides `run`, `assert_success`, `assert_failure`, and `assert_output` helpers ideal for testing these small shell scripts in isolation with mocked inputs, catching regressions in preflight checks.
acceptanceCriteria: test/lib/validate_preflight.bats tests that validate_preflight.sh exits non-zero when a required tool (jq, git) is absent from PATH
test/lib/memory_pressure.bats tests that memory-pressure-check.sh exits 1 when free memory (mocked via /proc/meminfo stub) is below threshold
test/lib/spiral_assert.bats tests assert_file_exists and assert_json_key helpers with known fixtures
All lib bats tests pass with `bats test/lib/`
technicalNotes: Mock missing binaries: `mock_create; mock_set_status $mock 1; export PATH="$(dirname $mock):$PATH"`
bats-file library provides `assert_file_exists`, `assert_file_not_empty` assertions out of the box
Source: https://bats-core.readthedocs.io/en/stable/usage.html

archivedStories.title: Add workflow_dispatch inputs to SPIRAL GitHub Actions workflow for manual reruns
archivedStories.description: The existing GitHub Actions CI workflow runs SPIRAL only on push/PR events. Adding `workflow_dispatch` with inputs (`max_iterations`, `gate`, `dry_run`) lets operators manually trigger a SPIRAL run from the GitHub UI — useful for a research-only pass or re-running after a transient API failure without pushing a commit.
acceptanceCriteria: `.github/workflows/spiral.yml` adds a `workflow_dispatch:` trigger with inputs: `max_iterations` (string, default '5'), `gate` (choice: proceed/skip/quit, default proceed), `dry_run` (boolean, default false)
The workflow step passes inputs to spiral.sh: `bash spiral.sh ${{ inputs.max_iterations }} --gate ${{ inputs.gate }}`
When `dry_run` is true, the workflow overrides gate to `skip` regardless of the gate input
The manual trigger appears in the GitHub Actions UI under 'Run workflow'
technicalNotes: workflow_dispatch supports up to 25 inputs with types: string, choice, boolean, environment
Inputs accessed via `${{ inputs.max_iterations }}` or `${{ github.event.inputs.max_iterations }}`
Source: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/events-that-trigger-workflows#workflow_dispatch

archivedStories.title: Dashboard: detect and report orphaned git worktrees vs live worker PIDs
archivedStories.description: After a crash or hard kill, `.spiral-workers/worker-N` directories may remain as orphaned worktrees whose worker processes are dead. spiral_dashboard.py should cross-reference `git worktree list` against live worker PID files (via `os.kill(pid, 0)`) and surface any orphaned worktrees with a suggested prune command.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral_dashboard.py reads active worker PID files from `.spiral-workers/worker-N/worker.pid`
For each PID file, it checks liveness with `os.kill(pid, 0)` — `ProcessLookupError` means dead PID
For each dead-PID worktree, the dashboard displays an 'ORPHANED' status with the worktree path and `git worktree remove <path>` suggested command
The orphan check runs at dashboard startup (not on a background timer)
technicalNotes: `subprocess.run(['git', 'worktree', 'list', '--porcelain'], capture_output=True)` gives structured worktree info
`os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `ProcessLookupError` if PID is dead, `PermissionError` if alive but not owned by us
Source: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree

archivedStories.title: disown background workers in spiral.sh to decouple from terminal SIGHUP
archivedStories.description: Background workers launched with `&` in spiral.sh receive SIGHUP when the controlling terminal closes (e.g., SSH disconnect), killing all workers mid-story. Calling `disown $!` after each worker launch removes it from the shell job table, preventing HUP propagation. Worker lifecycle is then tracked exclusively through PID files.
acceptanceCriteria: In run_parallel_ralph.sh, `disown $worker_pid` is called immediately after launching each worker with `&` and capturing `$!`
Closing the SSH session that launched SPIRAL does NOT send SIGHUP to running worker processes
Worker PIDs are written to `.spiral-workers/worker-N/worker.pid` before disown so they remain trackable
The existing SIGINT trap in spiral.sh still terminates workers explicitly when Ctrl+C is pressed (via `kill $worker_pids`)
technicalNotes: `disown $!` removes the most recently backgrounded job from the shell's job table without killing it
Pattern: `start_worker & worker_pid=$!; echo $worker_pid > worker.pid; disown $worker_pid`
Source: https://mywiki.wooledge.org/ProcessManagement

archivedStories.title: Emit JUnit XML from bats runs for GitHub Actions test summary
archivedStories.description: bats-core natively supports `--formatter junit` output, which GitHub Actions renders as a test summary panel with pass/fail counts per test case. Adding a JUnit XML output step to the CI workflow provides per-test visibility in the PR checks panel alongside the existing pytest JUnit output.
acceptanceCriteria: The GitHub Actions CI workflow runs `bats --formatter tap --report-formatter junit -o test-reports/ test/` in a dedicated step
