The step uploads `test-reports/*.xml` as a workflow artifact
GitHub Actions test summary shows the bats results panel with individual test names and pass/fail status
`test-reports/` is listed in .gitignore
technicalNotes: bats invocation: `bats --formatter tap --report-formatter junit -o test-reports/ test/`
Use `dorny/test-reporter@v1` action to parse JUnit XML and post PR annotations
Source: https://bats-core.readthedocs.io/en/stable/usage.html#reporters

archivedStories.title: Upload SPIRAL output artifacts (prd.json, spiral_events.jsonl) in CI workflow
archivedStories.description: SPIRAL generates key output files (prd.json, _research_output.json, results.tsv, spiral_events.jsonl) during a CI run but they are lost when the runner terminates. Uploading them as workflow artifacts with `actions/upload-artifact@v4` preserves intermediate state for post-run debugging without checking generated files into git.
acceptanceCriteria: A post-run step in `.github/workflows/spiral.yml` uses `actions/upload-artifact@v4` to upload `prd.json`, `.spiral/_research_output.json`, `results.tsv`, and `.spiral/spiral_events.jsonl`
Artifact name includes the run ID: `spiral-outputs-${{ github.run_id }}`
The upload step runs with `if: always()` so artifacts are preserved even on failure
Artifacts are retained for 7 days (set via `retention-days: 7`)
technicalNotes: actions/upload-artifact@v4 supports multi-path globs via YAML block scalar under `path:`
As of Feb 2026, v4 supports `archive: false` for non-zipped uploads (faster for text files)
Source: https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact and https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/store-and-share-data

archivedStories.title: Add per-worker execution timeout using `timeout --kill-after` in run_parallel_ralph.sh
archivedStories.description: Workers that hang indefinitely (e.g., waiting on a stalled Claude CLI subprocess) currently block the entire parallel batch with no recovery path. Wrapping each worker invocation with `timeout --kill-after=60s ${SPIRAL_WORKER_TIMEOUT:-600}s` provides a two-phase SIGTERM→SIGKILL sequence and returns exit code 124 on expiry, allowing the coordinator to distinguish a timeout from a crash and requeue the story.
acceptanceCriteria: SPIRAL_WORKER_TIMEOUT env var (default 600s) controls per-worker wall-clock limit
Worker process tree receives SIGTERM first, then SIGKILL after 60s grace period
Exit code 124 from timeout is detected and logged as a distinct 'timeout' failure reason in results.tsv
Timed-out stories are reset to pending for the next iteration rather than counted as a retry
Integration test: a mock worker that sleeps 700s is killed within SPIRAL_WORKER_TIMEOUT+75s
technicalNotes: Use `timeout --kill-after=60s ${SPIRAL_WORKER_TIMEOUT:-600}s bash ralph.sh ...` in run_parallel_ralph.sh
Detect exit code 124 and write {"_failureReason": "worker_timeout"} to prd.json story entry
bash's built-in timeout may lack --kill-after on some MSYS2 builds; fall back to a background SIGKILL watchdog if GNU timeout is unavailable
Coordinate with SIGCHLD trap (pending story) to avoid double-reaping

archivedStories.title: Add SPIRAL_VALIDATE_TIMEOUT to bound Phase V test-suite execution time
archivedStories.description: Phase V runs the full test suite via SPIRAL_VALIDATE_CMD with no deadline. If a test hangs (e.g., an integration test waiting on an unavailable network resource), the entire SPIRAL loop stalls indefinitely. Adding SPIRAL_VALIDATE_TIMEOUT (default 300s) wraps the validate command with a timeout and surfaces a clear failure message rather than a silent hang.
acceptanceCriteria: SPIRAL_VALIDATE_TIMEOUT env var (default 300s) limits Phase V wall-clock time
When Phase V times out, spiral_events.jsonl receives a phase_timeout event with duration_ms
Phase V timeout is treated as a test failure (not a crash), allowing the loop to continue to Phase C
A warning message is printed: 'Phase V timed out after Xs — treating as validation failure'
SPIRAL_VALIDATE_TIMEOUT=0 disables the timeout (unlimited, matching current behaviour)
technicalNotes: Apply `timeout ${SPIRAL_VALIDATE_TIMEOUT:-300}s bash -c "$SPIRAL_VALIDATE_CMD"` in spiral.sh Phase V block
Exit code 124 maps to a synthetic test failure report so Phase C sees a failing state
Document in spiral.config.sh template with a note that slow integration test suites may need a higher value

archivedStories.title: Detect git merge conflicts with `git merge-tree` before parallel worker integration
archivedStories.description: When multiple workers implement stories that touch the same files, merging them back to main can produce conflicts that are only discovered after all workers have finished. Using `git merge-tree $(git merge-base HEAD main) HEAD main` as a non-destructive dry-run before each worker pushes allows early conflict detection and targeted requeuing of only the conflicting stories without discarding sibling workers' results.
acceptanceCriteria: After each worker completes Phase I, run `git merge-tree` dry-run against the main branch before git push
If merge-tree reports conflicts, the worker marks its stories as pending (not failed) and logs the conflicting file paths
The coordinator in run_parallel_ralph.sh surfaces per-worker conflict status in spiral_events.jsonl
Non-conflicting workers continue to merge normally; only conflicting workers are requeued
bats integration test covers the conflict-detected requeue path with a fixture repo
technicalNotes: Command: `git merge-tree $(git merge-base HEAD "$MAIN_BRANCH") HEAD "$MAIN_BRANCH"` — exit code 0 = no conflicts, non-zero = conflicts
`git merge-tree` is available in Git 2.38+ with improved output; fall back to a test merge + reset for older Git versions
See github.com/clash-sh/clash for a reference implementation pattern in a parallel-agent context
Conflicts reset story state to 'pending' with _failureReason: 'merge_conflict' to distinguish from implementation failures

archivedStories.title: Add `spiral.sh --replay STORY_ID` to re-run a single story without full loop
archivedStories.description: Developers frequently need to re-run a single story without triggering the full 7-phase loop, resetting the story's pass state, and waiting through Phases R/T/M/G. A `spiral.sh --replay US-XXX` mode sets only the target story to pending, skips Phases R/T/M/G, runs Phase I for that story only in an isolated worktree, then validates and reports. This reduces the inner feedback loop from minutes to seconds.
acceptanceCriteria: `spiral.sh --replay US-XXX` accepts a single story ID and runs only Phases I+V+C for that story
All other stories remain untouched in prd.json during replay
Replay creates an isolated git worktree `.spiral-replay-{STORY_ID}` so main branch is not polluted
Phase G (human gate) is automatically skipped in replay mode
Replay result (pass/fail + log path) is printed on exit and written to spiral_events.jsonl
Error with exit 1 if the story ID does not exist in prd.json
technicalNotes: Extract the single-story execution path already present in ralph.sh; replay mode sets STORY_IDS=US-XXX before Phase I
Replay worktree is cleaned up on successful pass; preserved on failure for inspection
`main.py` CLI (pending story) should expose `spiral replay` as a subcommand for symmetry

archivedStories.title: Add UNIX /proc/meminfo memory pressure adapter for cross-platform watchdog parity
archivedStories.description: The current memory pressure watchdog (memory-watchdog.ps1) is PowerShell-only, leaving UNIX/Linux/WSL environments without adaptive memory signals. Adding a Bash adapter that reads MemAvailable from /proc/meminfo (Linux) or uses vm_stat on macOS provides the same JSON signal file that spiral.sh already consumes, giving cross-platform parity with no changes to the main loop.
acceptanceCriteria: New script lib/memory-watchdog.sh detects platform (Linux vs macOS) and reads available memory
On Linux: reads MemAvailable from /proc/meminfo (not MemFree — MemAvailable accounts for reclaimable cache)
On macOS: reads Pages free from vm_stat, converts page size to MB
Outputs the same JSON signal format that memory-pressure-check.sh already expects
spiral.sh auto-selects the watchdog based on platform: .ps1 on Windows, .sh on UNIX
Unit test covers the platform-detection branch and mock /proc/meminfo parsing
technicalNotes: MemAvailable field (not MemFree) is the correct metric — Red Hat KB 406773 explains why MemFree underestimates available memory
Cross-platform pattern: `if [ -f /proc/meminfo ]; then awk '/MemAvailable/ {print int($2/1024)}' /proc/meminfo; else vm_stat | awk '/Pages free/ {print int($3*4096/1048576)}'; fi`
The JSON signal file path should be configurable (SPIRAL_MEMORY_SIGNAL_FILE) so both watchdogs write to the same location

archivedStories.title: Add SPIRAL_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK for per-phase-transition HTTP POST notifications
archivedStories.description: The pending SPIRAL_ON_COMPLETE hook fires only at run completion. Teams operating SPIRAL in long-running unattended sessions need real-time phase-transition notifications (e.g., 'Phase G awaiting approval', 'Phase V failed') delivered to Slack, Teams, or a custom endpoint. Adding SPIRAL_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK sends a JSON POST at each phase start/end, enabling live monitoring without polling the log file.
acceptanceCriteria: SPIRAL_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK env var accepts an HTTPS URL
A POST is sent at the start and end of each phase (R, T, M, G, I, V, C) with JSON body: {run_id, phase, event: start|end, status: ok|failed|skipped, timestamp_iso, iteration}
Webhook POST failures are non-fatal: log a warning and continue the loop
SPIRAL_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT (default 5s) bounds each POST so the loop is not blocked
Phase G approval-pending event body includes the gate report file path
curl is used for the POST to avoid additional Python dependencies
technicalNotes: Implement as a Bash function `notify_webhook()` called at each phase boundary in spiral.sh
JSON body constructed with jq for correct escaping of special characters
SPIRAL_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_HEADERS optional env var allows Authorization: Bearer token header
Slack Incoming Webhooks accept this JSON format natively; Teams uses a similar shape

archivedStories.title: Add max diff size guard in ralph.sh to warn on oversized story implementations
archivedStories.description: AI-generated implementations that produce very large diffs (>500 lines changed) are frequently low quality — the model has gone off-scope, added unnecessary boilerplate, or implemented far more than the story required. A configurable SPIRAL_MAX_DIFF_LINES guard in ralph.sh detects oversized diffs before committing and marks the story for review or automatic retry with a tighter prompt.
acceptanceCriteria: SPIRAL_MAX_DIFF_LINES env var (default 500) sets the maximum allowed changed lines per story
After Phase I implementation, ralph.sh counts total changed lines via `git diff --stat HEAD`
If changed lines exceed SPIRAL_MAX_DIFF_LINES, the story is marked with _failureReason: 'oversized_diff' and the commit is not made
The oversized diff stat (files changed, insertions, deletions) is logged to spiral_events.jsonl
SPIRAL_MAX_DIFF_LINES=0 disables the guard (matches current behaviour)
Unit test verifies the line count extraction from `git diff --stat` output
technicalNotes: Use `git diff --stat | tail -1` to get total insertions+deletions summary line
Parse with awk: extract the numbers from '3 files changed, 450 insertions(+), 120 deletions(-)'
Consider a separate SPIRAL_MAX_DIFF_LINES_WARN threshold that emits a warning without failing
Oversized diffs should also trigger auto-decomposition if SPIRAL_DECOMPOSE_THRESHOLD is set (see related story)

archivedStories.title: Add SPIRAL_GIT_AUTHOR env to tag AI-generated commits with a distinct git identity
archivedStories.description: Commits produced by SPIRAL inherit the machine's default git config identity, making it impossible to distinguish human commits from AI-generated ones in `git log`. Setting SPIRAL_GIT_AUTHOR and SPIRAL_GIT_EMAIL in spiral.config.sh (e.g., 'SPIRAL Agent <spiral@noreply.local>') enables clear attribution, facilitates audit, and allows git blame and tooling to surface which lines were AI-generated.
acceptanceCriteria: SPIRAL_GIT_AUTHOR and SPIRAL_GIT_EMAIL env vars (optional) are read in ralph.sh before git commit
When set, commits use `git -c user.name=... -c user.email=... commit` to avoid modifying global git config
Commit message includes a 'Generated-By: SPIRAL' trailer when SPIRAL_GIT_AUTHOR is set
When unset, behaviour is unchanged (uses machine git config)
spiral.config.sh template includes commented-out examples for the new vars
Unit test verifies the git -c flags are passed correctly in ralph.sh
technicalNotes: Prefer `git -c user.name=... -c user.email=... commit` over GIT_AUTHOR_NAME env var to avoid polluting the child process environment
The 'Generated-By' trailer can be appended with: `git interpret-trailers --trailer 'Generated-By: SPIRAL'`
SPIRAL_VERSION var (pending story) can be included in the trailer: 'Generated-By: SPIRAL/v1.2.3'

archivedStories.title: Add prd.json story count health check: warn when total exceeds SPIRAL_MAX_STORIES
archivedStories.description: As SPIRAL runs Phase M across many iterations, prd.json can accumulate hundreds of stories. Very large PRDs degrade AI context quality (Claude must process the full prd.json on each ralph.sh invocation), slow jq operations, and risk exceeding context window limits. A preflight check that warns when total story count exceeds SPIRAL_MAX_STORIES (default 200) prompts operators to archive passing stories before context quality degrades.
acceptanceCriteria: SPIRAL_MAX_STORIES env var (default 200) sets the story count warning threshold
validate_preflight.sh checks total story count and emits a WARNING when count > SPIRAL_MAX_STORIES
SPIRAL_MAX_STORIES_ABORT env var (default 0/disabled) causes preflight to fail hard when count is exceeded
The warning message includes current count, threshold, and a suggestion to archive passing stories
spiral-doctor command (pending story) also reports story count in its health summary
technicalNotes: Count stories with: `jq '.stories | length' prd.json`
Consider a companion `spiral.sh --archive-passed` flag that moves stories with passes:true to prd.archive.json to reduce active PRD size
The 200 default is based on typical Claude context window capacity for structured JSON (~50K tokens for 200 medium-complexity stories at current model limits)

archivedStories.title: Auto-trigger story decomposition when retry_count reaches SPIRAL_DECOMPOSE_THRESHOLD
archivedStories.description: Story decomposition currently requires manual intervention or is triggered only on specific failure patterns. Stories that repeatedly fail without triggering existing failure analysis are stuck in an infinite retry loop until MAX_RETRIES marks them _skipped. Adding automatic decomposition at SPIRAL_DECOMPOSE_THRESHOLD (default 2) breaks the loop earlier by splitting the story into subtasks before retries are exhausted.
acceptanceCriteria: SPIRAL_DECOMPOSE_THRESHOLD env var (default 2) sets the retry count at which auto-decomposition triggers
In ralph.sh, after incrementing retry_count, check if retry_count >= SPIRAL_DECOMPOSE_THRESHOLD and invoke decompose_story.py
Auto-decomposition is logged to spiral_events.jsonl as an 'auto_decompose' event with parent story ID and generated child IDs
The parent story is marked _skipped: true with _failureReason: 'auto_decomposed' after successful decomposition
SPIRAL_DECOMPOSE_THRESHOLD=0 disables auto-decomposition (current behaviour)
Unit test verifies the threshold trigger path: story at threshold invokes decompose_story.py
technicalNotes: decompose_story.py already exists; this story wires ralph.sh to call it automatically at threshold
Decomposed child stories should inherit the parent's epicId (pending story) for report grouping
Distinguish from _skipped via MAX_RETRIES — auto-decomposed stories should not count against SPIRAL_COST_CEILING since work continues via children

archivedStories.title: Add optional Semgrep/Bandit security scan gate after Phase I implementation
archivedStories.description: Research shows 30-40% of AI-generated code contains security vulnerabilities including SQL injection, path traversal, and weak authentication patterns. Adding an optional Phase S (Security) between Phase I and Phase V, triggered by SPIRAL_SECURITY_SCAN=true, runs Semgrep (or Bandit for Python-only projects) on newly changed files and fails the story on HIGH-severity findings before the test suite runs.
acceptanceCriteria: SPIRAL_SECURITY_SCAN=true env var enables the optional Phase S gate
SPIRAL_SECURITY_SCAN_TOOL env var selects the scanner: 'semgrep' (default) or 'bandit'
Phase S scans only files touched by the current story's commit (not the full codebase)
HIGH-severity findings fail the story with _failureReason: 'security_scan_failure'; MEDIUM findings emit a warning only
Phase S results are written to .spiral/security_scan_{STORY_ID}.json
When the scanner binary is not found, Phase S is skipped with a logged warning (not a failure)
SPIRAL_SECURITY_SCAN_ARGS env var passes additional flags to the scanner
technicalNotes: Semgrep invocation: `semgrep --config=auto --json --output=scan.json $(git diff --name-only HEAD~1)`
Bandit invocation: `bandit -r $(git diff --name-only HEAD~1 | grep '.py$') -f json -o scan.json`
Parse .results[].extra.severity for Semgrep output; .results[].issue_severity for Bandit output
Reference: OpenSSF Security-Focused Guide for AI Code Assistant Instructions; AWS MCP Security Scanner pattern

archivedStories.title: Add story dependency auto-inference from filesTouch overlap in partition_prd.py
archivedStories.description: Story dependencies in prd.json are set manually or left empty, causing the partitioner to assign file-conflicting stories to different workers that later conflict on merge. Scanning filesTouch hints populated by populate_hints.py and detecting pairs that share files allows SPIRAL to suggest (or automatically add) dependency edges, improving partition quality and reducing merge conflicts in parallel worker runs.
acceptanceCriteria: New script lib/infer_dependencies.py reads prd.json and computes file-touch overlap between all pending story pairs
Story pairs sharing >= 50% of one story's filesTouch entries are flagged as strongly dependent
Strong dependencies are written to prd.json dependencies arrays when SPIRAL_AUTO_INFER_DEPS=true
Weak overlaps (> 0 but < 50%) are written to .spiral/_dependency_hints.json without modifying prd.json
infer_dependencies.py is called at the end of Phase M so new stories get hints before partitioning
Auto-inferred dependency edges pass check_dag.py cycle detection before being written
Unit tests cover: empty filesTouch, full overlap, partial overlap, and would-create-cycle scenarios
technicalNotes: Jaccard similarity: |A ∩ B| / |A ∪ B| — threshold 0.5 for strong dependency classification
Stories with no filesTouch history (brand new, no prior commits) cannot be inferred and are skipped
This directly addresses the 'new story areas added after baseline have zero hints' gap in partition_prd.py

archivedStories.title: Add circuit breaker for LLM API calls with half-open recovery
archivedStories.description: Implement a three-state circuit breaker (CLOSED/OPEN/HALF_OPEN) in ralph.sh for LLM API calls. When the failure count exceeds a threshold, the breaker trips to OPEN and blocks further calls for a cooldown period. After the cooldown, it enters HALF_OPEN and allows a single probe call to test recovery before re-closing.
acceptanceCriteria: Circuit breaker state is persisted in .spiral/circuit_breaker.json with fields: state, failure_count, last_failure_ts, cooldown_secs
After 5 consecutive API failures (429/502/503), state transitions to OPEN and no further LLM calls are made for SPIRAL_CB_COOLDOWN_SECS (default 60)
After cooldown, a single probe call is made; success resets to CLOSED, failure restarts cooldown
SPIRAL_CB_FAILURE_THRESHOLD and SPIRAL_CB_COOLDOWN_SECS are documented in spiral.config.example.sh
A bats test simulates 5 failures and verifies state transitions to OPEN, then HALF_OPEN after cooldown
technicalNotes: State file must be written atomically (write-to-tmp then mv) to avoid corruption during concurrent worker reads
Circuit breaker is per-model-endpoint, not global, to allow fallback routing
Distinguish transient errors (5xx, 429) from permanent errors (400, 401) — only transient errors increment failure count
Log all state transitions as circuit_breaker_open / circuit_breaker_closed events to spiral_events.jsonl

archivedStories.title: Add per-phase timeout with two-phase kill to all LLM invocations
archivedStories.description: Wrap every LLM CLI invocation (claude, amp, codex) in ralph.sh and spiral.sh with `timeout --kill-after=30 <phase_limit>` so that a hung API call cannot block a worker indefinitely. Each phase (R, I, V) has a distinct configurable deadline rather than a single global wall-clock limit.
acceptanceCriteria: SPIRAL_RESEARCH_TIMEOUT and SPIRAL_IMPL_TIMEOUT env vars configure per-phase deadlines in seconds (defaults: 300, 600) alongside the existing SPIRAL_VALIDATE_TIMEOUT
Each LLM call is wrapped: `timeout --kill-after=30 "$PHASE_TIMEOUT" <llm_command>`
Exit code 124 from timeout is caught and logged as a phase_timeout event in spiral_events.jsonl with the phase name and story ID
A timed-out phase is treated as a failure (increments retry count) not a hard abort
All three per-phase timeouts (R, I, V) are applied to their respective LLM calls
technicalNotes: Use `timeout --kill-after=30` (SIGTERM first, then SIGKILL after 30s) to allow graceful LLM CLI shutdown
Test on macOS with `gtimeout` (from coreutils) and Linux `timeout`; auto-detect in setup/doctor
Per-phase timeouts must survive the existing retry loop — a timeout retry still respects the backoff delay
Log timeout events with phase, story_id, timeout_secs for post-run analysis

archivedStories.title: Add prd.json JSON Schema file and validation as CI preflight gate
archivedStories.description: Define a JSON Schema for prd.json and validate it before every SPIRAL run and in CI. This catches malformed PRDs (missing required fields, wrong types, invalid priority values) before an LLM wastes API budget on a broken input.
acceptanceCriteria: A schema file prd.schema.json is committed to the repo root defining required story fields: id (string, pattern US-\d+), title (string maxLength 80), priority (enum: critical/high/medium/low), description (string), acceptanceCriteria (array of strings, minItems 1), passes (boolean)
spiral.sh runs `python -m jsonschema -i prd.json prd.schema.json` (or equivalent) as an early preflight step
Validation failure prints a diff-style error listing which story and field failed, then aborts with exit 2
A GitHub Actions workflow step validates prd.json on every PR that modifies prd.json
The --doctor flag checks that python jsonschema is importable and prints install instructions if missing
technicalNotes: Use python jsonschema library rather than adding a new binary
The schema should use additionalProperties: false on story objects to catch typos in field names
Allow extra top-level prd.json fields (productName, goals, etc.) but strictly validate each element of userStories array
Consider a jq-only fallback: `jq -e '[.userStories[] | select(.id == null or .title == null)] | length == 0'`

archivedStories.title: Add per-story token cost accumulation and soft/hard budget enforcement
archivedStories.description: Track cumulative LLM token usage and estimated cost per story by parsing Claude CLI usage output. Emit a cost_update event to spiral_events.jsonl after each LLM call. Enforce a per-story soft limit (warn) and hard limit (skip story) using SPIRAL_STORY_COST_WARN_USD and SPIRAL_STORY_COST_HARD_USD.
acceptanceCriteria: ralph.sh parses token counts from LLM CLI JSON output after each call and accumulates them in .spiral/story_costs.json keyed by story_id
A cost_update JSONL event is emitted after each LLM call with fields: story_id, tokens_input, tokens_output, estimated_usd
When cumulative story cost exceeds SPIRAL_STORY_COST_WARN_USD (default: $0.50), a warning is printed but execution continues
When cumulative story cost exceeds SPIRAL_STORY_COST_HARD_USD (default: $2.00), the story is abandoned with _failureReason: story_cost_ceiling
The --status flag shows total run cost accumulated across all stories from story_costs.json
technicalNotes: This is per-story cost, complementing the existing SPIRAL_COST_CEILING which is a session-level hard stop
Model pricing constants (input $/1M tokens, output $/1M tokens) should be defined in spiral.config.example.sh and overridable
story_costs.json must be written atomically to survive worker crashes
If the LLM CLI does not emit token counts, log tokens_input: null and skip cost estimation rather than blocking

archivedStories.title: Add model fallback chain with per-model circuit breaker state
archivedStories.description: When the primary LLM provider's circuit breaker is OPEN, automatically rotate to a secondary model from a configured fallback chain before giving up on a story. Each model in the chain maintains its own circuit breaker state so a fully degraded provider does not contaminate fallbacks.
acceptanceCriteria: SPIRAL_MODEL_FALLBACK_CHAIN env var accepts a colon-separated list of model identifiers (e.g., `claude-sonnet-4-5:claude-haiku-3-5:gemini-2.0-flash`)
ralph.sh attempts each model in the chain in order; a model is skipped if its circuit breaker is OPEN
If all models in the chain are OPEN, the story is deferred with _failureReason: all_models_unavailable and the next story is attempted
Each fallback attempt emits a model_fallback event to spiral_events.jsonl with primary model, fallback model, and reason
A bats test mocks all models as OPEN and verifies the story receives _failureReason: all_models_unavailable without infinite looping
technicalNotes: Depends on the circuit breaker implementation (story: Add circuit breaker for LLM API calls with half-open recovery)
Model IDs must map to the correct --model flag for each CLI tool (claude: claude-sonnet-4-5, amp: same, codex: gpt-4o)
Cost tracking must account for per-model pricing when a fallback is used
The fallback chain applies at the story-attempt level — a story started on sonnet completes on sonnet even if haiku is cheaper

archivedStories.title: Enforce shfmt formatting on all spiral bash scripts in CI
archivedStories.description: Add shfmt-based formatting checks for all .sh files in the SPIRAL repository. This enforces consistent style (2-space indentation, Google shell style) across spiral.sh, ralph.sh, and all lib/ helpers. A CI step and optional pre-commit hook block merges if any script is not properly formatted.
acceptanceCriteria: Running `shfmt -d -i 2 -ci spiral.sh ralph/ralph.sh lib/*.sh` exits 0 when all files are correctly formatted
GitHub Actions workflow step shfmt-check runs on every PR and fails if formatting diff is non-empty
A pre-commit hook config entry (.pre-commit-config.yaml) is added using mvdan/sh shfmt hook
setup.sh includes a check that shfmt is installed and prints install instructions if missing
All existing .sh files are formatted to pass the check before this story is marked complete
technicalNotes: Use shfmt -i 2 -ci (2-space indent, case-indent) matching Google Shell Style Guide
shfmt can be installed via `brew install shfmt`, `go install mvdan.cc/sh/v3/cmd/shfmt@latest`, or downloaded as a binary
Add shfmt to the --doctor dependency check in spiral_doctor.sh
Do not apply shfmt to vendored or generated files

archivedStories.title: Inject trace_id and span_id into every spiral_events.jsonl entry
archivedStories.description: Correlate all JSONL log entries with the active OpenTelemetry trace by injecting trace_id and span_id fields derived from the W3C traceparent environment variable. This allows a log aggregator to join spiral_events.jsonl lines with OTLP trace spans without a separate log-trace correlation service.
acceptanceCriteria: log_ralph_event() extracts trace_id and span_id from TRACEPARENT env var (format: 00-<trace_id>-<span_id>-<flags>) if set
All emitted JSONL lines include `"trace_id":"<32hex>"` and `"span_id":"<16hex>"` fields when TRACEPARENT is set
When TRACEPARENT is not set, the fields are omitted (no null values)
A bats test sets TRACEPARENT=00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01 and verifies the extracted fields in the emitted log line
SPIRAL_RUN_ID is also verified to appear in every log line as `"run_id"` (completeness check)
technicalNotes: Parse traceparent with bash parameter expansion: trace_id=${TRACEPARENT:3:32}, span_id=${TRACEPARENT:36:16}
This extends the existing W3C traceparent propagation story by ensuring the IDs flow into JSONL lines, not just outbound env vars
The correlation enables `jq 'select(.trace_id=="<id>")' spiral_events.jsonl` to reconstruct a full story timeline from logs

archivedStories.title: Harden GitHub Actions workflow with SHA-pinned actions and least-privilege permissions
archivedStories.description: Harden the SPIRAL CI workflow for self-hosted runners by pinning all action versions to full SHA digests, adding step-security/harden-runner for egress auditing, and using minimal job-level permissions. This prevents supply-chain attacks via compromised upstream actions.
acceptanceCriteria: All GitHub Actions workflow steps using external actions are pinned to a full SHA commit digest (e.g., `actions/checkout@<sha>`)
step-security/harden-runner@<sha> is added as the first step in all jobs with `egress-policy: audit`
All jobs declare `permissions: contents: read` at the job level and only elevate permissions where explicitly required
No workflow uses `pull_request_target` with untrusted code checkout (documented as forbidden in workflow comments)
A comment documents that `egress-policy: block` should be enabled after an audit period
technicalNotes: SHA-pinning prevents a compromised upstream action from injecting malicious code — use Dependabot to keep SHAs current
Recommend ephemeral self-hosted runners (--ephemeral flag) over persistent runners in .github/SECURITY.md
OIDC-based credentials (role-to-assume) eliminate the need for stored long-lived secrets
Document in .github/SECURITY.md that self-hosted runners should only be used for private repos

archivedStories.title: Add named exit code constants to spiral.sh for programmatic error handling
archivedStories.description: Replace ad-hoc exit 1 calls in spiral.sh with named, documented exit code constants. Define readonly constants at the top of the script so that CI pipelines and the SPIRAL_ON_COMPLETE hook can distinguish between failure modes programmatically.
acceptanceCriteria: At least 8 named exit code constants are defined as `readonly ERR_<NAME>=N` at the top of spiral.sh, with N in range 2-125
All bare `exit 1` calls in spiral.sh are replaced with `exit $ERR_<RELEVANT_CODE>`
A reference table of exit codes and their meanings is maintained in a comment block near the constants
The spiral_doctor.sh --help output lists the exit code table
A bats test verifies that triggering each distinct error condition produces the documented exit code
technicalNotes: Reserve exit code 0 for full success, 1 for unclassified errors (never intentionally used), 2 for misuse (wrong args)
Exit codes 3-125 are safe for scripts; 126/127 are reserved by the shell; 128+ indicate signal deaths
Consistent exit codes allow `$?` checks in the SPIRAL_ON_COMPLETE hook to trigger different downstream actions

archivedStories.title: Use pnpm global virtual store for node_modules deduplication across worktrees
archivedStories.description: When pnpm is detected as the package manager, configure new worktrees to share pnpm's global virtual store rather than copying node_modules. This reduces per-worktree disk usage by 50-80% for Node.js projects with large dependency trees.
acceptanceCriteria: run_parallel_ralph.sh detects pnpm by checking `command -v pnpm` before creating worktrees
When pnpm is available, each worktree is initialised with `cd <worktree> && pnpm install --prefer-offline` instead of copying node_modules
A pnpm-workspace.yaml symlink or copy is created in each worktree if it exists in the repo root
A SPIRAL_SKIP_PNPM_DEDUP=1 env var disables this behaviour as an escape hatch
If pnpm install fails in a worktree, fall back to copying node_modules from the main worktree with a warning
technicalNotes: pnpm's global virtual store location is `pnpm store path`; symlinks from node_modules/.pnpm point into this store
Only activate this for worktrees created during parallel runs; single-worker runs are unaffected
This does NOT require sparse-checkout — it only changes how node_modules are populated

archivedStories.title: Stream-process large prd.json with jq --stream to avoid full in-memory parse
archivedStories.description: For prd.json files exceeding SPIRAL_PRD_STREAM_THRESHOLD_KB (default: 512KB), use `jq --stream` to extract pending story IDs without loading the entire document into memory. This supports PRDs with hundreds of stories or large embedded specs without hitting jq's memory limits.
acceptanceCriteria: A helper function get_pending_story_ids() in ralph.sh detects prd.json file size and switches to `jq --stream` when it exceeds SPIRAL_PRD_STREAM_THRESHOLD_KB
The streaming version produces identical output to the non-streaming version on the same input (verified by a bats test with a 1000-story synthetic prd.json)
SPIRAL_PRD_STREAM_THRESHOLD_KB is documented in spiral.config.example.sh
The non-streaming path (small files) is unchanged and no performance regression is introduced for typical prd.json files
A bats test exercises both code paths and compares their output
technicalNotes: jq --stream emits [path, value] pairs; use `tostream` / `fromstream` patterns to reconstruct objects
Streaming is only needed for the story selection query, not for the passes=true update (which uses atomic write-and-replace already)
jq 1.6+ is required for --stream support — document minimum jq version in spiral_doctor.sh

archivedStories.title: Add shellcheck static analysis gate to CI for all bash scripts
archivedStories.description: ShellCheck detects semantic errors in bash scripts (unquoted variables, incorrect conditionals, subshell bugs) that shfmt cannot — shfmt only enforces formatting. Without ShellCheck, subtle runtime bugs in spiral.sh, ralph.sh, and lib/ scripts slip through. CI must enforce zero ShellCheck violations at severity=error.
acceptanceCriteria: CI runs `shellcheck --severity=error` over all `.sh` files in the repo and fails on any violation
ShellCheck version is pinned in a requirements/CI config file to prevent surprise failures from upstream changes
A pre-commit hook stage runs shellcheck on modified `.sh` files before commit
`spiral-doctor` verifies shellcheck is installed and reports its version
technicalNotes: ShellCheck is distinct from shfmt — shfmt is style/formatting, shellcheck is semantic correctness
Use `koalaman/shellcheck-action` GitHub Action with explicit `version:` pin (e.g., v0.10.0)
Output format: `--format=gcc` for GitHub Actions annotation integration
Pair with pre-commit hook using `repo: https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck-precommit`

archivedStories.title: Add mypy strict type checking enforcement to Python CI pipeline
archivedStories.description: SPIRAL's Python scripts (spiral_dashboard.py, route_stories.py, check_done.py, etc.) currently lack static type checking enforcement in CI. mypy in strict mode catches type errors, missing annotations, and incorrect return types before runtime. This prevents a class of production bugs and makes refactoring safer.
acceptanceCriteria: CI runs `mypy --strict` over all Python source files and fails on any type error
mypy version is pinned in `pyproject.toml` under `[tool.mypy]`
A `pyproject.toml` section configures mypy with `python_version`, `strict = true`, and per-module overrides for gradual adoption
CI job reports mypy output as annotations on PRs using `--output json` piped to a formatter
technicalNotes: Use `dmypy` daemon for faster incremental checks during local development
For gradual adoption start with `check_untyped_defs = true` then escalate to `disallow_untyped_defs = true`
Pin version: `mypy==1.11` in dev dependencies to avoid CI flakiness on upstream releases
Reference: https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/existing_code.html for phased rollout strategy

archivedStories.title: Generate CHANGELOG.md automatically using git-cliff on tagged releases
archivedStories.description: SPIRAL commits follow conventional-commit style but has no automated CHANGELOG generation. git-cliff parses commit history using a regex-based config, groups by type (feat, fix, refactor), and outputs a formatted CHANGELOG.md. This makes releases traceable and documents what changed between iterations without manual effort.
acceptanceCriteria: `cliff.toml` config exists at repo root specifying commit parsing patterns and CHANGELOG template
Running `git-cliff --output CHANGELOG.md` from repo root produces a valid, correctly grouped CHANGELOG
A `make changelog` or `./spiral.sh --changelog` target generates the CHANGELOG for the current HEAD
CI validates that `CHANGELOG.md` is updated on release tags via git-cliff --unreleased check
CHANGELOG groups entries by: feat, fix, perf, refactor, docs, test, ci
technicalNotes: Use git-cliff (Rust binary, zero Node.js dependency): https://git-cliff.org/
Config: `cliff.toml` with `[git] conventional_commits = true` and `[changelog] header/body/footer` templates
Install via `cargo install git-cliff` or download binary from GitHub releases
GitHub Actions: add `git-cliff-action` step on `push: tags: ['v*']` to auto-update CHANGELOG and commit

archivedStories.title: Add pytest code coverage reporting with configurable fail-under threshold
archivedStories.description: SPIRAL's Python unit tests run in CI but have no coverage measurement or enforcement gate. Without a fail-under threshold, coverage can silently regress. pytest-cov generates HTML/XML/terminal reports and enforces a minimum coverage percentage, ensuring new code is tested before merging.
acceptanceCriteria: CI runs `pytest --cov=spiral --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml --cov-report=html:htmlcov --cov-fail-under=80`
HTML coverage report is uploaded as a GitHub Actions artifact on each CI run
Coverage summary is appended to GitHub Actions step summary via `--cov-report markdown-append:$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`
Coverage threshold is stored in `pyproject.toml` under `[tool.coverage.report] fail_under = 80`
CI fails if overall coverage drops below the configured threshold
technicalNotes: Install: `uv add --dev pytest-cov coverage[toml]`
pyproject.toml config: `[tool.coverage.run] source = ["spiral"]` and `[tool.coverage.report] show_missing = true`
For trend tracking upload `coverage.xml` to Codecov: `codecov/codecov-action@v4`
Reference: https://pytest-cov.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reporting.html

archivedStories.title: Add stale story detection flagging stories inactive beyond SPIRAL_STALE_DAYS
archivedStories.description: Stories that remain in `todo` or `in_progress` status for extended periods without retry attempts become stale and indicate blocked or forgotten work. A configurable staleness detector warns operators and optionally iceboxes stories beyond a threshold, keeping the active backlog honest and actionable.
acceptanceCriteria: SPIRAL_STALE_DAYS env var (default: 7) controls the staleness threshold for active runs
At loop startup SPIRAL logs a warning for each story where `last_attempted` timestamp exceeds SPIRAL_STALE_DAYS
The spiral_dashboard.py overview section highlights stale stories with a distinct visual indicator
A `--stale-report` flag to spiral.sh prints all stale stories with their ages and last attempt timestamps
Stale stories are included in spiral_events.jsonl with event type `story_stale_detected`
technicalNotes: Add `last_attempted` ISO 8601 timestamp field to each prd.json story when ralph.sh begins working on it
Python: `datetime.fromisoformat(story['last_attempted'])` compared to `datetime.now() - timedelta(days=SPIRAL_STALE_DAYS)`
Dashboard: use CSS class `stale-story` with red/orange badge in the story table
Reference: https://resources.scrumalliance.org/Article/scrum-stale for threshold guidance

archivedStories.title: Add SPIRAL_LOG_LEVEL env var for configurable output verbosity
archivedStories.description: spiral.sh currently emits all diagnostic output regardless of context. In production unattended runs, verbose debug output creates noise and obscures real errors. SPIRAL_LOG_LEVEL (DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR) allows operators to control verbosity: DEBUG for development, WARN/ERROR for CI, reducing log volume and improving signal-to-noise ratio.
acceptanceCriteria: SPIRAL_LOG_LEVEL accepts values: DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR (case-insensitive, default: INFO)
All spiral.sh output is routed through a `log_msg LEVEL message` shell function that filters by SPIRAL_LOG_LEVEL
DEBUG messages include function name and line number context for traceability
SPIRAL_LOG_LEVEL is recorded in .spiral/_checkpoint.json for debugging reproducibility on resume
spiral_events.jsonl entries include a `level` field matching the SPIRAL_LOG_LEVEL scale
technicalNotes: Shell log function pattern: `log_msg() { local lvl=$1; shift; [[ ${LOG_LEVELS[$lvl]} -ge ${LOG_LEVELS[$SPIRAL_LOG_LEVEL]} ]] && echo "[$lvl] $*" >&2; }`
Use associative array for level ordering: `declare -A LOG_LEVELS=([DEBUG]=0 [INFO]=1 [WARN]=2 [ERROR]=3)`
Requires bash 4.0+ for associative arrays (already assumed by existing spiral.sh)
Structured log entries: `{ "ts": "...", "level": "INFO", "msg": "...", "phase": "I" }`

archivedStories.title: Run Phase V validation only on files touched by current story (incremental validation)
archivedStories.description: Phase V currently runs the full SPIRAL_VALIDATE_CMD test suite on every story attempt, even when the story only modifies 2-3 files. Incremental validation runs only the tests covering changed files (via pytest --testpaths or vitest --related), reducing Phase V time by 60-90% for large projects and making the loop significantly faster.
acceptanceCriteria: ralph.sh reads the `filesTouch` field from prd.json for the current story to determine changed files
When SPIRAL_INCREMENTAL_VALIDATE=true ralph.sh constructs a targeted test command covering only those files
For pytest projects: tests are filtered to modules derived from filesTouch entries
For vitest projects: `vitest run --related <filesTouch entries>` is used
SPIRAL_INCREMENTAL_VALIDATE defaults to false to preserve existing behavior; full suite still runs at the final iteration gate
technicalNotes: Differential analysis: feed `git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD` and filesTouch to determine scope
Pytest path mapping: `src/foo/bar.py` to test file `tests/test_bar.py` via configurable `SPIRAL_TEST_PREFIX`
Vitest `--related` flag natively handles this: `vitest run --related src/foo/bar.ts`
Reference: https://sdtimes.com/devops/demystifying-differential-and-incremental-analysis-for-static-code-analysis-within-devops/

archivedStories.title: Add SPIRAL_PRE_PHASE_HOOK and SPIRAL_POST_PHASE_HOOK for user-defined phase scripts
archivedStories.description: Different projects need custom actions at specific SPIRAL phases — e.g., seeding a test database before Phase V, or posting a Slack notification after Phase I. Generic pre/post phase hooks (env vars pointing to executable scripts) enable this without modifying spiral.sh itself, following the Unix composability philosophy.
acceptanceCriteria: SPIRAL_PRE_PHASE_HOOK and SPIRAL_POST_PHASE_HOOK accept a path to an executable script
The hook script receives SPIRAL_CURRENT_PHASE (I/R/M/V/G) and SPIRAL_CURRENT_STORY_ID as env vars
spiral.sh sources the hook before/after each phase transition and captures its exit code
A non-zero exit code from a pre-phase hook aborts the current story attempt and records the failure reason
Hook execution is logged to spiral_events.jsonl with event type `phase_hook_pre` / `phase_hook_post` and duration
technicalNotes: Pattern: `if [[ -x "${SPIRAL_PRE_PHASE_HOOK:-}" ]]; then "$SPIRAL_PRE_PHASE_HOOK" || handle_hook_failure; fi`
Pass story context via env: `SPIRAL_CURRENT_PHASE SPIRAL_CURRENT_STORY_ID SPIRAL_RUN_ID SPIRAL_ITERATION`
Timeout hook execution with `timeout ${SPIRAL_HOOK_TIMEOUT:-30}` to prevent hooks from stalling the loop
Document hook contract in SPIRAL README: expected env vars, exit code semantics, and example scripts

archivedStories.title: Add SPIRAL_WORKSPACE_CLEANUP to auto-prune transient artifacts on successful run completion
archivedStories.description: Completed SPIRAL runs accumulate research cache files, intermediate JSON files, old iteration summaries, and stale log entries in `.spiral/`. Without cleanup, these consume disk space over many runs. SPIRAL_WORKSPACE_CLEANUP=true triggers a post-completion sweep that archives completed run artifacts and removes transient files.
acceptanceCriteria: SPIRAL_WORKSPACE_CLEANUP env var (default: false) enables post-run cleanup
When enabled cleanup runs only after 100% of stories reach `passed` or `skipped` status
Cleanup removes: `.spiral/research_cache/` entries older than SPIRAL_CACHE_TTL, iteration summary JSONs older than 5 iterations, and zero-byte log files
Cleanup preserves: `prd.json`, `spiral_events.jsonl`, `_checkpoint.json`, and `results.tsv`
Cleanup actions are logged to spiral_events.jsonl with event type `workspace_cleanup` and bytes_freed metric
technicalNotes: Implement as a `cleanup_workspace()` bash function called at the end of spiral.sh main loop
Use `find .spiral/research_cache -mtime +${SPIRAL_CACHE_TTL:-7} -delete` for expired cache entries
Archive old iteration summaries: `tar -czf .spiral/archive/iter_summaries_$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz .spiral/_iteration_summary_*.json`
Report bytes freed: `du -sb .spiral/` before and after and emit delta to spiral_events.jsonl

archivedStories.title: Create annotated git tag on successful SPIRAL run completion with run metadata
archivedStories.description: When all stories in a SPIRAL run pass, the resulting codebase state has no persistent git marker. Creating an annotated git tag (e.g., `spiral/run-42-complete`) with run metadata (stories completed, iteration count, duration) makes it trivially easy to identify and checkout the state produced by any completed SPIRAL run.
acceptanceCriteria: When all stories reach `passed` status spiral.sh creates an annotated git tag `spiral/run-{SPIRAL_RUN_ID}-complete`
The tag annotation includes: total stories completed, iterations taken, wall-clock duration, and final commit SHA
Tag creation is conditional on SPIRAL_CREATE_TAGS=true (default: false) to avoid cluttering repos
Tag creation is logged to spiral_events.jsonl with event type `run_complete_tagged`
If the tag already exists it is updated with --force only when SPIRAL_CREATE_TAGS=true
technicalNotes: Shell: `git tag -a "spiral/run-${SPIRAL_RUN_ID}-complete" -m "SPIRAL run complete: ${story_count} stories in ${iteration_count} iterations"`
Include ISO 8601 timestamp in tag annotation for traceability
Push tag if SPIRAL_AUTO_PUSH_TAGS=true: `git push origin "spiral/run-${SPIRAL_RUN_ID}-complete"`
Reference: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-tag for annotated tag format

archivedStories.title: Pinchtab Phase V E2E browser assertions integration
archivedStories.description: Add SPIRAL_PINCHTAB_URL config var and pinchtab E2E block to Phase V of spiral.sh. When set, Phase V calls pinchtab CLI after pytest to navigate to SPIRAL_DEV_URL and extract page text as a lightweight browser assertion. Text mode costs ~800 tokens vs ~10,000 for a screenshot. A custom SPIRAL_PINCHTAB_E2E_CMD override supports login flows and multi-step assertions.
acceptanceCriteria: SPIRAL_PINCHTAB_URL is documented in spiral.config.sh (commented out) and templates/spiral.config.example.sh
When SPIRAL_PINCHTAB_URL is unset, Phase V behaves exactly as before (no regression)
When SPIRAL_PINCHTAB_URL and SPIRAL_DEV_URL are set and pinchtab CLI is present, Phase V runs nav + text steps and prints first 20 lines of page text
When SPIRAL_PINCHTAB_E2E_CMD is set, Phase V runs that command instead of the default nav+text steps
A pinchtab failure prints a WARNING but does not change the Phase V validation result (VALIDATE_EXIT is unchanged)
uv run pytest passes
technicalNotes: Pinchtab block goes in spiral.sh after the Chrome DevTools screenshot block (before write_checkpoint V)
Use: pinchtab --server "$SPIRAL_PINCHTAB_URL" nav / text
Guard with: command -v pinchtab to print a helpful install hint if missing
ralph/CLAUDE.md already updated: clarifies Chrome DevTools MCP is for Phase I inline checks; pinchtab is Phase V only
Do NOT start/stop pinchtab server from spiral.sh — user manages the server lifecycle externally

archivedStories.title: Enable Anthropic prompt caching for ralph.sh system prompts
archivedStories.description: Use Anthropic's prompt caching beta (cache_control breakpoints) to cache the large system prompt sent to Claude on every ralph.sh invocation. Cache hits reduce input token cost by 90% and latency by 85%, compounding significantly across hundreds of story attempts per run.
acceptanceCriteria: ralph.sh adds cache_control: {type: ephemeral} breakpoint after the system prompt in API payloads
cache_creation_input_tokens and cache_read_input_tokens fields are extracted from API responses and appended to the structured log
results.tsv gains cache_hit (boolean) and cache_read_tokens columns
Integration test verifies that on second invocation with identical system prompt, cache_read_input_tokens > 0
technicalNotes: Requires X-Anthropic-Beta: prompt-caching-2024-07-31 header on API requests
Cache TTL is 5 minutes for ephemeral; keyed on exact prefix byte sequence
Minimum cacheable block is 1024 tokens; system prompts in ralph.sh comfortably exceed this
Official docs: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching

archivedStories.title: Add gitleaks secret scanning gate before AI-generated code is committed
archivedStories.description: Run gitleaks detect on the staged diff before committing AI-generated code to prevent accidentally committing API keys, tokens, or credentials that an LLM might hallucinate into implementation files. This is a critical security gate unique to AI-assisted development workflows.
acceptanceCriteria: ralph.sh runs `gitleaks detect --staged --report-format json` before git commit in Phase I
If gitleaks finds any findings, the commit is aborted and the story is marked _failureReason: 'secret_detected'
SPIRAL_SKIP_SECRET_SCAN=true bypasses the gate with a structured warning log entry
spiral-doctor verifies gitleaks binary is present and reports its version
technicalNotes: gitleaks GitHub: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks
Command: gitleaks detect --source . --staged --report-format json --report-path .spiral/gitleaks-report.json
Allow-list spiral's own config variable names via .gitleaks.toml to prevent false positives
Alternative: trufflehog OSS (https://github.com/trufflesecurity/trufflehog)

archivedStories.title: Truncate story context to fit Claude context window using token counting
archivedStories.description: Before sending a story implementation request to Claude, measure the assembled prompt token count using the Anthropic token-counting API (or tiktoken approximation). If the count exceeds a configurable threshold (default: 180,000 tokens), truncate the least-relevant context sections to fit. Prevents silent context truncation by the API that causes incomplete implementations.
acceptanceCriteria: ralph.sh calls lib/truncate_context.py to measure token count before every API call
Truncation priority: drop _researchOutput first, then hints, then filesTouch context; never drop story spec
When truncation occurs, a structured warning is emitted with original_tokens and truncated_tokens fields
SPIRAL_CONTEXT_LIMIT env var overrides the default 180000 token threshold
Unit tests cover: truncation ordering, edge case where story spec alone exceeds limit, no-op when under threshold
technicalNotes: Anthropic token-counting endpoint: POST /v1/messages/count_tokens (beta, no charge)
tiktoken cl100k_base is a reasonable local approximation: https://github.com/openai/tiktoken
Official token counting docs: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/token-counting
Cache token counts per (story_id, attempt) to avoid redundant API calls on retries

archivedStories.title: Add `spiral.sh --rollback STORY_ID` to revert a passed story's commit
archivedStories.description: Provide a one-command way to revert the git commit(s) associated with a specific passed story, resetting its prd.json status back to pending. This complements the existing --replay flag and closes the full undo/redo cycle for story implementations.
acceptanceCriteria: `spiral.sh --rollback US-042` reads _passedCommit SHA from prd.json and runs `git revert --no-edit <sha>`
prd.json story status resets to pending; _passedCommit, _passedAt, and _adrPath fields are cleared
If _passedCommit is absent, print actionable error message and exit 1
Rollback is rejected with an error if there are uncommitted working-tree changes
Unit test covers: successful rollback, missing _passedCommit error, dirty working-tree guard
technicalNotes: `git revert --no-edit <sha>` creates a new revert commit without opening an editor
Prefer revert over reset --hard to preserve linear history and auditability
Pair with --replay to form a full redo cycle: rollback then replay
git revert docs: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-revert

archivedStories.title: Create GitHub PR per passed story when SPIRAL_CREATE_PRS=true
archivedStories.description: After a story passes validation, optionally push the story commit to a feature branch and open a GitHub Pull Request using the gh CLI. Enables human review of AI-generated code before it reaches main, supporting team workflows where all changes go through PR review.
acceptanceCriteria: When SPIRAL_CREATE_PRS=true, ralph.sh pushes story commit to branch `spiral/<STORY_ID>` and calls `gh pr create`
PR title matches the story title; PR body includes story description, acceptanceCriteria, and SPIRAL_RUN_ID
PR URL is stored in prd.json as _prUrl field on the story
If gh CLI is not authenticated, emit actionable error and skip PR creation without failing the story
SPIRAL_PR_BASE_BRANCH env var sets target base branch (default: main)
technicalNotes: GitHub CLI pr create docs: https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_create
Command: gh pr create --base main --head spiral/US-042 --title '...' --body '...' --label 'spiral-ai'
Auto-create 'spiral-ai' label if it does not exist via `gh label create`
SPIRAL_PR_DRAFT=true creates draft PRs to prevent auto-merge triggers

archivedStories.title: Add Ollama local LLM fallback when Claude API is unreachable
archivedStories.description: Configure a fallback LLM provider (Ollama with qwen2.5-coder or codellama) that activates when Claude API returns repeated connection errors or 529 overload responses. Improves offline resilience and reduces hard dependency on a single API provider during extended outages.
acceptanceCriteria: SPIRAL_OLLAMA_FALLBACK_MODEL env var specifies Ollama model name (e.g., qwen2.5-coder:32b)
After 3 consecutive Claude API connection failures (curl exit 7 or 28), ralph.sh switches to Ollama for the current story
Ollama requests use the OpenAI-compatible endpoint at SPIRAL_OLLAMA_HOST (default: http://localhost:11434/v1)
Stories implemented via Ollama are tagged _model: 'ollama/<model>' in prd.json
spiral-doctor checks Ollama reachability when SPIRAL_OLLAMA_FALLBACK_MODEL is configured
technicalNotes: Ollama OpenAI-compatible API docs: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/openai.md
Endpoint: POST http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions with standard OpenAI payload format
Recommended coding models: qwen2.5-coder:32b, codellama:34b, deepseek-coder-v2:16b
curl exit code 7 = connection refused; exit code 28 = timeout; both indicate API unreachable

archivedStories.title: Add LLM self-review gate (Phase I.5) between implementation and validation
archivedStories.description: After Phase I (implement) and before Phase V (validate), send the generated diff to Claude with a structured code-review prompt asking it to identify bugs, security issues, and spec deviations. If the self-review flags critical issues, re-enter Phase I with the issue list as additional context, reducing first-attempt test failures.
acceptanceCriteria: New Phase I.5 (REVIEW) sends story spec + git diff to Claude with a JSON-mode review prompt
Review response schema: {issues: [{severity: critical|major|minor, location: string, description: string}]}
If any issue has severity='critical', Phase I is re-entered with the issue list injected into the implementation prompt
SPIRAL_SKIP_SELF_REVIEW=true disables Phase I.5; review is also skipped on retries beyond SPIRAL_MAX_RETRIES/2
review_tokens column is added to results.tsv to track self-review cost
technicalNotes: Use haiku model for self-review to minimise cost; escalate to sonnet only on complex diffs
Limit git diff to 500 lines to prevent context overflow in the review step
Review system prompt should be a cacheable constant using prompt caching
Anthropic JSON mode reference: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/increase-consistency

archivedStories.title: Generate Conventional Commit message from story metadata in ralph.sh
archivedStories.description: Replace the current freeform commit message with a Conventional Commits-compliant message derived from story metadata: type from story tags, scope from the primary filesTouch path, and subject from the story title. Enables automated CHANGELOG generation and semantic versioning tools to parse SPIRAL commit history.
acceptanceCriteria: Commit message format: `<type>(<scope>): <story title>` with Story and SPIRAL-Run trailers in the footer
Type is derived from story tags field (feat, fix, chore, refactor, test, docs); defaults to feat when absent
Scope is the top-level directory of the first filesTouch entry (e.g., lib, ralph, spiral)
Footer lines: `Story: <STORY_ID>` and `SPIRAL-Run: <SPIRAL_RUN_ID>`
Unit test verifies correct message format for stories with tags, without tags, and with no filesTouch entries
technicalNotes: Conventional Commits v1.0 spec: https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/
Git trailer format: key-colon-space-value lines after a blank line in the commit body
git-cliff uses these trailers for automatic CHANGELOG generation
Validate with: echo '<message>' | npx commitlint in CI

archivedStories.title: Add pre-flight API cost projection before spiral.sh loop start
archivedStories.description: Before starting a SPIRAL run, estimate the total API cost of implementing all pending stories using historical results.tsv token data and current model pricing. Display a cost projection table and prompt for confirmation when the projected cost exceeds SPIRAL_COST_WARN_THRESHOLD. Prevents surprise bills on large PRD files.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.sh prints a cost projection table (model tier, story count, estimated tokens, estimated USD) before entering the main loop
Projection uses mean tokens-per-story from recent results.tsv rows; falls back to SPIRAL_DEFAULT_TOKENS_PER_STORY (default: 8000) when insufficient history
When projected cost > SPIRAL_COST_WARN_THRESHOLD (default: $5.00), prompts `Estimated cost: $X.XX — Continue? [y/N]`
--yes flag skips the confirmation prompt for non-interactive CI environments
Projection is skipped when results.tsv has fewer than 5 data rows
technicalNotes: Claude model pricing page: https://www.anthropic.com/pricing
haiku-4-5: ~$0.80/MTok input; sonnet-4-6: ~$3.00/MTok input; opus-4-6: ~$15.00/MTok input
Implement projection in lib/cost_project.py; expose via main.py estimate subcommand
Show confidence range: projection ± 1 std deviation from results.tsv sample

archivedStories.title: Parallelize Phase V test execution with pytest-xdist or parallel bats
archivedStories.description: When SPIRAL_PARALLEL_TESTS=true, run the Phase V test suite in parallel across available CPU cores using pytest-xdist (Python) or GNU parallel (bats). Reduces Phase V wall-clock time on large test suites, directly improving story throughput on multi-core workers.
acceptanceCriteria: SPIRAL_PARALLEL_TESTS=true activates parallel test execution
SPIRAL_TEST_WORKERS controls parallelism level (default: nproc/2, minimum 1)
For pytest suites, SPIRAL_VALIDATE_CMD automatically gains `-n $SPIRAL_TEST_WORKERS` when xdist is installed
For bats suites, SPIRAL_VALIDATE_CMD gains `--jobs $SPIRAL_TEST_WORKERS` when GNU parallel is available
spiral-doctor reports whether pytest-xdist and GNU parallel are installed
technicalNotes: pytest-xdist docs: https://pytest-xdist.readthedocs.io/en/stable/
bats parallel support: https://bats-core.readthedocs.io/en/stable/parallel-support.html
Detect xdist: `python -c 'import xdist; print(xdist.__version__)'`
Detect GNU parallel: `command -v parallel && parallel --version`
Warn when SPIRAL_PARALLEL_TESTS=true but tests use shared file-system state

archivedStories.title: Emit SARIF 2.1.0 report from static analysis gates for GitHub Code Scanning
archivedStories.description: Output static analysis results (shellcheck, semgrep, pylint) in SARIF 2.1.0 format and upload to GitHub Advanced Security Code Scanning. Provides inline PR annotations for security and quality findings without requiring a separate plugin installation.
acceptanceCriteria: CI workflow runs `semgrep --sarif --output semgrep.sarif` and uploads via github/codeql-action/upload-sarif
shellcheck output is converted to SARIF using the shellcheck-sarif converter tool
SARIF files are also uploaded as GitHub Actions artifacts for offline inspection
Upload step uses `continue-on-error: true` so SARIF findings do not fail the build
SARIF output passes schema validation against https://json.schemastore.org/sarif-2.1.0.json
technicalNotes: SARIF 2.1.0 spec: https://docs.oasis-open.org/sarif/sarif/v2.1.0/sarif-v2.1.0.html
GitHub upload-sarif action: https://github.com/github/codeql-action/tree/main/upload-sarif
shellcheck-sarif converter: https://github.com/rust-phile/shellcheck-sarif (cargo install shellcheck-sarif)
Semgrep SARIF: `semgrep scan --sarif --output results.sarif`

archivedStories.title: Guard against story scope creep: warn when implementation touches > N files
archivedStories.description: After Phase I commits the story implementation, count the number of files modified. If the count exceeds SPIRAL_MAX_FILES_PER_STORY (default: 10), emit a structured scope-creep warning. Scope creep is a leading indicator that a story should be decomposed and correlates with higher first-attempt failure rates.
acceptanceCriteria: ralph.sh counts modified files via `git diff --name-only HEAD~1 | wc -l` after Phase I commit
When count exceeds SPIRAL_MAX_FILES_PER_STORY, a scope_creep event is emitted to spiral_events.jsonl with the file list
SPIRAL_SCOPE_CREEP_ACTION=abort marks story _failureReason: 'scope_creep' and triggers retry with decomposition hint
SPIRAL_SCOPE_CREEP_ACTION=warn (default) logs the warning but continues to Phase V
spiral_dashboard.py highlights stories that triggered scope-creep warnings in the story table
technicalNotes: Exclude lock files and generated files from the count via a configurable .spiralignore pattern list
Example exclusions: *.lock, *_generated.*, *pb.go
Combine with auto-trigger decomposition story for a full guard pipeline
Google Engineering recommends <10 files per change for reviewability

archivedStories.title: Add API rate-limit budget forecasting widget to spiral_dashboard.py
archivedStories.description: Based on current story velocity and per-request token usage from results.tsv, forecast when the daily API rate limit will be exhausted and display a projected completion time. Helps users schedule runs, manage quota, and avoid unexpected mid-run throttling.
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard shows: current burn rate (tokens/hour), projected daily-limit exhaustion time, and projected run completion time
Forecast uses a rolling 1-hour window of results.tsv timestamps and token usage columns
When projected exhaustion is less than 2 hours away, the widget is highlighted in amber
SPIRAL_DAILY_TOKEN_LIMIT env var sets the budget ceiling for forecast calculation (default: 1,000,000)
Forecast widget is hidden when results.tsv has fewer than 3 recent data rows
technicalNotes: Anthropic rate limits reference: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api/rate-limits
Default tier: 40k tokens/min, 1M tokens/day (varies by usage tier)
Burn rate formula: sum(input_tokens + output_tokens for rows in last 3600s) / 3600
Display format: 'At current pace, daily limit reached in ~2h 15m (at 14:32)'

archivedStories.title: Validate prd.json for non-UTF-8 bytes and control characters at startup
archivedStories.description: Add a startup preflight check that validates prd.json is well-formed UTF-8 and contains no ASCII control characters (0x00-0x1F except tab and newline) in string values. LLM-generated content occasionally embeds null bytes or other control characters that silently corrupt downstream JSON parsing and bash variable assignments.
acceptanceCriteria: validate_preflight.sh checks prd.json UTF-8 validity using `python3 -c 'import json,sys; json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))'`
Additional scan checks all string values for control characters via regex matching bytes 0x00-0x08, 0x0b-0x0c, 0x0e-0x1f
On detection, emit structured error with field path and hex representation of the offending byte
SPIRAL_SANITIZE_PRD=true auto-strips control characters instead of aborting
Unit tests: valid file passes, file with null byte in description fails, SANITIZE mode strips and continues
technicalNotes: JSON UTF-8 requirement: RFC 8259 Section 8.1 (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8259#section-8.1)
Shell-level check: `jq . prd.json > /dev/null 2>&1` exits non-zero on malformed input
Use json.loads() after reading raw bytes to obtain precise error offset
Common causes: LLM-generated content with Windows CRLF, smart quotes, or Word clipboard paste artifacts

archivedStories.title: Add `spiral status` subcommand with color-coded story progress table
archivedStories.description: Implement a spiral status CLI subcommand that prints a compact color-coded story progress table to stdout without launching the full dashboard server. Provides a fast at-a-glance view of story counts by status, current iteration, and estimated completion for use in terminal sessions and CI logs.
acceptanceCriteria: `spiral status` prints a table with columns: status, count, percentage, avg_retry_count
Header shows SPIRAL_RUN_ID and current iteration number
Color coding uses ANSI codes: green=passed, yellow=in_progress, red=skipped, grey=pending; respects NO_COLOR env var
`spiral status --json` outputs machine-readable JSON for CI pipeline consumption
Command completes in under 1 second (reads only prd.json and results.tsv, no API calls)
technicalNotes: Use rich library for table rendering: https://github.com/Textualize/rich
NO_COLOR standard: https://no-color.org/ — check `os.environ.get('NO_COLOR')` before applying ANSI
Falls back to plain aligned text when rich is not installed
Distinct from existing --status flag: this is a full subcommand with richer output and --json mode

archivedStories.title: Add `spiral search QUERY` subcommand to find stories by natural language
archivedStories.description: Implement a local semantic/fuzzy search over prd.json story titles, descriptions, and acceptanceCriteria, allowing users to quickly find a story ID without scrolling through the full PRD. Provides fast relevance-ranked results directly in the terminal.
acceptanceCriteria: `spiral search 'rate limit retry'` prints top-5 matching stories with ID, title, status, and relevance score
Search covers title, description, and acceptanceCriteria fields
Uses rapidfuzz fuzzy matching when sentence-transformers is unavailable; uses cosine similarity when available
Results are printed as a compact table; --json flag outputs machine-readable JSON
Command exits 0 even when no results found; prints 'No matching stories found'
technicalNotes: rapidfuzz for fuzzy matching: https://github.com/rapidfuzz/RapidFuzz (pip install rapidfuzz)
sentence-transformers for semantic search: https://www.sbert.net/
Implement in lib/search_stories.py; expose via main.py search subcommand
Cache sentence-transformer embeddings in .spiral/story_embeddings.pkl to avoid recomputation

archivedStories.title: Auto-generate Architecture Decision Record (ADR) when story passes
archivedStories.description: After a story passes validation, generate a lightweight ADR markdown file capturing the design choices made during implementation. ADRs are placed in docs/decisions/ and committed as part of the story commit, building a long-term architectural knowledge base alongside the code.
acceptanceCriteria: On story pass, ralph.sh calls Claude (haiku) with the story spec + diff and an ADR generation prompt
Generated ADR follows MADR format: Title, Status: Accepted, Context, Decision, Consequences
ADR file is saved to docs/decisions/<STORY_ID>-<kebab-title>.md and included in the story commit
SPIRAL_SKIP_ADR=true disables ADR generation entirely
prd.json story record gains _adrPath field pointing to the generated ADR file
technicalNotes: MADR (Markdown Architectural Decision Records) format: https://adr.github.io/madr/
Use haiku model for ADR generation to minimise cost (~$0.001 per ADR)
Store the ADR prompt template in lib/prompts/adr_template.md for maintainability
adr-tools CLI (optional integration): https://github.com/npryce/adr-tools

archivedStories.title: Add `spiral compact-prd` command to strip transient runtime fields from prd.json
archivedStories.description: Provide a spiral compact-prd subcommand that strips transient runtime fields (_lastAttempt, _workerPid, _researchOutput, _routerScore) from completed/skipped stories in prd.json. Keeps the PRD file clean and human-readable as it accumulates hundreds of stories across multiple runs.
acceptanceCriteria: `spiral compact-prd` removes transient fields from all stories with status passed or skipped
Original prd.json is backed up to .spiral/prd_pre_compact_<timestamp>.json before modification
Write operation is atomic: write to prd.json.tmp then rename
Prints summary: 'Compacted N stories, removed M fields, saved X KB'
Unit test verifies that required schema fields (id, title, status) are never removed
technicalNotes: Fields to strip: _lastAttempt, _workerPid, _researchOutput, _routerScore, _lastResearchAttempt
Implement in lib/compact_prd.py; expose via main.py compact subcommand
Reuse the atomic write pattern from merge_stories.py
Add to spiral-doctor: warn when prd.json file size exceeds 1MB

archivedStories.title: Add SPIRAL_BRANCH_PREFIX for per-story feature branch creation and naming
archivedStories.description: Optionally check out a dedicated feature branch for each story before Phase I implementation, enabling clean PR-per-story workflows. Branch name follows `<SPIRAL_BRANCH_PREFIX>/<STORY_ID>` convention (e.g., spiral/US-042). After story passes, branch is merged back to the base branch or left open for PR creation.
acceptanceCriteria: When SPIRAL_BRANCH_PREFIX is set, ralph.sh creates branch `<SPIRAL_BRANCH_PREFIX>/<STORY_ID>` before Phase I
After Phase V passes, branch is merged to SPIRAL_BASE_BRANCH with --no-ff unless SPIRAL_CREATE_PRS=true
When SPIRAL_CREATE_PRS=true, branch is pushed to remote and left open for PR creation step
Branch creation is idempotent: reuses existing branch for the same STORY_ID to support replays
Branch is deleted after successful merge unless SPIRAL_KEEP_STORY_BRANCHES=true
technicalNotes: Use git worktree for parallel worker isolation rather than local branch switching
For sequential mode, use `git checkout -B spiral/US-042` (force create or reset)
Guard against 'branch already checked out in another worktree' with `git worktree list`
Git branching workflows: https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Branching-Branching-Workflows

archivedStories.title: Add per-worker CPU and memory resource accounting columns to results.tsv
archivedStories.description: Record per-story CPU time (user+system seconds) and peak RSS memory alongside token counts in results.tsv. Enables identifying computationally expensive stories, correlating resource usage with model choice and story complexity, and feeding data into OOM watchdog threshold calibration.
acceptanceCriteria: ralph.sh wraps the Phase I+V execution block with `/usr/bin/time -f '%e %U %S %M'` measurement
results.tsv gains columns: wall_seconds, user_cpu_s, sys_cpu_s, peak_rss_kb
spiral_dashboard.py displays median and p95 resource usage grouped by model tier
When peak_rss_kb exceeds SPIRAL_WORKER_MEMORY_LIMIT, the existing OOM guard is triggered
Unit test verifies all four new columns are present in the results.tsv header and populated per row
technicalNotes: GNU time format string: '%e %U %S %M' (wall seconds, user CPU, sys CPU, max RSS KB)
macOS uses `/usr/bin/time -l` instead; detect platform with `uname -s`
Portable alternative: `{ TIMEFORMAT='%R %U %S'; time cmd; } 2>&1` in bash
GNU time man page: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/time.1.html

archivedStories.title: Cache Gemini pre-analysis results per story ID to skip redundant calls on retry
archivedStories.description: On story retry (attempt 2 or 3), ralph.sh re-runs the Gemini pre-analysis for the same story, burning quota and adding 10-30 seconds. Since the story definition has not changed, the output is identical. Cache the Gemini result in .spiral/gemini-cache/{story_id}.json keyed by SPIRAL_RUN_ID and reuse it on retry.
acceptanceCriteria: ralph.sh writes Gemini output to .spiral/gemini-cache/{story_id}.json after a successful call
On retry for the same story_id within the same SPIRAL_RUN_ID, the cache is used
Cache miss triggers a fresh Gemini call
Cache hits are logged as '[precontext] Gemini cache hit for {story_id}'
Cache directory is cleaned up at the start of each new Spiral run
technicalNotes: Store cache as JSON: {run_id, story_id, timestamp, content}
Validate: jq -r .run_id cache.json == $SPIRAL_RUN_ID
Add .spiral/gemini-cache/ to .gitignore

archivedStories.title: Add SPIRAL_RESEARCH_CACHE_TTL_HOURS to reuse Phase R output across iterations
archivedStories.description: Phase R runs a full web research pass every iteration even when the project has not changed. Add TTL-based caching: if _research_output.json is younger than SPIRAL_RESEARCH_CACHE_TTL_HOURS (default: 0 = disabled), skip Phase R and reuse the cached output. Useful for short-interval re-runs after manual story edits.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.sh checks _research_output.json mtime against SPIRAL_RESEARCH_CACHE_TTL_HOURS before Phase R
If file is newer than TTL: Phase R is skipped with '[Phase R] cache hit (Nh old)'
If SPIRAL_RESEARCH_CACHE_TTL_HOURS=0 (default): cache disabled, Phase R always runs
--skip-research flag still works as before
SPIRAL_RESEARCH_CACHE_TTL_HOURS documented in spiral.config.example.sh
technicalNotes: Use stat or python -c 'import os; print(os.path.getmtime(...))' for mtime
Compare: (now - mtime) / 3600 < SPIRAL_RESEARCH_CACHE_TTL_HOURS
Log cache age when reusing: '[Phase R] skipping -- research is 2h old (TTL: 6h)'

archivedStories.title: Fast-path small stories: skip Gemini pre-analysis for estimatedComplexity=small
archivedStories.description: The Gemini pre-analysis adds 10-30 seconds to every story including trivially small ones. For stories with estimatedComplexity=small and at most 2 filesTouch entries, skip the Gemini call entirely and go straight to Claude implementation. Saves 10-30 seconds per small story with no quality loss.
acceptanceCriteria: ralph.sh skips Gemini when story.estimatedComplexity == 'small' AND len(filesTouch) <= 2
Skip is logged: '[precontext] skipped -- small story with <= 2 file hints'
SPIRAL_GEMINI_SKIP_SMALL=false disables the fast-path (default: true)
Fast-path does not apply when SPIRAL_GEMINI_ANNOTATE_PROMPT is set
A bats test confirms the Gemini call is not made for qualifying stories
technicalNotes: Add the condition in ralph.sh before the Gemini invocation block
filesTouch length: jq '(.filesTouch // []) | length'

archivedStories.title: Compress old .spiral/ iteration artifacts with gzip to reduce disk usage
archivedStories.description: Each Spiral iteration writes several JSON files to .spiral/. On long runs these accumulate to tens of MB. Compress artifacts from iterations N-2 and older with gzip, keeping only the last 2 iterations uncompressed for easy inspection.
acceptanceCriteria: At the start of each iteration, JSON files from iter N-2 and older are gzip-compressed
Compressed files are named <original>.gz and originals are removed
Checkpoint resume logic handles a mix of compressed and uncompressed artifacts
Total .spiral/ disk usage is logged when SPIRAL_LOG_LEVEL=debug
A bats test confirms compression happens and originals are removed
technicalNotes: Use gzip without --keep to replace in place, or gzip --keep then rm
Skip compression if gzip is unavailable (log warning, continue)
Do not compress _checkpoint.json or latest-review.html (needed at runtime)

archivedStories.title: Implement Phase S (Story Validate) — auto-reject out-of-scope research stories
archivedStories.description: The Phase S stub exists in lib/phases/phase_s_story_validate.sh but has no implementation. Wire it into spiral.sh between Phase T and Phase M. Phase S reads candidate stories, checks each against prd.json goals[] and the constitution (if set), drops stories with no clear goal connection, and writes accepted stories to _validated_stories.json for Phase M.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.sh calls run_phase_story_validate() between Phase T and Phase M
Phase S produces .spiral/_validated_stories.json with only accepted stories
Stories with no connection to any prd.json goal[] are dropped with reason logged
Stories violating the constitution are also dropped when SPIRAL_SPECKIT_CONSTITUTION is set
Phase M reads _validated_stories.json instead of raw research output
A bats test with known off-topic stories confirms they are rejected
technicalNotes: Use Claude haiku as the reviewer with a simple YES/NO prompt against each goal
Fallback to keyword overlap check if the Claude call fails
Log acceptance rate per iteration to spiral_events.jsonl

archivedStories.title: Implement Phase 0 (Clarify) — interactive startup with time-limit and focus setting
archivedStories.description: The Phase 0 stub exists in lib/phases/phase_0_clarify.sh but has no implementation. Wire it into spiral.sh as a one-time pre-loop step. Phase 0 confirms focus area, asks how many hours to run (sets TIME_LIMIT_MINS), and optionally accepts initial story seeds from the user. Fully skipped in --gate proceed/skip mode.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.sh calls run_phase_clarify() once before the main loop, not on resume
Phase 0 asks 'How many hours should Spiral run? (Enter for unlimited)' and sets TIME_LIMIT_MINS
Phase 0 asks 'Any focus area for this session?' and sets SPIRAL_FOCUS if answered
Phase 0 accepts initial story seeds (one per line) and adds them to prd.json
With --gate proceed or --gate skip: Phase 0 is skipped entirely
Checkpoint records phase_0_complete: true so resume skips it
