technicalNotes: Use bash read -t 60 -p '...' to avoid hanging on no input
Story seeds: convert plain text lines to minimal story objects with priority:medium
Output written to .spiral/_clarify_output.json for auditability

archivedStories.title: Atomic prd.json write in merge_stories.py using temp-file rename
archivedStories.description: merge_stories.py writes directly to prd.json in-place. A crash or SIGKILL mid-write produces a truncated or corrupt prd.json. Rewrite the write path to write to prd.json.tmp first, then atomically rename via os.replace(). This prevents the file from ever being caught in a half-written state.
acceptanceCriteria: merge_stories.py writes output to prd.json.tmp then os.replace() to prd.json
prd.json.tmp is removed on both success and exception via try/finally
Simulating a kill mid-write leaves prd.json intact from before the merge
A unit test mocks os.replace to raise and confirms prd.json is unchanged
Existing merge_stories.py unit tests continue to pass
technicalNotes: os.replace() is atomic on POSIX; on Windows it is safer than direct overwrite
Apply the same pattern to every other location that writes prd.json directly

archivedStories.title: Force-remove orphaned worker git worktree and branch on implementation timeout
archivedStories.description: When a parallel worker hits SPIRAL_IMPL_TIMEOUT, run_parallel_ralph.sh kills the process but leaves the git worktree and branch in place. These ghost worktrees consume disk, cause branch-already-checked-out errors on the next run, and bloat git internals. Add a post-kill cleanup step that force-removes the worktree and deletes the branch.
acceptanceCriteria: When a worker is killed by timeout, its worktree is removed within 10 seconds
The worker feature branch is deleted after worktree removal
If removal fails, a warning is logged but the run continues
spiral.sh --status reports no orphaned worktrees after a timeout scenario
Integration test with a mock hanging worker confirms cleanup fires
technicalNotes: Add cleanup_worker() called from the timeout handler in run_parallel_ralph.sh
Use: git worktree remove --force <path> && git branch -D <branch>
On Windows add a short sleep before removal to allow file handle release

archivedStories.title: Detect and stash dirty working tree before Phase I to prevent git errors
archivedStories.description: If a user edits files while Spiral is paused at Phase 0 or Gate, the working tree becomes dirty. Phase I then fails with confusing git errors when creating worktrees. Add a pre-Phase-I check: detect uncommitted changes and auto-stash them (SPIRAL_AUTO_STASH=true) or abort with a clear actionable message.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.sh detects uncommitted changes before Phase I using git status --porcelain
With SPIRAL_AUTO_STASH=true: changes are stashed, Phase I runs, stash is popped after
With SPIRAL_AUTO_STASH=false (default): Phase I is skipped with an actionable message
Stash pop failure is logged as a warning and does not crash the run
A bats test exercises both the stash and abort paths
technicalNotes: git stash push --include-untracked -m spiral-auto-stash-iter-N
Pop in a trap so it runs even on interrupt
SPIRAL_AUTO_STASH documented in spiral.config.example.sh

archivedStories.title: Rotate ralph-run.log when size exceeds SPIRAL_LOG_MAX_MB
archivedStories.description: ralph-run.log grows unbounded across runs. Long projects accumulate hundreds of MB. Add automatic rotation: when the log exceeds SPIRAL_LOG_MAX_MB (default 50 MB), rename to .log.1 and start fresh. Keep at most SPIRAL_LOG_KEEP_ROTATIONS (default 3) old files.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.sh checks log file size before each iteration
When size exceeds limit: rename .log to .log.1, .log.1 to .log.2, etc.
Files beyond SPIRAL_LOG_KEEP_ROTATIONS are deleted
A rotation notice is written as the first line of the new log
Both config vars documented in spiral.config.example.sh
technicalNotes: Portable size check via python3 os.path.getsize()
Rotate at iteration start before appending
On Windows, close and reopen the fd around the rename

archivedStories.title: Add Claude API reachability probe to pre-flight check and spiral-doctor
archivedStories.description: Spiral discovers Claude is unreachable only after a full phase timeout, wasting minutes. Add a fast 5-second connectivity probe to startup pre-flight and spiral-doctor. Fail immediately with exit code 5 and a clear message if the API does not respond.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral-doctor reports PASS/FAIL for Claude API reachable check
spiral.sh pre-flight includes the same probe (skippable with SPIRAL_SKIP_API_CHECK=true)
The probe uses a 5-second timeout and does not count against SPIRAL_RESEARCH_RETRIES
Failure exits with code 5 and a clear message
Probe is skipped in --dry-run mode
technicalNotes: Use timeout 5 claude --version or a minimal 1-token completion
Add check_claude_api() to lib/spiral_doctor.sh
Also verify ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is non-empty before any network call

archivedStories.title: Scan for duplicate story IDs in prd.json at startup and abort or deduplicate
archivedStories.description: Parallel merges or manual edits can produce duplicate story IDs. When jq processes duplicates, one silently overwrites the other causing data loss. Add a startup scan: strict mode (default) exits with a conflict list; lenient mode (SPIRAL_DEDUP_IDS=lenient) keeps the passes:true entry and drops the duplicate.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.sh scans prd.json for duplicate IDs at startup
Strict mode (default): duplicate IDs cause exit 1 with a printed conflict list
Lenient mode: keep passes:true entry, drop duplicate, log warning
Result is written back atomically
A bats test covers both modes with a pre-seeded duplicate prd.json
technicalNotes: Use jq group_by to detect duplicates
Run after config load, before prd_stats()
Write events to spiral_events.jsonl

archivedStories.title: Replace bare exit numbers in spiral.sh with named exit code constants
archivedStories.description: Spiral exits with 0 or generic 1 from most paths. CI pipelines cannot distinguish all-done from API-crashed from cost-ceiling-hit. Define named readonly constants (EXIT_DONE=0, EXIT_MAX_ITERS=2, EXIT_COST_CEILING=3, EXIT_CYCLE=4, EXIT_API_DOWN=5, EXIT_PRD_CORRUPT=6) and use them everywhere. Document in --help and README.
acceptanceCriteria: Named constants defined near top of spiral.sh with readonly
All exit points use constants not bare numbers
spiral.sh --help lists exit codes with descriptions
README.md has an exit codes table
A bats test triggers each path and asserts the correct code
technicalNotes: Use values 2-9 to stay in the conventional range
Audit all existing exit 1 calls and remap each
Keep EXIT_DONE=0 and EXIT_ERR=1 to match POSIX convention

archivedStories.title: Run Phase R and Phase T in parallel to halve story-preparation wall time
archivedStories.description: Phase R (60-300s) and Phase T (30-60s) are completely independent but run sequentially. Launching them as background bash jobs and awaiting both halves story-preparation latency every iteration with no quality tradeoff.
acceptanceCriteria: Phase R and Phase T run as background jobs awaited before Phase M
If either fails, the other continues and its output is treated as empty
The banner shows combined wall time as max(R,T) rather than R+T
Checkpoint records R and T independently so resume skips only what finished
A bats test with mock scripts confirms they run simultaneously
technicalNotes: run_phase_r & PID_R=$!; run_phase_t & PID_T=$!; wait $PID_R; RC_R=$?; wait $PID_T; RC_T=$?
Redirect each phase stdout to a dedicated section to avoid log interleaving
Checkpoint needs phase_r_done and phase_t_done as separate fields

archivedStories.title: Skip Phase V test suite when Phase I produced zero new story passes
archivedStories.description: Phase V runs the full test suite after every Phase I even when all stories were retried or skipped and nothing changed. Snapshot the passed-story count before Phase I; if it has not increased after, skip Phase V and go directly to Phase C.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.sh counts passed stories before and after Phase I
If the count did not increase: Phase V is skipped with a logged message
If the count increased: Phase V runs normally
SPIRAL_FORCE_VALIDATE=true bypasses the skip for CI
Skip is recorded in _checkpoint.json and _iteration_summary.json
A bats test confirms Phase V is skipped when Phase I produces no passes
technicalNotes: PASSES_BEFORE=$(jq count) before Phase I; PASSES_AFTER=$(same) after
Works in parallel-worker mode because prd.json is the shared source of truth

archivedStories.title: Emit OTel GenAI agent spans per story phase using semconv
archivedStories.description: SPIRAL already emits JSONL telemetry events but not standard OpenTelemetry traces. Instrument each phase (R, T, I, V, M, G) as an OTel child span under a root invoke_agent span, setting the required GenAI semantic convention attributes (gen_ai.agent.name, gen_ai.agent.id, gen_ai.operation.name, gen_ai.system) so traces are consumable by any OTLP-compatible backend. This enables cross-tool observability and cost attribution without vendor lock-in.
acceptanceCriteria: Each story execution produces a root span named invoke_agent spiral with child spans per phase
Spans include gen_ai.agent.name=spiral, gen_ai.operation.name matching phase letter, gen_ai.system=anthropic
Token counts from Claude responses are recorded as gen_ai.usage.input_tokens and gen_ai.usage.output_tokens span attributes
Spans export via OTLP HTTP to OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT when env var is set; silently no-ops when unset
A Jaeger or Zipkin trace confirms parent/child relationship across all 6 phases
technicalNotes: Use opentelemetry-sdk Python package; wrap existing phase invocations in lib/ Python modules
OTel GenAI agent span spec: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans/
Span kind should be CLIENT for cross-process agents, INTERNAL when in-process
Correlate with existing trace_id / span_id fields already written to JSONL event log

archivedStories.title: Import user stories from GitHub Issues via GraphQL API
archivedStories.description: Teams who track work in GitHub Issues must manually copy stories into prd.json. Add a spiral import-github command that queries a repo's issues via the GitHub GraphQL API, maps issue title/body/labels to prd.json story fields, and appends them with state=pending. This eliminates dual-entry and keeps SPIRAL in sync with the team's issue tracker.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral import-github --repo owner/repo --label spiral pulls all open issues with the given label
Issue title maps to story title; body maps to description; milestone maps to priority
Duplicate detection: issues whose title already exists in prd.json are skipped with a warning
Paginated fetching handles repos with >100 matching issues using GraphQL cursor pagination
Dry-run mode (--dry-run) prints the stories that would be added without modifying prd.json
Requires GITHUB_TOKEN env var; exits with error code 1 and clear message if missing
technicalNotes: GitHub GraphQL Issues query: https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/objects#issue
Use gh CLI's --paginate flag or python-gql library for cursor-based pagination
Map GitHub labels to priority: priority:critical→critical, priority:high→high, else medium

archivedStories.title: Pre-flight cross-story file conflict detection using git merge-tree
archivedStories.description: When SPIRAL assigns multiple stories to parallel workers, stories that touch the same files will produce merge conflicts at Phase M, wasting compute. Before launching workers for a batch, run a read-only git merge-tree simulation between each pair of active worktree branches to detect overlapping file edits early and requeue one story of each conflicting pair to the next batch.
acceptanceCriteria: Before each parallel batch launch, all story pair combinations are checked with git merge-tree --write-tree
If merge-tree exits non-zero for a pair, the lower-priority story is removed from the current batch and its state is set back to pending
The conflict detection result is written to a conflict-log.jsonl entry with story pair, conflicting file paths, and batch number
Detection completes within 5 seconds for batches of up to 8 stories
A --skip-conflict-preflight flag bypasses the check for debugging purposes
technicalNotes: git merge-tree --write-tree <base> <branchA> <branchB> exits non-zero and lists conflicts to stdout
Base commit for three-way merge is the common ancestor: git merge-base branchA branchB
Conflict preflight is distinct from the existing merge conflict detection story which operates post-implementation

archivedStories.title: Detect and block prompt injection patterns in prd.json story fields
archivedStories.description: prd.json is readable by external contributors and could contain adversarial instructions in description or acceptanceCriteria fields. Before passing story content to Claude, scan text fields through an injection pattern detector and abort the phase with a security error if injection signatures are found, protecting the SPIRAL agent from indirect prompt injection.
acceptanceCriteria: A scan_for_injection(text) function checks for OWASP LLM01:2025 injection patterns before each LLM call
Detected patterns include: ignore/disregard previous instructions, system prompt override attempts, jailbreak tokens (DAN, STAN), and base64-encoded suspicious payloads
When injection is detected, the story is set to failed with reason=security_block and a WARN entry is appended to the security audit log (security-audit.jsonl)
A --allow-unsafe-stories flag bypasses scanning (requires explicit user opt-in)
Unit tests cover at least 10 known injection variants from OWASP Top 10 for LLMs 2025
technicalNotes: OWASP LLM01:2025 Prompt Injection: https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm01-prompt-injection/
LLM Guard PromptInjection scanner uses a fine-tuned classifier: https://github.com/protectai/llm-guard
Lightweight alternative: regex-based pattern list covering common jailbreak phrases
NIST AI RMF and ISO 42001 now mandate prompt injection controls for production AI agents

archivedStories.title: Sanitize LLM output before writing to disk to block indirect injection
archivedStories.description: SPIRAL writes Claude's generated code and test files directly to the worktree. A compromised upstream package or injected web content fetched during Phase R could cause Claude to emit shell escape sequences, git config overwrites, or malicious hook scripts. Add an output sanitizer that validates generated file paths stay within the worktree and strips ANSI escape codes and null bytes before disk writes.
acceptanceCriteria: All file write operations from Phase I validate the target path resolves within the story's worktree directory (path traversal prevention)
ANSI escape sequences and null bytes are stripped from all LLM-generated file content before writing
Attempts to write to .git/ paths are blocked and logged to security-audit.jsonl
Attempts to write executable files outside src/ and tests/ directories require SPIRAL_ALLOW_EXEC_WRITES=true
Sanitization does not break legitimate code generation (test with a Python file containing ANSI strings as data)
technicalNotes: Path traversal prevention: use os.path.realpath() and assert path.startswith(worktree_root)
OWASP LLM Prompt Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/LLM_Prompt_Injection_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html
Strip ANSI: re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m', '', content); strip null: content.replace('\x00', '')

archivedStories.title: Record per-phase LLM token metrics as OTel GenAI metrics
archivedStories.description: Complement span-level tracing with OTel metrics for token throughput and latency so operators can set alerts on token budgets without parsing spans. Emit the four mandatory GenAI metrics (gen_ai.client.token.usage, gen_ai.client.operation.duration, gen_ai.server.request.duration, gen_ai.server.ttft) as histograms/counters with story_id and phase labels attached as attributes.
acceptanceCriteria: gen_ai.client.token.usage counter increments by prompt+completion tokens after each LLM call
gen_ai.client.operation.duration histogram records wall-clock ms per LLM call
Metrics are exported via OTLP when OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is set
Prometheus scrape endpoint /metrics available when SPIRAL_PROM_PORT env var is set
Dashboard (spiral-ui) shows a per-story token burn sparkline sourced from these metrics
technicalNotes: OTel GenAI metrics spec: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-metrics/
Use opentelemetry-sdk MeterProvider with PrometheusExporter for local scrape endpoint
Attribute token counts from Claude's usage field in API response body

archivedStories.title: Add semantic-release automated version bump on spiral completion
archivedStories.description: When a SPIRAL run finishes with at least one story merged, automatically determine the next SemVer version from conventional commit history since the last tag, create a git tag, and write a CHANGELOG section. This removes manual tagging and ensures every successful run produces a traceable artifact. Uses python-semantic-release so no Node.js runtime is required.
acceptanceCriteria: Running spiral.sh with SPIRAL_AUTO_RELEASE=true triggers version calculation after Phase M completes all stories
Version bump follows conventional commits: feat→minor, fix/perf→patch, BREAKING CHANGE footer→major
A git tag vX.Y.Z is created and pushed when SPIRAL_GIT_PUSH=true
CHANGELOG.md is updated with a new section listing story titles and commit SHAs
If no releasable commits exist, no tag is created and a warning is logged
technicalNotes: python-semantic-release docs: https://python-semantic-release.readthedocs.io/
SPIRAL already enforces conventional commits; add semantic_release.toml config pointing at main branch
Integrate as a post-run hook in spiral.sh after the final merge phase completes

archivedStories.title: Implement model benchmark harness to compare worker model outputs
archivedStories.description: SPIRAL supports a model routing table but has no way to measure which model produces higher-quality story implementations. Add a benchmark mode that runs the same story through two configured models in separate worktrees, scores both outputs against acceptance criteria using an LLM judge, and writes results to benchmark-results.jsonl. This enables data-driven model routing decisions.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.sh --benchmark <story-id> --models modelA,modelB executes both models against the same story
Each model run is isolated in its own worktree and branch
An LLM judge (configurable, defaults to claude-3-5-haiku) scores each output on a 1-5 rubric across correctness, test pass rate, and code style
benchmark-results.jsonl records model name, story id, score per dimension, token cost, and wall time
spiral-ui benchmark tab visualises side-by-side scores for all benchmarked stories
technicalNotes: LLM-as-judge evaluation pattern documented by DeepEval: https://docs.confident-ai.com/docs/evaluation-introduction
Score dimensions align with SPIRAL acceptance criteria fields already in prd.json
Use existing worktree isolation infrastructure; add a benchmark state to story lifecycle

archivedStories.title: Track actual vs estimated complexity and surface calibration report
archivedStories.description: Stories in prd.json carry estimatedComplexity (small/medium/large) but SPIRAL never measures whether estimates were accurate. After each story completes, record actual phase durations and pass/fail count to a calibration log. Periodically compute a calibration score and surface it in spiral-ui so users can improve future estimates.
acceptanceCriteria: On story completion, a calibration record is appended to calibration.jsonl with story_id, estimated_complexity, actual_duration_s, phase_retries, and passed boolean
spiral-ui shows a calibration panel with median actual duration per complexity tier (small/medium/large)
When actual duration exceeds the median for a tier by 2x, the story is flagged as underestimated in the dashboard
A calibration summary is written to the run report after each full SPIRAL run
spiral --calibration-report prints the calibration table to stdout
technicalNotes: Agile velocity feedback loop pattern: use rolling window of last 20 completed stories for median calculation
Complexity tiers can be mapped to rough hour buckets: small=<30m, medium=30m-2h, large=>2h
Integrate with existing results.tsv output so no new file format is strictly required

archivedStories.title: Implement SPIRAL plugin system with hook-based extension points
archivedStories.description: SPIRAL has per-phase hooks in config but no formal plugin API for third-party extensions. Introduce a plugins/ directory convention where each subdirectory is a plugin containing a plugin.toml manifest and hook scripts. SPIRAL scans plugins/ on startup, validates manifests, and invokes hook scripts at declared lifecycle points. This enables community extensions without forking spiral.sh.
acceptanceCriteria: plugins/my-plugin/plugin.toml with name, version, hooks[] fields is discovered and loaded on startup
Supported hook points: pre-phase, post-phase, post-story, post-run, pre-merge
Plugins receive story context as JSON on stdin and may exit non-zero to abort the triggering operation
spiral --list-plugins prints all loaded plugins with name, version, and declared hooks
A sample plugin (plugins/notify-slack/) ships as documentation of the plugin contract
Malformed plugin.toml emits a warning and skips the plugin without crashing SPIRAL
technicalNotes: Declarative plugin manifest pattern from Claude Code plugins architecture
plugin.toml fields: name (string), version (semver string), hooks (array of hook point names), allowed_env (array of required env var names)
Hook scripts are executed via bash with a 30-second timeout enforced by timeout(1)

archivedStories.title: Add Slack notification plugin for story lifecycle events
archivedStories.description: Development teams need real-time visibility into SPIRAL run progress in their chat tool. Add a built-in Slack notification plugin that posts a message to a configured channel when a story passes, fails, or when a full run completes. Uses Slack Incoming Webhooks so no OAuth flow is needed.
acceptanceCriteria: Setting SPIRAL_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL env var activates Slack notifications automatically
A message is posted when a story transitions to passed or failed, including story title and retry count
A summary message is posted on run completion with total stories passed/failed/skipped and run duration
Messages use Slack Block Kit formatting with colour-coded attachments (green=passed, red=failed)
Notification failures are non-fatal: SPIRAL logs a warning and continues the run
SPIRAL_SLACK_EVENTS env var accepts a comma-separated subset of events (e.g. failed,completed) to reduce noise
technicalNotes: Slack Incoming Webhooks API: https://api.slack.com/messaging/webhooks
Block Kit reference: https://api.slack.com/reference/block-kit/blocks
Implement as a plugin in plugins/notify-slack/ using the plugin system from the companion story

archivedStories.title: Generate Mermaid dependency graph of prd.json stories on demand
archivedStories.description: prd.json stories have a dependencies array but there is no visual way to inspect the graph before running SPIRAL. Add a spiral graph command that reads dependencies and generates a Mermaid flowchart (LR direction) showing story IDs, titles, and dependency edges, written to docs/dependency-graph.md. This helps authors spot cycles and understand execution order.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral graph outputs a valid Mermaid flowchart block to stdout by default
spiral graph --output docs/dependency-graph.md writes to file and prints the path
Nodes are labelled with story ID and truncated title (max 40 chars)
Stories with no dependencies are visually distinct (different shape or style)
Cycles in the dependency graph are detected, reported as an error, and the offending edges are highlighted in the output
Graph renders correctly in GitHub markdown preview
technicalNotes: Mermaid flowchart syntax: https://mermaid.js.org/syntax/flowchart.html
Use Python networkx for cycle detection (nx.find_cycle) then render to Mermaid string
spiral-ui could embed the Mermaid diagram using mermaid.js CDN in the existing React dashboard

archivedStories.title: Add `spiral import-jira` command using Jira REST API v3
archivedStories.description: Enterprises tracking work in Jira Cloud need to feed epics and stories into SPIRAL without manual JSON editing. Add a spiral import-jira command that queries a Jira project via REST API v3 with JQL, maps issue fields to prd.json format, and appends stories with state=pending. Jira priority levels map to SPIRAL priority strings and the Jira issue key is stored for two-way traceability.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral import-jira --host mycompany.atlassian.net --project ENG --jql 'labels=spiral AND status=Backlog' fetches matching issues
Jira priority Highest/High maps to critical/high; Medium maps to medium; Low/Lowest maps to low
Jira issue key (e.g. ENG-42) is stored in story metadata under jiraKey field
Authentication uses JIRA_API_TOKEN + JIRA_USER_EMAIL env vars with Basic auth base64 encoding
Pagination handles >50 results using Jira's maxResults/startAt cursor mechanism
Dry-run flag prints preview without modifying prd.json
technicalNotes: Jira REST API v3 issues search: https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-issue-search/
Authentication: base64(email:api_token) passed as Authorization: Basic header
Use requests library; paginate by incrementing startAt by maxResults (default 50) until total is reached

archivedStories.title: Render interactive story dependency graph in spiral-ui React dashboard
archivedStories.description: spiral-ui currently shows story cards in a list but does not visualise dependency relationships. Integrate mermaid.js into the React dashboard to render a live dependency flowchart sourced from prd.json dependencies arrays, with colour-coded nodes reflecting current story status. This gives operators an at-a-glance view of the critical path and any blocked stories.
acceptanceCriteria: A new Graph tab in spiral-ui renders a Mermaid LR flowchart of all stories and their dependency edges
Node colours reflect story status: pending=grey, in_progress=blue, passed=green, failed=red, skipped=yellow
Clicking a node opens the story detail panel (existing drilldown component)
The graph re-renders automatically when prd.json is polled for updates (existing polling interval)
The graph renders within 2 seconds for a PRD with 100 stories on a modern browser
technicalNotes: mermaid.js React integration: npm install mermaid and use useEffect to call mermaid.initialize + mermaid.run
Generate Mermaid source string client-side from the prd.json data already fetched by the dashboard
Mermaid npm package: https://mermaid.js.org/

archivedStories.title: Run LLM Guard input scanner on Phase R web-fetched content
archivedStories.description: Phase R fetches arbitrary web content and documentation which is passed into subsequent LLM prompts, creating an indirect prompt injection surface. Integrate LLM Guard's PromptInjection input scanner to scan fetched research content before it is inserted into prompts, blocking content that scores above a configurable threshold.
acceptanceCriteria: Web-fetched content in Phase R is passed through LLM Guard PromptInjection scanner before prompt assembly
Scan threshold is configurable via SPIRAL_INJECTION_THRESHOLD env var (default 0.8, range 0.0-1.0)
Content exceeding the threshold is truncated and replaced with a sanitized placeholder; Phase R continues with the remaining sources
Scan results (score, threshold, truncated boolean) are recorded in the story's JSONL event log
Performance: scanning a 4KB text block completes in under 500ms on CPU-only hardware
technicalNotes: LLM Guard PromptInjection scanner: https://protectai.github.io/llm-guard/input_scanners/prompt_injection/
pip install llm-guard; from llm_guard.input_scanners import PromptInjection
LLM Guard uses a fine-tuned deberta-v3-base-prompt-injection model; cached locally after first download

archivedStories.title: Add pip-audit and npm audit dependency vulnerability scan gate in CI
archivedStories.description: Run pip-audit on Python dependencies and npm audit on Node dependencies as a CI gate that fails the build on HIGH or CRITICAL CVEs. AI-generated code that introduces new dependencies could silently pull in vulnerable packages; automated scanning catches these before merge.
acceptanceCriteria: GitHub Actions workflow runs pip-audit and fails on severity >= HIGH
npm audit --audit-level=high is run when package.json is present
Scan results are uploaded as a CI artifact in JSON format
A known-safe suppress list (audit-ignore.txt or .pip-audit.toml) is supported to handle false positives
technicalNotes: pip-audit docs: https://pypi.org/project/pip-audit/
npm audit: https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v10/commands/npm-audit
Use pip-audit --format json --output pip-audit-results.json
Pin pip-audit version in CI to ensure reproducible scans

archivedStories.title: Validate LLM JSON outputs with Pydantic models before downstream processing
archivedStories.description: Parse every LLM-returned JSON blob through a strict Pydantic v2 model before any downstream code processes it. Currently, malformed or unexpected LLM output can cause cryptic KeyError or AttributeError failures deep in the pipeline; Pydantic validation surfaces the exact field mismatch at the point of ingestion with a structured error.
acceptanceCriteria: Pydantic models are defined for all LLM output shapes: story decomposition, research output, route_stories result, and synthesize_tests report
A ValidationError is caught, logged to spiral_events.jsonl with the raw LLM output, and triggers a retry or graceful skip
The validation error message includes the field path and received value
100% of LLM JSON parse sites use model_validate() rather than bare json.loads()
technicalNotes: Use Pydantic v2 model_validate() with strict=False for lenient coercion where safe
Pydantic v2 docs: https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/models/
Define a BaseModel subclass per LLM call site in a new spiral/models/ package
Add model_json_schema() output to CI artifact for schema documentation

archivedStories.title: Cascade skip status through dependency chain when a dependency is _skipped
archivedStories.description: When a story is marked _skipped: true, automatically propagate that skip to all downstream stories that declare it as a dependency. Currently, blocked stories stay in pending state and waste worker time attempting implementation when their prerequisite will never be satisfied.
acceptanceCriteria: When a story transitions to _skipped, a cascade function traverses prd.json and marks all direct and transitive dependents as _skipped with _failureReason: 'dependency <ID> was skipped'
Cascaded skips are logged to spiral_events.jsonl with event_type: dependency_cascade_skip
The cascade runs after every story skip, not just at startup
A --no-cascade-skip flag in spiral.sh disables this behavior for debugging
technicalNotes: Implement as a BFS/DFS traversal over the dependency graph in a new cascade_skip() function in state_machine.py
Must be idempotent: running cascade multiple times produces the same result
Update prd.json atomically after computing the full cascade set

archivedStories.title: Add CodeQL security scanning GitHub Actions workflow for AI-generated code
archivedStories.description: Add a CodeQL analysis workflow that runs on every push and pull request to detect security vulnerabilities (injection flaws, insecure deserialization, path traversal) in AI-generated code. Standard static analysis like Semgrep focuses on patterns; CodeQL performs dataflow analysis that catches subtle injection chains Semgrep misses.
acceptanceCriteria: GitHub Actions workflow runs CodeQL analysis for Python and JavaScript on push/PR
Workflow uses SHA-pinned github/codeql-action version
Results are uploaded to GitHub Code Scanning via upload-sarif action
High-severity findings block PR merge via required status check
Workflow runs only on changed files using path filters to reduce CI time
technicalNotes: CodeQL setup: https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/code-scanning/creating-an-advanced-setup-for-code-scanning
Use actions/checkout@<SHA> and github/codeql-action/init@<SHA> with pinned SHAs
CodeQL queries: use security-and-quality suite for broader coverage

archivedStories.title: Graceful degradation: fall back to Claude for Phase R when Gemini returns 503
archivedStories.description: When the Gemini API returns HTTP 503 Service Unavailable during Phase R pre-analysis, automatically retry once then fall back to Claude with a simplified research prompt rather than failing the phase. Gemini outages are common; current behavior blocks the entire iteration until the user manually intervenes.
acceptanceCriteria: On Gemini 503, Phase R retries once after a 10-second backoff, then switches to Claude with SPIRAL_RESEARCH_MODEL as fallback
Fallback to Claude is logged with event_type: gemini_fallback in spiral_events.jsonl
A SPIRAL_GEMINI_FALLBACK_MODEL env var specifies which Claude model to use (default: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 for cost)
If both Gemini and Claude fallback fail, Phase R exits with a clear error and the iteration is retried up to SPIRAL_RESEARCH_RETRIES times
spiral-doctor reports SPIRAL_GEMINI_FALLBACK_MODEL in its dependency check
technicalNotes: Google AI Studio API error codes: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/troubleshooting
Distinguish 503 (transient, fall back) from 400 (bad request, do not retry)
Log which model ultimately served the Phase R response in _iteration_summary.json

archivedStories.title: HMAC-SHA256 signing for SPIRAL_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK outbound payloads
archivedStories.description: Sign outbound webhook POST bodies with HMAC-SHA256 using a configurable secret key and include the signature in the X-Spiral-Signature-256 header. Receivers can verify payload authenticity and reject tampered or spoofed requests. Without signing, any actor who learns the webhook URL can inject fabricated events.
acceptanceCriteria: When SPIRAL_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set, every POST request includes an X-Spiral-Signature-256: sha256=<hex> header
The HMAC key is read from SPIRAL_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET env var and never logged
Sending without the secret still works (backward-compatible, header omitted)
spiral-doctor reports a warning when SPIRAL_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK is set but SPIRAL_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not
technicalNotes: Use Python hmac.new(key, body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest() to generate signature
Follow GitHub's webhook signing convention: https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/securing-your-webhooks
Add SPIRAL_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET to spiral.config.sh template comments

archivedStories.title: Add `spiral import-csv` command to bulk-import stories from CSV spreadsheet
archivedStories.description: Allow users to import multiple stories at once by pointing `spiral import-csv stories.csv` at a spreadsheet. Product managers and stakeholders often manage backlogs in Excel or Google Sheets; supporting CSV import removes the manual JSON editing step and reduces entry errors.
acceptanceCriteria: Command accepts a CSV file path with columns: title, description, priority, estimatedComplexity, acceptanceCriteria (semicolon-separated), technicalNotes (semicolon-separated)
Imported stories are assigned sequential IDs following the existing SPIRAL_STORY_PREFIX convention
Duplicate titles (exact match) are skipped with a warning rather than creating duplicates
A --dry-run flag prints the parsed stories without writing to prd.json
Invalid rows (missing title or priority) are reported with row numbers and skipped
technicalNotes: Use Python csv.DictReader for parsing; support both comma and tab delimiters via --delimiter flag
Reuse the atomic prd.json write pattern (temp-file rename) from merge_stories.py
Validate priority field against allowed enum values before inserting

archivedStories.title: Lint prd.json at startup: warn on stories missing acceptanceCriteria
archivedStories.description: At startup, scan prd.json and emit a structured warning for every story that has an empty or missing acceptanceCriteria array. Acceptance criteria are essential for Phase V validation; stories lacking them will pass validation trivially and produce untested implementations.
acceptanceCriteria: startup lint enumerates stories where acceptanceCriteria is absent, null, or an empty array
Each violation is printed as WARN [prd-lint] Story <ID> '<title>' has no acceptanceCriteria
Violations are also written to spiral_events.jsonl with event_type: prd_lint_warning
A SPIRAL_STRICT_AC=true env var causes the lint to be a hard error that aborts startup
Stories with _skipped: true are excluded from the lint check
technicalNotes: Add prd_lint() function to validate_prd.py or a new prd_lint.py module
Run after prd.json is loaded but before worker dispatch
Consider adding a --fix flag that prompts the user to add criteria interactively

archivedStories.title: Add `spiral export-report` command to generate Markdown story status report
archivedStories.description: Generate a human-readable Markdown report summarizing all stories, their current status, failure reasons, and passed commit SHAs. This report serves as a release audit trail and can be attached to pull requests or sprint reviews without requiring access to the raw prd.json file.
acceptanceCriteria: Command writes SPIRAL_REPORT_<timestamp>.md with sections: Summary, Passed Stories, Failed/Skipped Stories, Pending Stories
Each story entry shows: ID, title, status, _passedCommit (if passed), _failureReason (if skipped), retry count
Summary section includes: total stories, pass rate %, total API cost estimate (if tracked)
Output path is configurable via --output flag; defaults to current directory
Report is valid CommonMark Markdown renderable by GitHub
technicalNotes: Read directly from prd.json; no external dependencies needed beyond Python stdlib
Use Python's textwrap.dedent and f-strings for template rendering
Add --format json option to emit machine-readable version for CI artifact ingestion

archivedStories.title: Validate git user.name and user.email config before any AI commit
archivedStories.description: Before ralph.sh or any script invokes git commit, verify that git config user.name and user.email are set in either the local repo or global config. Commits without author identity silently fail or produce anonymous commits that break git blame and changelog generation downstream.
acceptanceCriteria: Pre-commit check runs git config user.name and git config user.email; aborts with a clear error if either is empty
Error message provides the exact git commands to fix the missing config
Check is part of spiral-doctor output
When SPIRAL_GIT_AUTHOR is set, it is used as a fallback if local/global config is missing
Check runs in spiral.sh preflight, not just in ralph.sh, so it catches the issue before any worker launches
technicalNotes: Use git config --get user.name and check exit code
If SPIRAL_GIT_AUTHOR=Name <email> is set, auto-configure: git config user.name and user.email from it
Reference: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config

archivedStories.title: Record per-phase wall-clock timing in _iteration_summary.json
archivedStories.description: Capture time.perf_counter() start and end timestamps for each pipeline phase (R, T, I, V, G, M) and write them to _iteration_summary.json under a phase_timings map. This data drives performance optimization decisions and helps users identify which phase is the bottleneck in slow iterations.
acceptanceCriteria: _iteration_summary.json includes phase_timings: {R: {start_epoch: float, duration_seconds: float}, ...} for each phase that ran
Timing is measured with time.perf_counter() for monotonic accuracy
Phase timings are also included in the spiral_events.jsonl phase_end events
spiral_dashboard.py displays a per-phase timing bar chart using the iteration summary data
Phases that were skipped (e.g., Phase V when no stories passed) are omitted from phase_timings
technicalNotes: Python time.perf_counter() docs: https://docs.python.org/3/library/time.html#time.perf_counter
Store epoch timestamp alongside duration for absolute time reference: time.time() for epoch, perf_counter for duration
Consider a PhaseTimer context manager: with PhaseTimer('R') as t: ... that auto-writes to summary

archivedStories.title: Add exponential backoff with jitter for transient filesystem I/O errors on prd.json
archivedStories.description: Wrap all prd.json read and write operations in a retry loop with exponential backoff and jitter to handle transient OS-level file lock errors (PermissionError, OSError EACCES/ETXTBSY) on Windows. These errors occur when antivirus or file indexers briefly lock the file; current code raises immediately and corrupts state.
acceptanceCriteria: prd.json read and write functions retry up to 5 times on PermissionError or OSError with errno EACCES/ETXTBSY
Backoff follows: base_delay=0.1s * 2^attempt + random.uniform(0, 0.1) seconds
After all retries fail, the full error is logged to spiral_events.jsonl and re-raised
Retry attempts are logged at DEBUG level with attempt number and delay
Windows-specific errno values (EACCES=13, ETXTBSY=26) are handled alongside POSIX equivalents
technicalNotes: Python errno module: https://docs.python.org/3/library/errno.html
Use tenacity library or implement manually with time.sleep and random.uniform
Test with a mock that raises PermissionError on first N calls then succeeds

archivedStories.title: Add ASCII dependency tree view to `spiral status` subcommand output
archivedStories.description: Extend the `spiral status` subcommand to include an ASCII tree rendering of story dependencies, similar to the Unix `tree` command. This gives users a visual overview of the dependency DAG without needing the full dashboard, making it easy to spot which stories are blocked by pending dependencies directly in the terminal.
acceptanceCriteria: `spiral status --tree` renders a Unicode/ASCII box-drawing tree of story dependencies
Each node shows: story ID, title (truncated to 50 chars), and status icon (checkmark/X/hourglass/circle with slash)
Root nodes (no dependencies) are shown at the top level; dependents are indented
Cyclic dependencies (if any) are shown with a [CYCLE] marker instead of infinite recursion
Output respects SPIRAL_LOG_LEVEL: --quiet shows only IDs, default shows title + status
technicalNotes: Implement tree rendering in a new cli/tree_view.py module using recursive DFS
Use Unicode box-drawing characters for cross-platform terminal output
Fall back to ASCII +-- `-- | when TERM does not support Unicode

archivedStories.title: Emit OTel agentic-system spans for tasks, actions, teams, and artifacts
archivedStories.description: The 2025 OTel GenAI agentic-systems proposal defines span conventions for tasks (trackable units of work), actions (tool calls, LLM queries, API requests), teams (agent groups), and artifacts (prompts, code, embeddings). Instrumenting Spiral's worker loop with these conventions enables end-to-end trace correlation across the full story lifecycle and makes telemetry compatible with CNCF-standard observability backends.
acceptanceCriteria: Each story execution emits a root 'task' span with gen_ai.task.id and gen_ai.task.status attributes
Each LLM call inside a worker emits a child 'action' span tagged with gen_ai.action.type = 'llm_query'
Tool/bash executions inside workers emit 'action' spans with gen_ai.action.type = 'tool_call'
Spans carry W3C traceparent headers so they stitch into a single distributed trace
A smoke test verifies at least one task span and one action span appear in the OTLP export
technicalNotes: See OTel gen-ai-agent-spans spec: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans/
GitHub issue tracking agentic conventions: https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/issues/2664
Span kind CLIENT for cross-process, INTERNAL for same-process agent invocations

archivedStories.title: Pin all GitHub Actions to full commit SHA and enforce via policy
archivedStories.description: Third-party actions pinned to mutable tags (e.g., actions/checkout@v4) are a supply-chain attack vector; a compromised tag can inject malicious code. Pinning to the immutable full 40-character SHA guarantees the exact code that was reviewed is always executed. GitHub's 2025 allowed-actions policy can now enforce SHA pinning org-wide and block unpinned workflows from running.
acceptanceCriteria: All uses of third-party actions in .github/workflows/*.yml are updated to full-length SHA pins with a version comment
A CI job (pinned-actions-check) runs actionlint or a grep-based check that fails if any action ref matches @v[0-9] or @main/master
README documents the process for updating a pinned action to a new release
No first-party actions (actions/checkout, etc.) are exempted without explicit justification
technicalNotes: StepSecurity best practices: https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/github-actions-security-best-practices
GitHub 2025 SHA-pinning enforcement announcement: https://github.blog/changelog/2025-08-15-github-actions-policy-now-supports-blocking-and-sha-pinning-actions/
Use 'actionlint' linter or 'pin-github-action' CLI tool for bulk pinning

archivedStories.title: Replace GitHub Actions long-lived secrets with OIDC short-lived tokens
archivedStories.description: Long-lived API keys stored as GitHub Secrets (e.g., for AWS, GCP, or Anthropic billing) are a persistent credential-leak risk. GitHub Actions OIDC lets cloud providers and services issue short-lived tokens scoped to a single workflow job, automatically expiring after the job ends. This eliminates secret rotation burden and reduces the blast radius of any credential compromise.
acceptanceCriteria: AWS/GCP deploy steps use OIDC role assumption instead of static key secrets where applicable
Workflows that use OIDC have id-token: write in permissions and read-only for all other scopes
Trust policy restricts token issuance to exact repository and branch (no wildcards)
A checklist in .github/SECURITY.md documents which integrations still require static secrets and why
technicalNotes: GitHub OIDC concepts: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/openid-connect
AWS OIDC setup: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/deployment/security-hardening-your-deployments/configuring-openid-connect-in-amazon-web-services
Minimum TTL for OIDC tokens is one workflow job; no explicit revocation needed

archivedStories.title: Replace shell=True subprocess calls with create_subprocess_exec to prevent injection
archivedStories.description: Python worker scripts that pass shell=True (or subprocess.run with a string command) are vulnerable to shell injection if any part of the command is derived from LLM output, story titles, or branch names. Migrating to asyncio.create_subprocess_exec() (or subprocess.run with a list of args) executes commands without a shell interpreter, making injection impossible regardless of input content.
acceptanceCriteria: A grep CI check fails if any Python file in the project contains 'shell=True' without a '# spiral-allow-shell' inline comment
All existing shell=True call sites in worker utilities are migrated to exec-form equivalents
Pipe deadlock prevention: all subprocess calls that capture stdout also capture stderr or use communicate()
Tests cover at least one case with a command argument containing shell-special characters (semicolons, backticks)
technicalNotes: asyncio.create_subprocess_exec docs: https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-subprocess.html
Security rationale: https://runebook.dev/en/docs/python/library/asyncio-eventloop/asyncio.loop.subprocess_shell
Use asyncio.wait_for(proc.communicate(), timeout=N) to prevent pipe deadlocks and hangs

archivedStories.title: Implement explicit prompt cache breakpoints for system prompts and PRD context
archivedStories.description: Claude's prompt caching charges cache reads at 10% of normal input token cost (90% discount) when cache_control breakpoints are explicitly placed at the end of static content. Spiral re-sends the full system prompt and PRD context on every LLM call; adding cache_control: {type: ephemeral} breakpoints after these static sections will dramatically reduce per-story API costs, especially for large PRDs.
acceptanceCriteria: All LLM call sites in Python workers that send system_prompt + prd_context add a cache_control breakpoint after the last static block
Token cost tracking differentiates cache_read_input_tokens from input_tokens in cost calculations
Cache hit rate is logged per story phase (R/D/I/T) and surfaced in the dashboard
An integration test verifies cache_read_input_tokens > 0 on the second call with the same system prompt
Cost savings from caching are included in the per-story cost report
technicalNotes: Claude prompt caching docs: https://platform.claude.ai/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching
Cache TTL is 5 minutes for Claude; batched calls must complete within the TTL window
Place breakpoints after: system prompt, PRD snapshot, story context — before the per-call user message
Gemini context caching requires 32k+ token minimum and explicit cache object creation via API

archivedStories.title: Propagate W3C trace context across worker subprocess boundaries
archivedStories.description: When spiral.sh spawns worker subprocesses (bash or Python), the parent trace context is currently lost, creating disconnected traces in any OTLP backend. Injecting the W3C traceparent/tracestate environment variables into each worker's environment and reading them at startup stitches all spans into a single end-to-end trace per story, making cross-worker debugging practical.
acceptanceCriteria: Parent process writes TRACEPARENT and TRACESTATE env vars before fork/exec of each worker
Worker Python code reads these vars and sets them as the active OTel context on startup
An integration test with a local OTLP collector verifies parent-child span relationship
No regression on existing OTel span tests
technicalNotes: W3C Trace Context spec: https://www.w3.org/TR/trace-context/
OTel context propagation overview: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/context-propagation/
Python opentelemetry-api TraceContextTextMapPropagator can inject/extract from dicts

archivedStories.title: Add stale git lock-file detection and safe cleanup to spiral.sh
archivedStories.description: When a worker is killed mid-operation, git may leave behind a stale .git/index.lock or packed-refs.lock file in the worktree. This causes all subsequent git commands in that worktree to fail with 'Another git process seems to be running', blocking story retries indefinitely. A pre-flight check that detects lock files older than a configurable threshold (default 5 min) and removes them — only after confirming no live git process owns them — prevents this class of stuck worker.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.sh pre-flight phase checks each active worktree for .git/*.lock files
Lock files older than SPIRAL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MINUTES (default 5) are removed after verifying no live git PID holds them
An event is logged to the Spiral audit log whenever a stale lock is removed
Unit test (bats) covers: no lock present, fresh lock (skipped), stale lock (removed), stale lock with live PID (skipped)
technicalNotes: Common pattern: check mtime > threshold AND 'ps aux | grep git' returns no matching PID
Claude Code has known issue with stale index.lock: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/11005
Use 'flock' or 'lsof' to verify ownership before deletion on Linux

archivedStories.title: Migrate CI Python toolchain from pip to uv for 10-100x faster installs
archivedStories.description: GitHub Actions CI currently installs Python dependencies with pip, which is slow and inconsistent across runs due to resolver differences. Replacing it with uv — a Rust-based drop-in replacement — provides 10-100x faster cold installs via parallel downloads and system-wide caching, plus reproducible builds via uv sync --frozen. This directly reduces CI wait time and flakiness from resolver non-determinism.
acceptanceCriteria: All GitHub Actions Python setup steps use 'pip install astral-sh/setup-uv' then 'uv sync --frozen'
A requirements.lock (or uv.lock) file is committed and kept up to date
CI cold install time for Python deps is measured before and after; at least 3x speedup documented
Local dev docs updated to recommend 'uv sync' instead of 'pip install -r requirements.txt'
uv.lock file is validated in CI (uv lock --check) to catch drift
technicalNotes: uv docs: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/
uv vs pip comparison: https://realpython.com/uv-vs-pip/
Use --frozen flag in CI to enforce exact lockfile; use --locked for local dev

archivedStories.title: Add dead-letter queue for permanently failed stories with manual replay command
archivedStories.description: Stories that exhaust all retry attempts currently stay in a terminal 'failed' state with no structured path to recovery. A dead-letter queue (DLQ) pattern moves exhausted stories into a distinct dlq state in prd.json, preventing them from clogging the active queue and making their failure metadata (error type, last attempt timestamp, retry count) queryable. A 'spiral replay --story US-XYZ' command re-enqueues a DLQ story after human review.
acceptanceCriteria: Stories that fail more than SPIRAL_MAX_RETRIES consecutive times transition to 'dlq' state in prd.json
'spiral list --state dlq' shows all dead-lettered stories with failure reason and timestamp
'spiral replay --story <id>' validates the story is in dlq state, resets retry count to 0, and re-enqueues it
DLQ transitions are written to the audit log
Dashboard shows a DLQ badge/count separate from active failures
technicalNotes: DLQ pattern overview: https://dev.to/andreparis/queue-based-exponential-backoff-a-resilient-retry-pattern-for-distributed-systems-37f3
Distinguish transient failures (network, rate-limit) from permanent failures (invalid story, auth error) — only permanent failures go to DLQ immediately
Store last_error_type and last_error_message in the story's DLQ metadata

archivedStories.title: Add self-consistency hallucination check for LLM-generated acceptance criteria
archivedStories.description: When Spiral's Phase D (Design) or Phase R (Research) generates acceptance criteria or implementation plans, the LLM may hallucinate API names, file paths, or library versions that do not exist. A self-consistency check that re-prompts the model with the same input using temperature variation and compares outputs flags divergent claims for human review before implementation begins.
acceptanceCriteria: Phase D runs the design prompt twice with temperature 0.0 and 0.7, then compares JSON outputs
Fields that differ between runs are flagged with a 'low_confidence' marker in prd.json
If more than 20% of acceptance criteria fields are low-confidence, the story is paused and a human-review flag is set
The consistency check cost (second LLM call) is tracked separately in token cost accounting
A --skip-consistency-check flag allows disabling for fast-path small stories
technicalNotes: SelfCheckGPT paper and repo: https://github.com/potsawee/selfcheckgpt
For structured outputs, compare field-by-field rather than full string similarity
Consistency threshold should be configurable via SPIRAL_CONSISTENCY_THRESHOLD env var

archivedStories.title: Enforce least-privilege permissions block on all GitHub Actions workflow jobs
archivedStories.description: Without an explicit permissions block, GitHub Actions grants read/write access to the GITHUB_TOKEN for all scopes, giving any compromised step broad repository write access. Adding a top-level permissions: read-all (or no permissions) block and granting only the scopes each job actually needs (e.g., contents: write only for release jobs) limits the blast radius of a supply-chain compromise.
acceptanceCriteria: Every .github/workflows/*.yml file has a top-level 'permissions: {}' or 'permissions: read-all' block
Jobs that write to the repository (e.g., release, PR creation) have a job-level permissions block granting only contents: write and pull-requests: write
A CI lint step (actionlint) fails if any workflow is missing a permissions block
No workflow uses the default implicit 'write-all' permission
technicalNotes: GitHub permissions reference: https://graphite.com/guides/github-actions-permissions
actionlint checks for missing permissions blocks: https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint
Best practice: set permissions at workflow level to read-all, then override at job level for write needs

archivedStories.title: Add asyncio timeout and communicate() deadlock prevention to all worker subprocess calls
archivedStories.description: Python worker scripts that use proc.wait() or proc.stdout.read() on subprocesses with large output risk deadlocking when the OS pipe buffer fills — the subprocess blocks on write while the parent blocks on wait. Using proc.communicate() (which drains pipes concurrently) wrapped in asyncio.wait_for() with a hard timeout prevents both deadlocks and hung workers that never terminate.
acceptanceCriteria: All asyncio subprocess calls in Python workers use 'await asyncio.wait_for(proc.communicate(), timeout=SPIRAL_SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT)' instead of proc.wait()
SPIRAL_SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT defaults to 300s and is configurable via environment variable
TimeoutExpired exceptions are caught and result in a worker 'timeout' failure state (distinct from 'error')
A test spawns a subprocess that writes 10 MB to stdout and verifies no deadlock occurs
Subprocess timeout events are logged with the command prefix and timeout value for debugging
technicalNotes: asyncio subprocess deadlock explanation: https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-subprocess.html
Pattern: output, err = await asyncio.wait_for(proc.communicate(), timeout=300)
After TimeoutExpired, call proc.kill() then await proc.communicate() to drain and avoid zombie

archivedStories.title: Add worktree health audit command that detects and reports all anomalies
archivedStories.description: In long-running Spiral sessions, worktrees accumulate inconsistent states: detached HEADs, branches checked out in multiple worktrees (violating git's safety constraint), stale lock files, and worktrees whose branch has been merged/deleted. A 'spiral worktree audit' command that enumerates all worktrees and reports each anomaly type gives operators a single actionable view before starting a new iteration.
acceptanceCriteria: 'spiral worktree audit' exits non-zero and prints a structured report if any anomaly is found
Detected anomaly types: stale locks, detached HEAD, missing branch, duplicate branch checkout, worktree directory missing from disk
Report includes remediation suggestion for each anomaly type (e.g., 'run spiral worktree prune')
A --fix flag auto-resolves safe anomalies (prune missing, remove stale locks) and leaves unsafe ones for human action
Audit output is machine-parseable JSON when --json flag is passed
technicalNotes: git worktree list --porcelain provides machine-readable worktree state
git worktree best practices: https://www.kenmuse.com/blog/using-git-worktrees-for-concurrent-development/
OpenAI Codex uses worktrees for parallel agents: https://developers.openai.com/codex/app/worktrees

archivedStories.title: Emit gen_ai.usage.* metric counters for token consumption per story phase
archivedStories.description: The OTel GenAI metrics spec defines gen_ai.client.token.usage (histogram), gen_ai.client.operation.duration, and gen_ai.server.request.duration as standard metric instruments. Emitting these from every LLM call allows aggregating per-phase token burn (Research, Design, Implement, Test) in any OTLP-compatible metrics backend (Prometheus, Datadog, Grafana Cloud) without custom parsing of log lines.
acceptanceCriteria: Every LLM API call records gen_ai.client.token.usage with attributes: gen_ai.operation.name, gen_ai.system, gen_ai.request.model, spiral.story.phase
gen_ai.client.operation.duration histogram is recorded per call in milliseconds
Metrics are exported via the existing OTLP exporter alongside traces
A Prometheus scrape test verifies the metric names and at least one non-zero sample
Dashboard can display token usage by phase using these metrics
technicalNotes: OTel GenAI metrics spec: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-metrics/
Use opentelemetry-sdk Meter.create_histogram() for token counts
Add spiral.story.id and spiral.story.phase as extra attributes beyond the standard semconv set

archivedStories.title: Implement idempotent tool execution with per-story undo stack
archivedStories.description: Each phase action in ralph.sh should be idempotent so re-running after a partial failure produces the same result. An undo stack records reversible operations (file writes, git commits) before executing them, so a failed story can cleanly roll back to a known-good state instead of leaving partially applied changes.
acceptanceCriteria: ralph.sh records each destructive operation (file write, git commit, branch create) to a per-story undo log before executing it
A 'spiral undo STORY_ID' command replays the undo log in reverse, restoring the worktree to pre-attempt state
Re-running a previously failed story does not double-apply file changes or create duplicate commits
Undo log is stored in the worktree at .spiral/undo/STORY_ID.jsonl and cleaned up on successful merge
A bats test verifies that a simulated mid-story failure leaves the worktree cleanly restorable via the undo log
technicalNotes: Pattern: 'agent undo stacks and transaction components that encapsulate complex logic into atomic, reversible units' (InsightFinder, 2025)
Use git stash or patch files as the undo payload for file-level changes; record git SHA before commit for git-level undo
Undo log format: JSONL with {operation, target, inverse_command, timestamp}

archivedStories.title: Add flaky bats test detection and quarantine registry
archivedStories.description: Bats tests that fail intermittently block the Gate phase without distinction from real regressions. A quarantine registry tracks per-test pass/fail history across runs; tests exceeding a flakiness threshold are automatically quarantined so they no longer block the gate while remaining visible for monitoring and eventual fix.
acceptanceCriteria: A JSON registry (.spiral/flaky-tests.json) records per-test pass/fail counts across the last N gate runs (default N=20)
Tests with a flakiness ratio above SPIRAL_FLAKY_THRESHOLD (default 0.3) are marked quarantined
Quarantined tests still execute but their failure does not cause the Gate phase to fail
A 'spiral flaky-tests report' command prints all quarantined tests with their current failure rates
Quarantine is automatically lifted when a test achieves 10 consecutive passes
technicalNotes: Detection approach: retry-based (re-run failing test in same invocation) combined with historical scoring across runs (Atlassian Flakinator pattern, 2025)
Storage: .spiral/flaky-tests.json keyed by test name with {passes, failures, quarantined, lastSeen} fields
Threshold and window size configurable via SPIRAL_FLAKY_THRESHOLD and SPIRAL_FLAKY_WINDOW env vars

archivedStories.title: Implement observation masking for ralph.sh context window management
archivedStories.description: As worker loops accumulate large conversation histories, LLM context costs escalate and performance degrades. Observation masking replaces older phase outputs with compact placeholders while retaining the most recent N turns in full, reducing token usage by up to 52% without sacrificing task performance.
acceptanceCriteria: ralph.sh tracks a rolling window of the last 10 phase outputs passed to the LLM (configurable via SPIRAL_CONTEXT_WINDOW)
Phase outputs older than the window are replaced with a one-line summary placeholder before being sent to the LLM
The LLM is informed of masking via a system prompt note: 'earlier phase outputs omitted for brevity'
Token count before and after masking is logged to the iteration summary under _contextStats
Masking achieves at least 40% token reduction on stories with more than 5 completed phases
technicalNotes: JetBrains Research (2025): keeping latest 10 turns gave best balance; masking achieved 52% cost reduction vs full history
Do NOT summarize old turns (adds 7% cost overhead and 13-15% longer runs per JetBrains study); replace with single-line placeholder
Implement in ralph.sh as a bash function that truncates the context array before each LLM call

archivedStories.title: Add policy adherence validation gate before high-risk phase actions
archivedStories.description: Research shows agents can achieve perfect tool sequencing while violating safety policies. Before ralph.sh executes high-risk actions (git push, merge, file deletion), a lightweight policy-lookup step checks the action against a configurable allow-list and logs a policy verdict, creating an explicit safety layer separate from LLM instruction following.
acceptanceCriteria: A .spiral/policy.json file defines allowed and forbidden operations per phase (R, I, V, M)
ralph.sh checks the policy file before executing any destructive operation; forbidden operations are logged and skipped
Policy violations are reported in the checkpoint with a dedicated _policyViolations array field
A bats test verifies that a worker attempting a forbidden operation has it blocked and recorded
Policy file ships with safe defaults that can be overridden per project
technicalNotes: Four-pillar framework finding: 'policy non-compliance before executing actions' is a distinct and common agent failure mode (arxiv 2512.12791, 2025)
Keep policy checks in bash (not LLM) to make enforcement deterministic and auditable
Policy file format: {phase: {allow: [patterns], deny: [patterns]}}

archivedStories.title: Add permission-scoped command allow-list for worker terminal commands
archivedStories.description: Workers currently have unrestricted shell access within their worktree, allowing accidental or LLM-hallucinated destructive commands. A configurable allow-list of permitted commands per phase prevents unauthorized operations without requiring human approval for routine work.
acceptanceCriteria: A .spiral/command-allowlist.json file maps each phase (R, I, V, M) to a list of permitted command prefixes
ralph.sh intercepts shell commands extracted from LLM output and checks them against the phase allow-list before execution
Commands not on the allow-list are logged as blocked and the LLM is informed with a structured error message
The allow-list ships with safe defaults: Phase R (curl, python, cat, ls, jq), Phase I (file ops, git add/commit), Phase V (bats, pytest), Phase M (git merge)
A bats test verifies a blocked command is not executed and is logged to .spiral/security-events.log
technicalNotes: From martinfowler.com: 'a carefully curated allow-list of terminal commands' is a concrete safety pattern for autonomous code generation agents
Block dangerous patterns by default: 'git push --force', 'rm -rf /', 'git reset --hard' unless explicitly allow-listed
Log blocked commands to .spiral/security-events.log with timestamp, workerId, and full command attempted

archivedStories.title: Enforce diagnosis-before-action block in Phase I before code modification
archivedStories.description: A key finding from agentic reliability research is that agents skip diagnostic steps before remediation, leading to incorrect fixes. Phase I workers should be required to output a structured diagnosis block before any code modification, making reasoning explicit and verifiable.
acceptanceCriteria: The Phase I system prompt requires workers to output a diagnosis block before any file edits: {currentState, problemIdentified, plannedChanges}
ralph.sh validates the presence of a diagnosis block in Phase I output before proceeding to execute changes
Missing diagnosis block causes Phase I to re-prompt: 'Diagnosis block required before making changes. Please output your diagnosis first.'
Diagnosis blocks are stored in the checkpoint under _phaseI.diagnosisBlock
A bats test verifies that Phase I output without a diagnosis block triggers re-prompt and does not execute changes
technicalNotes: Tools pillar finding: 'skipped diagnostic steps before remediation' is the highest-frequency tool failure pattern in complex agent scenarios (arxiv 2512.12791)
Pattern: 'enforce diagnostic-before-action patterns; implement DAG-based task dependencies'
Diagnosis block format: require specific section headers (## Current State, ## Problem, ## Planned Changes) for reliable parsing

archivedStories.title: Launch workers in dedicated process groups for targeted crash cleanup
archivedStories.description: When a worker crashes, spiral.sh currently risks killing sibling workers by targeting all background jobs. Launching each worker with setsid to create its own process group enables surgical kill-by-PGID, ensuring only the crashed worker and its descendants are cleaned up.
acceptanceCriteria: Each worker is launched with setsid so it leads its own process group
On worker crash detection, spiral.sh kills only the crashed worker's process group: kill -- -PGID
A worker crash is detected within 5 seconds and logged to progress.txt without interrupting running sibling workers
After a worker crash, its worktree is inspected for corrupted shared resources and cleaned before the next retry
A bats test simulates a worker crash (SIGKILL to a worker PID) and verifies sibling workers continue and crash is logged
technicalNotes: Vellum 2025: 'faults in one agent don't cascade to others; specialized agents with limited scope reduce complexity'
QCon SF 2025: 'timeouts and circuit breakers for each parallel branch prevent one slow/failing agent from blocking the entire process'
Use setsid (POSIX) rather than cgroups for portability across Linux and macOS environments

archivedStories.title: Implement shared-fetch optimization for parallel worker git worktrees
archivedStories.description: Each worker currently fetches from origin independently, creating redundant network transfers proportional to the number of parallel workers. Since all worktrees share one object database, a single coordinated fetch in the main repo satisfies all workers simultaneously, reducing total fetch time from O(N*12s) to O(1.3s) for 10 workers.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.sh performs a single 'git fetch origin' in the main repo before launching workers
Workers do not independently fetch; they use 'git reset --hard origin/main' against already-fetched objects
A timing log entry records pre-launch fetch duration vs. estimated per-worker fetch total
With 5+ parallel workers, total fetch time is reduced by at least 50% compared to per-worker fetches
A bats test verifies that only one network fetch event occurs in the git trace log when multiple workers start
technicalNotes: Shared object database: 'a single fetch operation in any worktree synchronizes objects for all worktrees, eliminating redundant network transfers' (gitcheatsheet.dev)
Benchmark reported: 12s sequential per-worktree fetch → 1.3s shared fetch across 10 worktrees
CPU-bound git ops can be parallelized; network ops should be limited to a single shared fetch

archivedStories.title: Add git diff-index fast-path before full worktree status checks
archivedStories.description: spiral.sh runs full git status on all worktrees at startup and during gate checks, costing ~80ms per worktree. Replacing this with a lightweight git diff-index --quiet HEAD check (~15ms) as a pre-screen reduces total status check time by up to 81% when most worktrees are clean.
acceptanceCriteria: The worktree status check function uses 'git diff-index --quiet HEAD' as a fast pre-check before running full 'git status'
Full status is only run on worktrees where diff-index reports uncommitted changes
The optimization is logged: 'Skipped full status on N/M worktrees (clean)'
With 10 worktrees and 2 dirty, total check time is under 200ms (benchmark baseline: ~800ms)
A bats test verifies the fast path is taken for clean worktrees and full status for dirty ones
technicalNotes: From gitcheatsheet.dev: selective approach reduces total time from ~800ms to ~150ms for 10 worktrees when only 2 contain changes (81% reduction)
diff-index ~15ms vs. full status ~80ms per worktree
Apply same fast-path pattern to the dirty-worktree detection logic at startup

archivedStories.title: Implement retrieval completeness check before memory-dependent decisions
archivedStories.description: When workers query prd.json or checkpoint state to make decisions, incomplete retrieval can cause the agent to act on stale or partial information. A completeness check verifies retrieved context satisfies minimum coverage requirements before the LLM proceeds, catching truncated reads and missing fields early.
acceptanceCriteria: Before Phase I begins, ralph.sh verifies the research output contains content for all acceptanceCriteria fields of the story
Before resuming from checkpoint, spiral.sh verifies the checkpoint contains all required state fields (phase, storyId, retryCount)
Incomplete retrieval triggers a re-fetch/re-read with an error logged to progress.txt
After 3 failed completeness checks for the same context, the story is marked blocked with reason 'incomplete_context'
A bats test verifies a truncated checkpoint triggers re-read before resuming
technicalNotes: Memory pillar failure: 'low recall despite high precision (13.1% recall, 30% precision)' — agents act on incomplete context (arxiv 2512.12791)
Mitigation: 'add retrieval coverage checks before decisions'
Coverage check: for prd.json story fields, verify title + description + acceptanceCriteria all non-empty and non-null

archivedStories.title: Enforce cgroups v2 memory and CPU limits on worker subprocesses
archivedStories.description: Each ralph.sh worker subprocess currently runs unconstrained, allowing a single runaway LLM call or compilation step to exhaust host memory and OOM-kill unrelated workers. Using Linux cgroups v2, assign a per-worker memory.max and cpu.max slice so that individual worker failure is contained and does not cascade. This pairs with the existing OOM-prevention heap caps by adding a kernel-enforced hard boundary.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.sh creates a named cgroup slice under /sys/fs/cgroup/spiral/ for each worker before exec
Each worker cgroup has memory.max set to SPIRAL_WORKER_MEM_LIMIT_MB (default 2048 MB) and cpu.max set to SPIRAL_WORKER_CPU_QUOTA (default 80%)
When a worker exceeds its memory.max, the kernel OOM-kills only that worker's cgroup; other workers continue unaffected
spiral.sh cleans up the cgroup slice on worker exit or crash via a trap
SPIRAL_WORKER_MEM_LIMIT_MB and SPIRAL_WORKER_CPU_QUOTA are documented in .env.example
Falls back gracefully with a warning log when cgroups v2 is unavailable (e.g., macOS or older kernels)
technicalNotes: Use cgcreate/cgexec from libcgroup-tools, or write directly to /sys/fs/cgroup/spiral/<worker-id>/
cgroups v2 unified hierarchy: memory.max (hard), memory.high (soft reclaim), cpu.max (quota/period)
Check availability with: [ -f /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.controllers ] && grep -q memory /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.controllers
Reference: https://kindatechnical.com/operating-systems/lesson-98-cgroups-v2.html

archivedStories.title: Add story drift detection by diffing implementation against acceptance criteria
archivedStories.description: After Phase I (Implementation), the code written by the worker may silently diverge from the story's acceptanceCriteria — implementing a different interface, omitting edge cases, or gold-plating out-of-scope features. A post-implementation drift check uses an LLM to compare the git diff of the worktree against the story's acceptanceCriteria and flags specific deviations before Phase V (Validation), reducing wasted validation cycles and misaligned merges.
acceptanceCriteria: After Phase I completes, spiral.sh runs a drift-check step that sends the story's acceptanceCriteria and the git diff to the configured LLM
The LLM returns a structured JSON response: { driftScore: 0-100, missingCriteria: [], scopeCreep: [], verdict: 'pass'|'warn'|'fail' }
A driftScore >= 70 is 'pass', 40-69 is 'warn' (proceeds with annotation), < 40 is 'fail' (worker is paused for human review)
Drift report is written to .spiral/workers/<worker-id>/drift_report.json
The spiral status command shows a drift indicator column (green/yellow/red) per story
Drift threshold values are configurable via SPIRAL_DRIFT_PASS_THRESHOLD and SPIRAL_DRIFT_FAIL_THRESHOLD env vars
technicalNotes: Use git diff HEAD~1 within the worktree, or compare against the branch point from main
Prompt engineering: present each acceptance criterion as a numbered checklist; ask LLM to tick each one as met/partial/absent
Industry data: AI-generated code contains 1.7x more defects than human-written; drift detection is the primary mitigation
Reference spec-driven drift detection: https://www.javacodegeeks.com/2026/03/spec-driven-developmentwith-ai-coding-agents-the-workflow-replacingprompt-and-pray.html

archivedStories.title: Implement local Ollama model fallback with cold-start pre-warm and explicit policy flags
archivedStories.description: When Claude or Gemini API calls fail due to rate limits or network issues, SPIRAL workers silently stall or abort. Adding an Ollama-backed fallback tier with an explicit SPIRAL_LOCAL_FALLBACK_POLICY (allow|deny|local-only) ensures workers continue on local models when permitted, and fail loudly with a clear error when the policy forbids cloud fallback — preventing silent data leakage and cold-start timeouts that cause false failures.
acceptanceCriteria: SPIRAL_LOCAL_FALLBACK_POLICY env var accepts 'allow' (try local on cloud failure), 'deny' (fail with error, no fallback), 'local-only' (never use cloud)
When policy is 'allow' and a cloud API call fails, worker retries the same prompt against SPIRAL_OLLAMA_BASE_URL with SPIRAL_OLLAMA_MODEL
Ollama model is pre-warmed via a GET request to SPIRAL_OLLAMA_BASE_URL/api/tags at worker startup; if model is absent, worker logs a warning but does not abort
Fallback events are logged as structured JSON in spiral_events.jsonl with reason, model_used, and original_error fields
When policy is 'deny' and cloud fails, worker exits with code 2 and prints 'LOCAL_FALLBACK_DENIED: <reason>' — never silently reroutes
A bats test simulates cloud failure by mocking the API endpoint and verifies the correct fallback behavior for each policy value
technicalNotes: Ollama cold-start: models take ~13 seconds to load on first request — pre-warm with GET /api/tags at startup
Tool-calling reliability is limited in open models; restrict local fallback to Phase R (research/summarisation) by default
SPIRAL_OLLAMA_BASE_URL defaults to http://localhost:11434; SPIRAL_OLLAMA_MODEL defaults to 'llama3.2'
Reference: https://medium.com/@rosgluk/local-llm-hosting-complete-2025-guide-ollama-vllm-localai-jan-lm-studio-more-f98136ce7e4a

archivedStories.title: Run Semgrep SAST scan on AI-generated code as a mandatory Gate phase check
