archivedStories.description: AI-generated code contains 1.7x more defects than human-written code and may introduce OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities such as injection, hardcoded secrets, and path traversal. Adding a Semgrep SAST scan as a blocking step in the Gate (G) phase ensures every AI-authored commit is checked for known vulnerability patterns before merge, with actionable findings reported directly to the story in prd.json.
acceptanceCriteria: Phase G runs 'semgrep scan --config auto --json' scoped to the files changed in the story branch (via git diff --name-only origin/main)
If Semgrep returns severity HIGH or CRITICAL findings, the Gate fails and the story is moved to status 'blocked-by-sast'
MEDIUM findings generate a warning annotation in prd.json under _sast_warnings but do not block merge
Semgrep results are written to .spiral/gate-reports/<story-id>_sast.json
The spiral status command shows a SAST column with pass/warn/fail per story
SPIRAL_SAST_ENABLED=false env var disables the check for development environments
A bats test asserts that a story with a planted SQL injection pattern in its diff fails the Gate
technicalNotes: Semgrep CLI: https://semgrep.dev — install via 'pip install semgrep'
Parse results.findings[].severity for HIGH/CRITICAL detection from JSON output
Restrict scan to git diff files only: 'git diff --name-only origin/main' piped as include list to semgrep
Reference: https://corgea.com/blog/the-best-ai-powered-sast-in-2025

archivedStories.title: Add prd.json schema validation using JSON Schema draft 2020-12 on every write
archivedStories.description: prd.json is mutated by multiple workers, scripts, and manual edits without schema validation, making it possible to introduce malformed stories that crash downstream phases silently. A schema validator using JSON Schema draft 2020-12 validates every write to prd.json, surfacing field-level errors with exact JSON Pointer paths so operators know precisely what is wrong and where.
acceptanceCriteria: A prd_schema.json file defines the full JSON Schema draft 2020-12 specification for prd.json including all story fields, required fields, and enum values
spiral.sh runs schema validation before and after every prd.json write operation using Python jsonschema
Validation errors are printed as 'SCHEMA ERROR: <jsonpointer> — <message>' and abort the write, restoring the previous file from prd.json.bak
The schema enforces: title (string, maxLength 80), priority (enum critical|high|medium|low), status (enum), estimatedComplexity (enum small|medium|large), acceptanceCriteria (array, minItems 1)
A pre-commit hook runs the same validation on staged prd.json changes
A bats test asserts that writing a story with an invalid priority value is rejected with the correct error message including the JSON Pointer path
technicalNotes: Python jsonschema library (pip install jsonschema[format]) supports draft 2020-12
JSON Schema spec: https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-validation
JSON Pointer in error messages (e.g., /stories/3/priority) pinpoints the offending field
Backup prd.json to prd.json.bak before each write; restore on validation failure

archivedStories.title: Add env var schema validation at SPIRAL startup with actionable missing-var errors
archivedStories.description: SPIRAL currently discovers missing environment variables mid-run, producing cryptic errors such as 'NoneType has no attribute strip' when an API key is absent. A startup validation step checks all required and optional env vars against a schema, prints a colour-coded table of missing or invalid vars with their purpose and a concrete fix command, and exits immediately — turning a 30-minute debugging session into a 10-second fix.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.sh runs a validate_env() function as the very first step before any worker is launched
A machine-readable env_schema.json lists every env var with: name, required (bool), type (string/int/url/bool), default, description, and fix_hint
Missing required vars print: 'MISSING [VAR_NAME]: <description>. Fix: export VAR_NAME=<example>'
Invalid values (e.g., non-URL string in OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT) print: 'INVALID [VAR_NAME]: expected URL, got "foo"'
Validation prints a summary table and exits with code 1 if any required var is missing; warns but continues if optional vars are absent
A bats test unsets a required var and verifies the error message contains the var name, a description, and a fix hint
technicalNotes: 12-factor app: store config in environment variables; validate at startup before first IO — https://12factor.net/config
Use Python pydantic BaseSettings v2 or manual bash validation with regex for URL/int types
Color output: red for missing required, yellow for missing optional, green for all-present (using tput or ANSI codes)
env_schema.json also serves as living documentation of all SPIRAL configuration surface

archivedStories.title: Enforce shell=False and per-phase command allowlist in all worker subprocess calls
archivedStories.description: Worker scripts call subprocess with shell=True in several places, exposing SPIRAL to command injection if an LLM-generated string is interpolated into a shell command. Enforcing shell=False with list-form arguments and validating every dynamically-constructed command against a per-phase allowlist before exec closes this injection surface without breaking existing functionality.
acceptanceCriteria: A grep/audit of all Python files finds zero occurrences of 'subprocess' with 'shell=True' after this change
All subprocess calls pass commands as lists (e.g., ['git', 'commit', '-m', msg]) not concatenated strings
A PHASE_COMMAND_ALLOWLIST dict in worker config defines permitted executables per phase; Phase I allows ['git', 'python', 'node', 'npm'] but not ['curl', 'wget', 'bash', 'sh']
Any attempt to execute a command not in the allowlist raises SubprocessPolicyViolation and logs the blocked command with timestamp to security-audit.jsonl
A unit test asserts that a shell metacharacter (';', '|', '$()') in a subprocess argument is passed as a literal string, not interpreted by the shell
A bats integration test verifies that an LLM-generated string containing '$(rm -rf /)' as an argument does not execute the injection
technicalNotes: OpenStack subprocess security guide: https://security.openstack.org/guidelines/dg_use-subprocess-securely.html
Primary rule: never use shell=True with any user/LLM-controlled input
Use shlex.split() only for developer-controlled config strings, never for LLM output
Reference: https://securecodingpractices.com/prevent-command-injection-python-subprocess/

archivedStories.title: Pin all GitHub Actions third-party steps to immutable full commit SHAs
archivedStories.description: SPIRAL's CI workflows reference third-party actions by mutable version tags such as actions/checkout@v4, which are vulnerable to tag-mutation supply-chain attacks where a compromised tag silently replaces the action with malicious code. Pinning every third-party action to its immutable 40-character commit SHA and adding a CI check that rejects any non-SHA reference closes this attack surface per GitHub's own security hardening guidance.
acceptanceCriteria: All workflow YAML files in .github/workflows/ reference third-party actions as 'owner/repo@<40-char SHA>' with an inline comment showing the human-readable version
A new workflow job 'check-action-pins' runs on every PR and fails if any 'uses:' line references a tag or branch instead of a 40-character hex SHA
The check pattern: grep -E 'uses:\s+[^#]+@(?![0-9a-f]{40})' fails the job on any match
Dependabot or a scheduled weekly workflow opens automated PRs to update SHA pins when new action releases are published
A CODEOWNERS rule assigns a designated security reviewer as required approver for any .github/workflows/ change
The check is documented in CONTRIBUTING.md with the rationale and instructions for updating pins
technicalNotes: GitHub security hardening guide: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use
StepSecurity harden-runner can auto-pin actions: https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/github-actions-security-best-practices
Wiz supply-chain attack analysis via mutable action tags: https://www.wiz.io/blog/github-actions-security-guide
Format: 'uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2'

archivedStories.title: Stream ralph.sh worker stdout to spiral_dashboard via Server-Sent Events
archivedStories.description: Pipe real-time worker output from ralph.sh subprocess stdout into the spiral_dashboard via Server-Sent Events (SSE) so operators can watch live implementation progress without tailing log files. Each SSE event carries the story ID, worker index, and a line of output.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/worker-stream/{worker_id} returns an SSE stream (Content-Type: text/event-stream)
Dashboard UI shows a live console panel per active worker, auto-scrolling to latest line
Stream ends with a final event {type: 'done', status: 'passed'|'failed'} when worker exits
Both stdout and stderr are interleaved in the stream using asyncio.create_task to prevent deadlock
When no active worker matches worker_id, endpoint returns HTTP 404 immediately
technicalNotes: Use asyncio.create_subprocess_exec with stdout=PIPE and stderr=PIPE; read both streams concurrently via asyncio.create_task to prevent OS pipe buffer deadlock
SSE format: 'data: {json}\n\n' per event; client reconnects with Last-Event-ID on disconnect
asyncio.StreamReader.readline() is non-blocking and safe for streaming; do not use process.communicate() which buffers everything
Reference: https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-subprocess.html

archivedStories.title: Block worker outbound network access during Phase I using network namespace isolation
archivedStories.description: Isolate each ralph.sh worker's network access during implementation to prevent AI-generated code from exfiltrating secrets, making unauthorized API calls, or introducing supply chain attacks. When SPIRAL_WORKER_NETWORK_ISOLATION=true, workers run in a restricted network namespace that blocks all outbound connections except to localhost.
acceptanceCriteria: When SPIRAL_WORKER_NETWORK_ISOLATION=true, ralph.sh is launched via 'unshare --net' (Linux) or equivalent
Worker can still read/write local filesystem; outbound HTTP from within a worker results in connection refused
Network isolation is skipped on Windows/macOS with a warning logged to spiral_events.jsonl
SPIRAL_WORKER_NETWORK_ISOLATION=false is the default to preserve backward compatibility
spiral-doctor checks whether 'unshare' binary is available and reports capability status
technicalNotes: Linux: 'unshare --net --fork -- bash ralph.sh' creates a new network namespace; loopback only by default
Namespaces are a visibility wall, not a full security boundary — combine with seccomp profiles for defense in depth
Docker --network none achieves equivalent isolation when workers run in containers
Reference: https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/container-security-fundamentals-part-2/

archivedStories.title: Capture worker crash tracebacks and persist to .spiral/crashes/ directory
archivedStories.description: When ralph.sh exits with a non-zero code, capture the full stderr output (including Python tracebacks) and write it to a timestamped file in .spiral/crashes/. Maintain a crash index JSON file so spiral-doctor and the dashboard can surface crash history without scanning file contents.
acceptanceCriteria: Any ralph.sh exit with code != 0 writes stderr to .spiral/crashes/{story_id}_{timestamp}.txt
.spiral/crashes/index.json is updated with {story_id, timestamp, exit_code, worker_id, crash_file} per crash
Crash files older than SPIRAL_CRASH_RETENTION_DAYS (default: 7) are pruned on startup
spiral-doctor reports the N most recent crashes from index.json
Dashboard shows crash count badge on worker cards when crash history is non-empty
Crash directory is added to .gitignore (not committed)
technicalNotes: In bash: capture stderr with 2>.spiral/crashes/${story_id}_${ts}.txt alongside the ralph invocation using tee
Crash index must be updated atomically using a temp-file rename to prevent corruption under parallel workers
Retain only last SPIRAL_CRASH_RETENTION_DAYS days of crash files to prevent unbounded disk growth
Reference: https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-subprocess.html

archivedStories.title: Inject unified diff of filesTouch files as context into ralph.sh instead of full files
archivedStories.description: Reduce ralph.sh context window usage by injecting a unified git diff of the filesTouch paths (last N commits) rather than full file contents. For large codebases, this can reduce context size by 60-80% while providing the precise delta the model needs to understand recent changes.
acceptanceCriteria: ralph.sh computes 'git diff HEAD~3 -- ${filesTouch[@]}' and injects the output into the story context block
Full file contents are still injected when the diff is empty (new files) or when filesTouch is absent
Context injection mode is controlled by SPIRAL_CONTEXT_MODE=diff|full (default: diff)
Diff is truncated at SPIRAL_MAX_DIFF_LINES (default: 500 lines) with a truncation notice if exceeded
Unit test verifies that diff context is smaller than full-file context for a modified file with known content
technicalNotes: Use 'git diff --unified=5 HEAD~${SPIRAL_DIFF_DEPTH:-3} -- <files>' for context-rich diffs
For new files, 'git show HEAD:<file>' provides the full content as a fallback
Combined with the existing max-diff-size guard, this prevents context overflow from large refactors
Reference: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff — unified diff format

archivedStories.title: Auto-tag prd.json stories with affected module names derived from filesTouch field
archivedStories.description: When a story has a filesTouch field populated, automatically derive module-level tags by extracting top-level directory prefixes from the file paths and appending them to the story's tags array. This enables --focus-tags filtering without requiring manual tagging.
acceptanceCriteria: populate_hints.py or merge_stories.py extracts unique directory prefixes (depth 1-2) from filesTouch entries
Derived tags are prefixed with 'module:' to distinguish them from user-supplied tags (e.g., 'module:lib', 'module:ralph')
Auto-tags are appended to the existing tags array without duplicating manually set tags
Stories with no filesTouch field are not modified
Unit test verifies that filesTouch: ['lib/phases/phase_r.sh', 'lib/merge_stories.py'] produces tags: ['module:lib']
technicalNotes: Use pathlib.PurePosixPath to extract the top-level directory consistently across platforms
Limit depth to first two path components to avoid overly granular tags
Auto-tagging runs as a post-process step after merge, not during Phase R — no LLM calls required
Connects to existing story tags field and --focus-tags CLI filter already implemented

archivedStories.title: Add `spiral config export-env` command to export spiral.config.sh as .env file
archivedStories.description: Add a `spiral config export-env` subcommand that reads spiral.config.sh, extracts all SPIRAL_* variable assignments, and writes them to a .env file. This enables CI/CD pipelines and Docker containers to load SPIRAL configuration without bash sourcing, following 12-factor app methodology.
acceptanceCriteria: 'spiral config export-env' writes a .env file with one SPIRAL_* variable per line in KEY=VALUE format
Output file defaults to .spiral/.env; overridden with --output flag
Sensitive values (containing TOKEN, KEY, SECRET in the variable name) are masked with *** in stdout preview but written in full to the output file
Generated .env is valid for use with 'docker run --env-file' and GitHub Actions env-file syntax
Command warns if spiral.config.sh contains dynamic bash expressions that cannot be statically extracted
technicalNotes: Parse spiral.config.sh with regex: '^\s*export\s+(SPIRAL_[A-Z_]+)=(.*)$' to extract variable assignments
Handle quoted values: strip surrounding single/double quotes from extracted values
GitHub Actions env-file format is identical to Docker --env-file: KEY=VALUE with no 'export' keyword
Reference: 12-factor app config methodology — https://12factor.net/config

archivedStories.title: Centralize model selection in lib/llm_router.py with tier-based routing
archivedStories.description: Create a dedicated Python module `lib/llm_router.py` that encapsulates model selection logic into Utility (haiku), Production (sonnet), and Frontier (opus) tiers. This consolidates ad-hoc model selection scattered across spiral.sh, ralph.sh, and config into a single, testable routing layer with heuristic scoring.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/llm_router.py exists and exports ModelTier enum and LlmRouter class
LlmRouter.route(story) returns a model ID string based on estimatedComplexity, retry_count, and SPIRAL_MODEL_ROUTING config
Unit tests cover all tier transitions and config override cases
ralph.sh can query routing decision via: uv run python lib/llm_router.py --story US-123
technicalNotes: Use Python dataclass for TaskContext with fields: complexity, retry_count, token_estimate, dependency_count
Tier mapping: small+retry0=haiku, medium+retry0=sonnet, large+retry0=sonnet, any+retry>=2=opus
Expose CLI: uv run python lib/llm_router.py --story US-123 prints routing decision as JSON

archivedStories.title: Context-window-aware model upgrade when story prompt exceeds safe token limit
archivedStories.description: Before dispatching a story to ralph.sh, estimate the total prompt token count (system prompt + PRD context + story + filesTouch contents). If the estimate exceeds the target model's context window safety margin, automatically upgrade to the next model tier to prevent silent truncation and hallucinated implementations.
acceptanceCriteria: Token estimation runs before each ralph.sh invocation in Phase I
If estimated tokens > model_context_limit * SPIRAL_CONTEXT_WINDOW_MARGIN, model is upgraded one tier
Upgrade decision is logged to spiral_events.jsonl with estimated_tokens and chosen_model fields
SPIRAL_CONTEXT_WINDOW_MARGIN env var configures the safety margin (default: 0.85)
Estimation uses 4-chars-per-token approximation when tiktoken is unavailable
technicalNotes: Use tiktoken cl100k_base encoding if available; fall back to len(text)//4
Context limit constants in lib/llm_router.py: haiku=200000, sonnet=200000, opus=200000
Log structured event: {event: context_window_upgrade, from_model, to_model, estimated_tokens}

archivedStories.title: Make model escalation retry thresholds configurable via SPIRAL_ESCALATION_RETRY_*
archivedStories.description: The current model escalation logic (retry 0→haiku, retry 1→sonnet, retry 2→opus) is hardcoded in spiral.sh. Extract these thresholds into env vars so users can tune escalation aggressiveness to match their cost/quality preferences.
acceptanceCriteria: SPIRAL_ESCALATION_RETRY_SONNET (default: 1) controls the retry count at which escalation to sonnet triggers
SPIRAL_ESCALATION_RETRY_OPUS (default: 2) controls the retry count for opus escalation
Setting SPIRAL_ESCALATION_RETRY_SONNET=0 forces sonnet as the starting model for all stories
Startup validation rejects configs where SPIRAL_ESCALATION_RETRY_OPUS < SPIRAL_ESCALATION_RETRY_SONNET with an actionable error
Both vars are documented with defaults in spiral.config.example.sh
technicalNotes: Modify model_routing_auto() function in spiral.sh to read these vars
Guard: SPIRAL_ESCALATION_RETRY_OPUS must be >= SPIRAL_ESCALATION_RETRY_SONNET
--preset flag integration: economy sets both to 99 (never escalate), quality sets both to 0 (always use best)

archivedStories.title: Phase 0 tech stack auto-detection to pre-fill wizard configuration defaults
archivedStories.description: During Phase 0 (Clarify) wizard initialization, scan the project root to detect the language, test framework, and package manager in use. Use detected values as smart defaults in wizard prompts, reducing required user input and improving first-run setup accuracy.
acceptanceCriteria: Wizard detects Python projects (pyproject.toml or setup.py) and suggests 'uv run pytest' as SPIRAL_VALIDATE_CMD default
Wizard detects Node.js projects (package.json) and suggests 'npm test' as default
Wizard detects Rust projects (Cargo.toml) and suggests 'cargo test' as default
Detected tech stack is displayed as a summary before wizard prompts begin
All auto-detected defaults can be overridden interactively
technicalNotes: Detection searches SPIRAL_PROJECT_ROOT (or cwd) for indicator files
Priority order: pyproject.toml > package.json > Cargo.toml > go.mod > Makefile
Store detection results in .spiral/detected_stack.json to speed up subsequent wizard runs
Implement as lib/detect_stack.py returning a structured dict of detected values

archivedStories.title: Invalidate research cache automatically when constitution.md content changes
archivedStories.description: The `.spiral/research_cache/` caches research HTTP responses across iterations. When `constitution.md` is modified between runs, cached research may be misaligned with updated project goals. Automatically clear the research cache when a content-hash change in constitution.md is detected at startup.
acceptanceCriteria: At SPIRAL startup, SHA-256 of constitution.md is compared to the stored hash in .spiral/_constitution_hash
If hashes differ, all entries in .spiral/research_cache/ are cleared before Phase R begins
New hash is written to .spiral/_constitution_hash after clearance
Invalidation event is emitted to spiral_events.jsonl with old_hash, new_hash, and cleared_count fields
SPIRAL_INVALIDATE_CACHE_ON_CONSTITUTION_CHANGE=false disables this behavior
technicalNotes: Hash check runs in validate_preflight.sh or the spiral.sh startup section before Phase R
Only invalidates the HTTP research_cache, not the checkpoint or LLM response cache
If SPIRAL_SPECKIT_CONSTITUTION points to a custom path, hash that file instead of default constitution.md

archivedStories.title: Integration Test: End-to-End Federated SPIRAL Loop with File Conflict Simulation
archivedStories.description: Run full R→C loop with 3 parallel workers modifying overlapping files. Mock Claude API returns conflicting implementations. Verify Phase M conflict detection, Phase I isolation enforcement, no prd.json corruption, and conflict timing recorded in results.tsv.
acceptanceCriteria: tests/test_e2e_federated_conflicts.py seeds 2 sub-projects with 6 stories, 3 workers, Phase R→C with mock Claude returning 30% file overlap
Phase M detects file collisions, Phase I routes to conflict resolution, workers finish without deadlock or prd.json corruption
results.tsv includes worker_id, conflict_file_count, phase_timing columns; verify conflict resolution cost <200 tokens

_phaseI.diagnosisBlock:
## Current State

The project has infrastructure for conflict detection and worker isolation testing. The `ResultsRecord` dataclass in `lib/results_tsv.py` currently has `conflict_files` but is missing `worker_id`, `conflict_file_count`, and `phase_timing` columns required by AC3. The test file `tests/test_e2e_federated_conflicts.py` does not exist yet.

## Problem Identified

Story US-1086 requires:
1. Adding three new columns to `ResultsRecord` for conflict tracking
2. Creating an integration test that simulates a federated SPIRAL run (2 sub-projects, 6 stories, 3 workers)
3. Mocking Claude API to return implementations with intentional file overlaps (30%)
4. Verifying Phase M detects collisions and Phase I routes them correctly
5. Verifying results.tsv captures timing and conflict counts

## Planned Changes

1. **lib/results_tsv.py**: Add `worker_id`, `conflict_file_count`, and `phase_timing` fields to `ResultsRecord` and update the `HEADER` list
2. **tests/test_e2e_federated_conflicts.py**: Create integration test with:
   - Fixture creating 2 sub-projects with 3 stories each (6 total)
   - Helper to simulate worker implementations with intentional 30% file overlap
   - Verification that conflict detection identifies overlapping files
   - Verification that results.tsv captures new columns
   - Verification that workers don't deadlock (sequential simulation)
   - Verification that prd.json isn't corrupted after worker modifications

archivedStories.title: Federation: Story Reassignment CLI with Dependency Cascade
archivedStories.description: Implement CLI command to move stories between sub-projects with automatic dependency graph validation and results.tsv migration. Prevents orphaned dependencies and maintains story execution history when reorganizing federated projects.
acceptanceCriteria: CLI: spiral reassign-story <story_id> --from <sub_proj_a> --to <sub_proj_b> updates prd.json (rewrites story ID namespace), migrates results.tsv rows to new sub-project, runs validate-federated to confirm no circular deps introduced

lib/federated/reassign.py: Implement reassign_story(story_id, from_proj, to_proj, prd_dict, results_tsv) that updates dependent_story_ids in prd.json and propagates cascading updates to any stories that depend on the moved story

Integration test: Reassign middle story in 3-story dependency chain (A→B→C), verify B's namespace changes, C's dependency still points to new B ID, and results.tsv rows are migrated; assert phase order preserved post-reassignment

archivedStories.title: Results TSV Incremental Archival with Historical Query CLI
archivedStories.description: Prevent results.tsv unbounded growth by archiving old rows to timestamped files while maintaining query ability. Keeps rolling 500-row window in active results.tsv for dashboard performance.
acceptanceCriteria: CLI spiral archive-results --older-than 30 moves rows with timestamp < 30 days to .spiral/archive/results-{YYYY-MM-DD}.tsv, maintains active results.tsv with last 500 rows
CLI spiral query-archive --story-id US-123 searches both .spiral/archive/*.tsv and active results.tsv, returns all matching rows with archive filename noted
Integration test: Archive 1000 rows, verify 500 remain in active file, query-archive finds old stories, dashboard endpoints still compute trends correctly

archivedStories.title: Episodic Memory Relevance Scorer with Similarity-Based Ranking
archivedStories.description: Score episodic memory patterns by semantic similarity to current story, ensuring Ralph receives most relevant past implementation examples. Improves implementation quality via better context injection.
acceptanceCriteria: Function lib/episodic_memory.py:get_similar_patterns(story_desc, top_k=3) computes cosine similarity of story description against all stored pattern embeddings, returns top_k patterns ranked by similarity score
Ralph CLAUDE.md prompt modified to inject top 3 similar patterns with scores (e.g., '90% similar: Past pattern X fixed Y by Z')
Integration test: Store 5 episodic patterns (e.g., API auth fix, DB migration, UI bug), call get_similar_patterns with auth-related story, verify top result is auth pattern with >80% similarity

archivedStories.title: Federated Sub-Project Health Aggregator Dashboard Endpoint
archivedStories.description: Unified monitoring dashboard for multi-repo federation showing per-sub-project story metrics, cost breakdown, and iteration-to-completion trends. Enables quick health assessment of federated projects.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/dashboard/federation-health endpoint queries results.tsv grouped by sub_project column (inferred from story ID prefix), returns {sub_projects: [{name: 'api', pass_count: 5, fail_count: 1, total_cost: 123.45, avg_iterations_to_pass: 2.3}]}
Sub-project names extracted via stable prefix rule (story ID 'api-US-123' → sub_project 'api'); unmapped stories grouped under 'default'

archivedStories.title: Phase S Story Validation Confidence Scorer for Enrichment Prioritization
archivedStories.description: Score each story (0-100) for validation likelihood based on complexity signals, dependency graph depth, and description hints. Helps Phase E prioritize enrichment and Phase S make rewrite-vs-reject decisions.
acceptanceCriteria: CLI spiral score-stories-for-validation analyzes prd.json, scores each story based on: (1) keyword complexity in description (control flow, concurrency, database = higher), (2) dependency_count (each dep -5 points), (3) file_change_hints from prior Phase E (complex patterns -10 points); outputs 0-100 range
Adds _validation_confidence field to each story in prd.json in-place; simple stories (e.g., 'add button') score >80, complex stories (e.g., 'implement distributed cache with monitoring') score <50

archivedStories.title: Integration Test: Phase R Research Query Deduplication Cache Effectiveness
archivedStories.description: Add integration test validating that Phase R deduplication cache skips redundant Gemini queries, measuring actual cache hit rate and latency savings. Uses mock Gemini responses and results.tsv to verify >30% latency improvement claimed in Phase R optimization.

Benchmark test measures latency: verify cached queries execute in <100ms vs 2000ms+ for uncached

archivedStories.title: CLI: spiral debug-worker-state — Dump Live Worker State and Diagnostics

Integration test verifies output format matches schema and worker data is consistent with actual filesystem state

archivedStories.title: Phase G: Link CHANGELOG Entries to GitHub Issues and PRs via Commit Messages

archivedStories.title: Phase V: Architectural Constraint Validator - Enforce Design Rules
archivedStories.description: Add pluggable validators to Phase V that enforce project-specific architecture constraints (no circular imports, max file size, naming conventions, layer violations). Fail stories that violate rules instead of proceeding to Phase C.

_phaseI.diagnosisBlock:
## Current State
Phase V validate runs pytest via `SPIRAL_VALIDATE_CMD`. No architectural constraint checking exists. `lib/arch_validators.py` does not exist yet.

## Problem Identified
Need to add pluggable arch validators that run before pytest in Phase V and fail the story if violations are found.

## Planned Changes

_phaseI.diagnosisBlock:
## Current State
`tests/test_phase_m_ordering.py` does not exist. The `lib/prd/merge_stories.py` assigns sequential IDs to new stories then applies a topological sort (priority + dependency count based). When all stories have the same priority and no dependencies, insertion order is preserved by the `seq` tiebreaker in the heap, so numerically-ordered IDs stay numerically ordered after sequential merges.

## Problem Identified
Need a test that verifies Phase M produces deterministic, numerically-sorted story IDs when 3 workers sequentially merge disjoint story slices into the same prd.json.

## Planned Changes
- **Create `tests/test_phase_m_ordering.py`**: 10 parametrized runs (seeds 0..9), each creating 30 candidates split into 3 × 10-story slices, running 3 sequential merges, then asserting US-100..US-129 are in numerical order with no duplicates. Titles use a UID format to prevent false Jaccard deduplication.

US-1080 is complete. Here's a summary:

**US-1080: Phase M Merge Story ID Ordering Consistency Under Parallel Writes** ✅

**What was built**: `tests/test_phase_m_ordering.py` — 10 parametrized integration tests (seeds 0–9) verifying that Phase M maintains deterministic, numerically-sorted story IDs when 3 workers sequentially merge disjoint 10-story slices into the same `prd.json`.

**Key discoveries**:
- `SPIRAL_MAX_RESEARCH_STORIES=5` was set in the local environment, silently capping each worker's candidates from 10→5. The test sets it to `0` to disable the cap.
- The topological sort in `story_reorder.py` preserves insertion order when all stories share the same priority and have no dependencies (using `seq` as a heap tiebreaker) — this is what guarantees US-100..US-129 stay numerically sorted.
- `merge_stories.py` has duplicate dead-weight logic (both `apply_dead_weight_detection()` and an inline loop), causing 2 increments to `_pending_iterations` per merge call. The test sets `SPIRAL_DEAD_WEIGHT_THRESHOLD=100` to prevent premature archiving.
The 47 mypy errors are all pre-existing (in `lib/prd/merge_stories.py`, `lib/research/`, `lib/resilience/`, etc.) — none introduced by my changes. The commit is clean.

archivedStories.title: Add episodic memory store for Ralph workers to recall past implementation patterns

The episodic record injection should be placed after the static system prompt but before the story description, to avoid invalidating the cached prompt prefix.
Reference: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.13564

archivedStories.title: Show failure type column in analytics retry history table
archivedStories.description: The retry history table shows Story, Attempts, Model Path, Outcome, Total Time but not WHY a story failed. The failure_root_cause field is already parsed from results.tsv in analyticsApi.ts (TsvRow.failure_root_cause) but never surfaced in the UI. Add a Failure Type column to the retry history table populated from failure_root_cause, with colour-coded badges: amber for syntax_error/type_error/missing_dependency, blue for test_assertion, purple for context_overflow, red for oom, orange for timeout, grey for other/empty.
acceptanceCriteria: Retry history table has a Failure Type column after Model Path
Column shows the failure_root_cause value from results.tsv for each story's last failed attempt
Badges are colour-coded: amber=syntax_error/type_error/missing_dependency, blue=test_assertion, purple=context_overflow, red=oom, orange=timeout, grey=other/empty
Column is present in both Most Recent and Most Retried sort views
analyticsApi.ts exposes failure_root_cause in the retryHistory payload

archivedStories.title: Fix analytics model performance and iteration velocity to count pass not keep
archivedStories.description: The Model Performance table shows 0% rate for all models even though 304 stories passed. Root cause: analyticsApi.ts counts status === keep as success, but Phase V marks stories as status === pass. Same bug causes Iteration Velocity bars to show 0 kept for every iteration. Fix: treat both pass and keep as successes in model performance rate and iteration velocity. Rename the Kept column header to Passed.
acceptanceCriteria: Model Performance table Rate column reflects stories with status pass OR keep as successes
Haiku/sonnet/opus rows show non-zero pass rates when results.tsv has matching pass/keep rows
Iteration Velocity bars show non-zero height for iterations where stories passed
Column header renamed from Kept to Passed in the model performance table
iterationVelocity data in API counts status in (pass,keep) not just keep

archivedStories.title: Add cumulative cost and stories-passed trend chart to analytics
archivedStories.description: The analytics summary only shows a single total cost number with no over-time view. Add a dual-axis line chart below the summary bar: x-axis = iteration number, left y-axis = cumulative API cost ($), right y-axis = cumulative stories passed. Both lines on the same chart show the economic efficiency curve. Data: group results.tsv by spiral_iter, accumulate cost and passed count per iteration.
acceptanceCriteria: A line chart appears below the summary metrics row
Chart has two y-axes: left for cumulative cost ($), right for cumulative stories passed
X-axis shows iteration numbers
Both lines are non-flat when multiple iterations of data exist
Chart has a legend identifying each line
analyticsApi.ts exposes a costTrend array: [{iter, cumulativeCost, cumulativePassed}]
Chart is hidden when fewer than 2 iterations of data exist

archivedStories.title: Show per-attempt failure messages in retry history drill-down
archivedStories.description: The retry history table has an expander per row but expanded content does not show the failure message for each attempt. When expanded, show a sub-table: one row per attempt with columns: Attempt #, Model, Duration, Status, Failure Message (from results.tsv failure_root_cause). This makes it possible to trace the full retry sequence, e.g. attempt 1 syntax_error (haiku), attempt 2 test_assertion (sonnet), attempt 3 passed (opus).
acceptanceCriteria: Expanding a retry history row shows a sub-table with one row per attempt
Sub-table columns: Attempt #, Model, Duration, Status, Failure Message
Failure Message populated from results.tsv failure_root_cause for that story_id + retry_num
Sub-table rows sorted by retry_num ascending
Stories with only 1 attempt show a message indicating single attempt
analyticsApi.ts exposes per-attempt detail under storyAttempts keyed by story_id

archivedStories.title: Fix missing story titles in Most Retried section of analytics
archivedStories.description: The Most Retried section shows US-418 (5x), US-403 (4x), US-351 (3x) with no titles, only IDs. The bottlenecks.mostRetried type has a title field but it is empty. Root cause: retry count data comes from retry-counts.json which has no titles, and the title lookup from prd.json is failing. Fix analyticsApi.ts buildBottlenecks() to cross-reference prd.json and populate title for all mostRetried entries.
acceptanceCriteria: Most Retried section shows story title next to the ID for all entries
Stories not found in prd.json show only the ID without crashing
analyticsApi.ts buildBottlenecks() reads prd.json userStories and maps id to title
Titles truncated to 80 chars with ellipsis if longer

archivedStories.title: Add filter controls to analytics retry history table
archivedStories.description: The retry history table has no way to slice the data. Add a filter bar above the table with three dropdowns: (1) Failure Type - filters by failure_root_cause value; (2) Model Tier - haiku/sonnet/opus/all; (3) Outcome - passed/skipped/decomposed/all. The existing Most Recent / Most Retried sort toggle should remain. Show empty state message when no rows match filters.
acceptanceCriteria: Filter bar with three dropdowns appears above the retry history table
Failure Type dropdown lists all distinct failure_root_cause values plus All
Model Tier dropdown: All, haiku, sonnet, opus
Outcome dropdown: All, passed, skipped, decomposed
Selecting a filter immediately updates rows without page reload
Active filter count badge shown on filter bar when filters are active
Empty state message shown when no rows match current filters
Show more / Show less still works with filters applied
